title: finding (CLASS): the consumer reports success while the step stopped working — 17 confirmed instances, no standing check
description:
THE CLASS: a step stops doing its job, and the thing that reports on it keeps
saying success. No alarm fires, because the alarm is downstream of the lie.

This is now the DOMINANT defect shape in this fleet — not a coincidence.
Thirteen confirmed instances.

--- FOUND BEFORE 2026-07-26 (7, from the session handoff) ---
 1. claude-vault-sync exited 0/SUCCESS through 121 blocked runs over 5 days.
 2. harnessd asserted 12 live windows when 10 sat at a zsh prompt.
 3. andrewzigler3's nightly build "succeeded" 8 days while deploying nothing.
 4. weekly-report's AirTable calibration 422'd silently for a month.
 5. `git status --porcelain` defaults to -unormal, so a month-old backlog read as
    minutes old — blinding the alarm built to catch exactly that.
 6. A hook that redacted in place would have COMMITTED the secret and reported
    success. The fix for the class nearly introduced the class.
 7. `git push … | tail -1 && echo pushed` reported success on a 403, because a
    pipeline's exit status is the LAST command's.

--- FOUND 2026-07-26, Opus-5 audit Wave 1 (4 new) ---
 8. Fleet proxy readJsonBody returned {} on unparseable input: an Asana write
    answered 200 OK with modified_at frozen, no error anywhere (dotfiles-bm1c).
    Even after routing through the strict parser, updateTask with a literal {}
    still produced 200 over an upstream no-op until that was closed too.
 9. push-github-readme.sh exits 0 WITHOUT pushing when the README is
    content-identical. bd-xtm9's own prescribed one-line fix
    (`cmd && PUSHED=true`) would have reproduced the defect one layer down.
    THE PRESCRIBED FIX WAS ITSELF AN INSTANCE.
10. A failed README push still advances the camp hash, so the README stays stale
    until camp changes again and nothing retries (bd-troe).
11. Hevy `stale: true` is never written to disk, so both consumers read the file,
    see no flag, and render + LEDGER a stale snapshot as current (bd-ie0t).

--- ADJACENT, same shape, same day ---
12. The granola auth fix was applied at the NGINX EDGE, not in the service. Every
    external probe said "authenticated" while pico's router answered anonymously
    to the whole tailnet (dotfiles-13qu). THE VERIFICATION was what lied.
13. daily-digest wrote "row":null on every ledger line — 30 ticks that ran and
    were uncountable, so the dashboard read "no problem" not "no data"
    (dotfiles-ldag). Two further ledgers had it, tracked by no bead.

--- WHY IT KEEPS HAPPENING (four generators) ---
a. EXIT CODE != EFFECT — wrappers exit 0 on a no-op path (9); pipelines return
   the last stage's status (7); a blocked run still returns 0 (1).
b. THE FLAG IS WRITTEN WHERE NOTHING READS — staleness in a build log (11), row
   identity dropped before the dashboard (13).
c. THE GATE ADVANCES ON INTENT, NOT OUTCOME — camp hash moves on CAMP_CHANGED
   rather than on the push landing (10).
d. THE PROBE TESTS A DIFFERENT PATH THAN THE ONE THAT MATTERS — edge vs service
   (12); status-only assertions that pass even when the write happened (8).

--- WHAT EXISTS, AND THE GAP ---
The /pulse ledger already refuses zero-distance proofs: `artifact` and `commit`
are REJECTED fleet-wide; only `cmd` (the hook RE-RUNS it) or `scrutinize` count
(explore-len0), enforced by pre-commit-checks.sh. That is the right principle,
implemented for exactly ONE surface.

Nothing applies it to daemon nightly builds, webhook receivers, deploy scripts,
proxy write routes, or any wrapper that exits 0. Instances 8-11 live in that gap.

--- THE ASK: a standing check, not more prose ---
Prose guidance demonstrably does not take (explore-369f carried standing
guidance and 44 of 128 findings ignored it). So:

1. REPORTING CONTRACT — any script whose success is consumed by another script
   prints an explicit verdict marker on EVERY terminal path, and the consumer
   treats "exit 0 with no marker" as FAILURE (fail-closed). Already implemented
   once: bd-xtm9's README_PUSH_RESULT. Lift it into a documented convention.
2. POST-WRITE VERIFICATION at every write boundary — re-read and compare instead
   of trusting the response. Correct already in lib/gdoc/handlers.ts:282,:319;
   missing on the Asana routes (dotfiles-580v).
3. NEGATIVE CONTROL as the standard of proof for a fix — stash the fix, re-run,
   the test MUST fail. Both Wave-1 agents that did this caught real gaps. "The
   suite is green" proves nothing about a test that would pass anyway.

--- THE META-POINT ---
Instances 6 and 9 are the ones to remember: in both, the PRESCRIBED FIX for the
class was itself an instance of it. That is why (3) matters most — the only
reliable defense is a check whose own failure mode is visible, applied to the fix.

Relates: dotfiles-b9ii (audit epic), dotfiles-mlti ("the documented example IS
the defect", the sibling class), explore-len0 (proof tokens), dotfiles-580v,
bd-troe, bd-ie0t, dotfiles-13qu, dotfiles-ldag.
notes:
## Instance count: 17 (was 14). Three more found the same day, all by loops auditing themselves.

15. recall-distill's gather_candidates() sorted by session-UUID STRING then
    truncated at 200, so all 200 candidates came from ONE session and ZERO from
    inside the target window — **66 of 67 sessions silently dropped**, and the tick
    logged a normal-looking row. Found by the tick itself, which then re-ran with a
    raised cap (5761 candidates / 57 sessions) and judged THAT set rather than
    logging a non-result. Filed explore-j2p9. Generator: the probe covered a
    different population than the claim.

16. **groundskeep-scan.sh ended in an UNCONDITIONAL `exit 10`** against the
    systemd unit's `SuccessExitStatus=0 10`. So a greenkeep that CRASHED made
    the unit go GREEN. Worse, `if $GREENKEEP scan; then` treated a scan error
    (exit 1) identically to drift (exit 10) and pressed on into a doomed run.
    Fixed in vs14d-l0t. Generator (a) in its purest form: EXIT CODE != EFFECT,
    with the systemd success-status list actively laundering the crash.

17. **gdoc.sh returns exit 0 on failure** — a bogus doc id dumps TypeScript source
    lines and exits 0; `read` on a tabbed doc returns EMPTY and exits 0. A caller
    cannot distinguish 'doc is empty' from 'doc does not exist' from 'credentials
    failed'. The weekly-report skill PUBLISHES through this shim on a live Tuesday
    timer. Filed dotfiles-79r8. Found only because a negative control was run on
    the probe rather than trusting a clean-looking result.

## What the newest three add to the analysis

All three were found by pointing a check at a loop's OWN reporting rather than at
its output — which is the practical form the standing check should take. Instance
16 is the strongest argument yet for the reporting contract: no amount of care
inside greenkeep.py could have surfaced a crash that the *unit's* success-status
list was configured to swallow. The verdict marker has to cross the process
boundary.

Instance 15 also generalises the coverage rule: it is not enough to report
'processed N'. It must be **N of M**, because N alone looked healthy.

## Measurement-side twin: dotfiles-effn (2026-08-07)
This bead is about a CONSUMER reporting success while the step stopped working.
`dotfiles-effn` is the same silence one layer down: six TOOL IDIOMS on this fleet that
return a confident wrong VALUE instead of an error — `find` without `-L` on the project
slug symlinks, `deferred` in the vault ledger, `rm -iv`, self-matching `pkill -f`,
leading-dash arguments, and uutils `ps`. Same failure shape: a plausible answer, not a
crash, indistinguishable from a true negative unless already suspected.

title: hooks: add post-gen-fanout-check.sh — gamma/openrouter fan-out reminder

title: task: propose-only /triage pulse row — closure must stop depending on Zig noticing
description:
Fix #4 from the beads-lifecycle audit (refs/research/beads-lifecycle-audit.md).
Fixes 1-3 are mechanical hook changes and are being implemented; this one is a
loop and deserves its own decision.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT MOTIVATES IT: closure is purely EPISODIC — 2-3 closes/day
when nobody is watching, versus 50-63 on a sweep day. That is Zig's literal
complaint, quantified. A lifecycle that only advances when an orchestrator happens
to be paying attention is the same shape as this fleet's dominant defect class: it
works until nobody looks, and nothing reports that it stopped.

PROPOSAL: a scheduled, PROPOSE-ONLY /triage row. It never closes anything —
consistent with the propose-never-close rule that /desk already follows for the
same reason (a wrong close is silent AND permanent, and the idea simply
disappears). It surfaces candidates and files them where Zig can act in one pass.

A READY FIRST BATCH EXISTS: the audit found 32 open beads whose OWN BODY says
superseded / obsolete / moot. Those are self-declared dead and need no judgement
to surface.

title: the lexicon-glyph window matcher in pulse-dispatch-remote has no test coverage — the ssh stub answers for the whole lookup
description:
Reported by the dotfiles-77s4 agent as adjacent; filed rather than fixed.

## Context
pulse-dispatch-remote.sh resolves a row window with a remote pipeline:

    tmux list-windows ... | awk ... sub(/^[^a-zA-Z0-9_]+/, "", name) ...

The awk strips lexicon glyph prefixes (✅ 🧠 🔔) so `work:✅ imc-aug26` still matches the
row `imc-aug26`. That matcher is the fix for a real leak — without it a run does not
recognise its own glyph-prefixed window and creates a SECOND one; it previously put two
`weekly-report` windows on the box.

The suite cannot exercise it. The ssh stub answers for the ENTIRE remote lookup
(`list-windows | awk`) as one canned response, so the awk never actually runs. The
matcher therefore has zero coverage today, and a regression in it would be invisible —
while its symptom (duplicate windows on a shared box) is exactly the class of problem
dotfiles-77s4 was filed for.

## Why it is not a quick fix
Covering it means teaching the stub to EXECUTE the awk against a fake `tmux` that emits
realistic `#{window_id} #{window_name}` lines, rather than returning a precomputed id.
That is a stub redesign, not an added case — which is why it was correctly left out of
77s4 rather than bolted on.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] the stub runs the real awk against synthetic list-windows output
- [ ] glyph-prefixed windows (✅ 🧠 🔔 and a bare name) all resolve to the right row
- [ ] a row whose name is a PREFIX of another does not cross-match
- [ ] a mutant removing the sub() is OBSERVED to fail, mutation asserted applied first
close_reason: The ssh stub now EXECUTES the dispatcher's own awk instead of answering for it. Option (a), sharpened past the drift risk: rsh() sends exactly one word (bash -lc <%q-quoted cmd>), so the stub strips the prefix and re-runs it as bash -c with a synthetic tmux prepended to PATH — non-login on purpose, since -l would reset PATH to the real tmux. Option (b) was rejected for a better reason than the brief gave: the fragile part of that line is its ssh double-quoting round-trip, and calling an extracted function locally would cover the awk while leaving the quoting untested; this covers both. DRIFT IS STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE, verified by the orchestrator: 0 copies of the awk in the test, 1 in production. Two secondary guards — the fake tmux refuses any -F other than the production format, and the retired WIN_LIST knob exits 3 loudly rather than degrading to a silent no-op. 13 cases: bare name, four glyph prefixes, right row picked from a glyph-laden list, di-mon vs di-monday both directions plus a glyph-prefixed near-miss, glyphs-only matching nothing, unrelated window, empty list. Suite 267 -> 280, production file untouched. Orchestrator independently mutated PRODUCTION (dropped the sub(), test untouched, bash -n clean, mutation asserted applied): 275/5, every glyph case failing with resolved '@99' — the no-match sentinel — instead of the real id, including the 🌀 case, which proves the strip is generic rather than a hardcoded glyph list.

title: harnessd state-bus.timer + .service are MASKED — the fleet dashboard has served frozen state since 2026-07-29
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
  systemctl --user list-unit-files 'state-bus*'
    state-bus.service   masked  enabled
    state-bus.timer     masked  enabled
  systemctl --user is-enabled state-bus.timer -> masked

Masked, not merely disabled -- someone actively blocked it, and nothing records why.

Downstream (found by the pico audit, dotfiles-5da3): pico's `com.zig.harness` job
serves `state.json` on :10000 with `--auth none`. That file is pushed by
zig-computer's `harness-refresh`, which state-bus.timer drives. With the timer masked,
the dashboard has shown data frozen at **2026-07-29** ever since.

`KeepAlive=true` keeps the pico job green the whole time. **A healthy process serving
stale data is indistinguishable from a working pipeline** -- the dotfiles-cxle class
again, and the third instance found on 2026-08-01 (after pulse-ledger-lint having no
hook caller, and agentgateway-run existing with nothing calling it).

agents/infra.md described this pipeline as "Live now via state-bus.timer" until
corrected today.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Establish WHY it was masked -- masking is deliberate, so there may be a good
      reason (a runaway loop, a cost issue). Check journal + git log around 2026-07-29
      before unmasking anything.
- [ ] Either unmask + verify fresh state lands on pico's :10000, or record the
      decision to leave it off and make the dashboard SAY it is stale
- [ ] The dashboard should fail loud rather than serve a frozen file: a freshness
      stamp with a max-age, so "frozen" renders differently from "healthy"
- [ ] Note the pico side is `--auth none` on a LAN-reachable port (dotfiles-28jw
      records that pico runs without a firewall by Zig's decision)
close_reason: FILED IN ERROR — retracted 2026-08-01 after verifying. The mask is DELIBERATE and documented: harnessd/CLAUDE.md:51 says 'generates in-proc in Go (HARNESSD_GEN_MODE=go); state-bus.timer is masked, so the Python no longer generates.' Masking WAS the migration off the Python generator. Verified live: harnessd.service active, HARNESSD_GEN_MODE=go, http://100.98.174.21:14174/state.json -> HTTP 200 with generated_at 2026-08-01T22:06:51Z (minutes old). The pipeline is healthy. Also verified the mask symlink is dated Jul 7, three weeks BEFORE the 07-29 freeze this bead blamed on it -- which should have been the tell. The narrow real finding (pico's :10000 job serves a frozen copy) is a RETIRED PROTOTYPE, not a break: harnessd/CLAUDE.md:104 says the same-origin Go daemon 'evaporates the rsync-push-to-pico seam the prototype used.' Nothing pushes to pico by design. Refiled as the accurate, much smaller finding.

title: githooks: staging session-start.sh maps to a nonexistent test file, so its suite never gates a commit
description:
## Context

`tools/githooks/pre-commit` runs "the suite matching each staged `agents/{hooks,scheduler,lib,doclint}` script". For `agents/hooks/session-start.sh` it derives
`agents/hooks/test/test-session-start.sh` — **which does not exist**. The real suite is
`agents/hooks/test/test-session-start-merge-driver.sh`.

So editing `session-start.sh` gates on nothing. Found 2026-08-01 while fixing
`dotfiles-1rj5` in that exact file: the suite had to be run by hand, and the commit went
through without it.

This is the gate CLAUDE.md rule #1 describes as the *mechanism* that replaced intention —
so a name-derivation miss here silently returns the repo to intention-only for that script.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `git config core.hooksPath tools/githooks`
2. Stage any edit to `agents/hooks/session-start.sh`
3. Commit — observe the merge-driver suite does not run.
4. `ls agents/hooks/test/test-session-start.sh` -> no such file.

## Fix direction

Name-derivation by convention is the underlying fragility: a suite whose filename does not
match its subject is invisible to it, and nothing reports the miss. Two parts:

1. Map `session-start.sh` to its real suite.
2. **Make an unmatched script loud rather than silent.** Right now "no suite found" and
   "suite passed" are indistinguishable. At minimum warn; better, maintain an explicit
   script->suite map and fail on an entry that names a missing file.

Audit the other `agents/{hooks,scheduler,lib,doclint}` scripts for the same mismatch while
in here — this is likely not the only one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] staging `session-start.sh` runs `test-session-start-merge-driver.sh`, demonstrated
- [ ] a staged script with NO matching suite produces a visible warning, not silence
- [ ] every script in the four gated dirs audited for name mismatch; misses fixed or mapped
close_reason: Fixed in 3fe8494 — seven mismatches found, not one. Staging session-start.sh now runs 4 suites / 65 cases (was 0). Unmatched script prints a stderr banner + trailing warning; a map entry naming a missing file now blocks.

title: decision: the mutation-discipline clauses land in dotfiles/CLAUDE.md rule 1, not /scrutinize
description:
## Context
dotfiles-3afr proposed two clauses — assert the mutation applied, and require a killed
mutant to fail the case it NAMES — and deliberately left the tier as an open question
for Zig: dotfiles/CLAUDE.md rule 1, or /scrutinize. Asked to "fix those remaining beads",
Zig delegated the choice back rather than answering it, so this is a decide-and-proceed.

## Decision
dotfiles/CLAUDE.md **rule 1**.

## Why
- Rule 1 already carries the sentence being refined: "A green suite is not evidence that
  a guard bites; only a mutant that dies is." The clauses are a refinement of that exact
  claim, not a new one. Splitting a claim from its refinement across two documents is how
  dotfiles-x1fn happened this same session.
- Rule 1 is scoped to THIS repo's hook/guard testing, which is precisely where the
  mutation harness lives (agents/scheduler/mutate-tunnel-ownership.sh,
  agents/hooks/test/mutate-scrutiny-guards.sh). /scrutinize is fleet-wide and owns the
  POST-IMPL AUDIT — stub bodies, composition gaps — a different gate at a different time.
- Cost of the alternative: /scrutinize is a global skill, so the clauses would load into
  every session in every project, to govern a discipline that only applies where a
  mutation harness exists.

## Reversibility
Cheap — it is prose in one file, and the rule points at the reference implementation
rather than restating it, so moving it later moves a pointer.

## What would change my mind
If a second repo grows a mutation harness, the guidance stops being dotfiles-specific and
/scrutinize (or a shared skills/_shared/ doc) becomes the right host.

title: task: the always-loaded staleness warning reaches Zig but not the running MODEL
description:
Known limit of the explore-6wwu fix (dotfiles de54842), flagged by its implementer.

The Stop hook surfaces a stale always-loaded file via systemMessage + stderr +
/tmp/claude-always-loaded/stale.log. That reaches ZIG.

It does NOT reach the running agent. Claude Code only feeds Stop-hook text back
to the model on exit 2 — which BLOCKS — and blocking was explicitly rejected in
decision explore-0z6r (it turns a typo in CLAUDE.md into an interrupted tick).

So a durable pulse window still acts on the stale snapshot; the human is now told,
the agent is not. That is a real improvement (the divergence is no longer silent)
but it is half the loop: the failure explore-6wwu documented was an UNATTENDED
tick escalating to xhigh and losing WebSearch, and an unattended tick has no human
reading systemMessage.

FIX DIRECTION (the implementer's own suggestion, and it is right): a
UserPromptSubmit hook emitting additionalContext. That path DOES reach the model,
does not block, and fires at exactly the moment the agent is about to act.
agents/hooks/lib/always-loaded.sh is already written to be reusable for it.

Relates: explore-6wwu (closed), explore-0z6r (the decision), dotfiles-cxle
(the flag-written-where-nothing-reads generator — this is a partial instance:
written where the HUMAN reads, not where the actor does).

title: hevyd listens on *:14877 (wildcard) while its own docs say 127.0.0.1:14389 — both port and bind drifted
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. `ss -ltnp | grep 14877` -> `LISTEN *:14877 users:(("hevyd",pid=995129))`
   A WILDCARD bind (all interfaces), not loopback and not tailnet-scoped.
2. `grep -n '14389' ~/hevyd/CLAUDE.md` -> L164 "systemd user service (hevyd.service)
   on `127.0.0.1:14389`". L109 documents 14389 as the chosen port.
3. `sudo iptables -S | grep -E '14877|14389'` -> no rule for either.
   INPUT policy is DROP, so it is NOT reachable from the internet.

## Assessment -- not an emergency, but two drifts in one
- **Port drift**: docs say 14389, live is 14877. Nothing in ~/hevyd explains the change.
- **Bind drift**: docs say 127.0.0.1, live is `*` -- so it IS reachable tailnet-wide.

hevyd/CLAUDE.md L459-461 records that this EXACT thing already happened once: it bound
`*:14389` since go-live while every doc said 127.0.0.1, and the resolution was that no
ufw rule exists and an off-box probe got REFUSED. So the internet exposure is genuinely
closed both times -- but the wildcard bind has now recurred on a NEW port, which means
the earlier fix did not stick (or was reverted) and nothing detects it.

⚠️ METHOD NOTE for whoever picks this up: `curl 51.81.33.136:14877` FROM zig-computer
returns 404. That is a loopback artifact -- the packet never traverses the firewall.
Do not read it as proof of public reachability. Probe from off-box (pico via tailnet
is also not the public internet; use a genuinely external vantage point).

Found during the dotfiles-w8xw infra.md refresh, 2026-08-01.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Establish which port is intended and make docs + service agree
- [ ] Bind to 127.0.0.1 or the tailnet IP explicitly, not `*` -- matching the
      documented norm and the earlier fix
- [ ] A check that DETECTS a wildcard bind regression, since this is the second
      occurrence; a doc statement alone demonstrably did not hold
- [ ] Cross-check against dotfiles-6wdw (the open P0 on unauthenticated
      internet->tailnet pivot) -- same hazard class, different port

title: o11y hole: claude sessions launched before their host gained a per-host zshenv route DIRECT and log NOTHING
description:
## Context
Reproducible instance captured live 2026-08-04 on marketing-vps before it could exit.
The earlier sighting (dotfiles-jfqq) vanished before it could be traced and was closed
as non-reproducing — THIS is that reproduction, with a better-supported cause.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. On marketing-vps, find a claude process in a pane launched before 2026-08-03:
   `pgrep -af 'claude --dangerously-skip-permissions'`
2. Read its environment: `tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/<pid>/environ | grep -E 'ANTHROPIC|CC_NO_GATEWAY'`
3. Observed on pid 1623429, pane work:4.0 (window "✅ di-tuesday"),
   cwd /home/andrew/linearb/dashboard-dev-interrupted:
     ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL       -> ABSENT  (so: direct to api.anthropic.com)
     CC_NO_GATEWAY            -> ABSENT  (so: NOT the escape hatch)
     ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS -> "X-Session-Identity: work:di-tuesday" and NO X-Machine-Origin
4. Confirm the absence in the log on pico: no request_logs rows attributed to that session.

## Cause
X-Machine-Origin was added to claude-identity-wrapper.sh in dotfiles-v93v, and
marketing-vps only gained zsh/.marketing-vps.zshenv — the file that exports
ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL here — on 2026-08-03. A pane whose claude was launched BEFORE that has
neither: the wrapper it launched under could not supply the base URL and did not yet send
the machine header. Both absences have ONE cause, an old launch. Same shell-age blindness
class as dotfiles-t6to, surviving in already-running processes rather than in config.

## Impact
The session works perfectly and is invisible to pico's request_logs. Per agents/infra.md a
client with no machine header logs group='unknown', indistinguishable from one that never
sent it — and a bypassing session is indistinguishable from an idle one. Confirmed in the
data: 5 rows today carried group='unknown', all agentgateway_user='zig-computer:zsh'.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Enumerate every running claude on zig-computer and marketing-vps whose environ
      lacks BOTH ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and CC_NO_GATEWAY, and report the pane for each
- [ ] Zig decides which panes to restart (a restart destroys session context, so it is
      his call — per-pane recipe is in dotfiles-9o46)
- [ ] After restart, confirm the session appears in pico's request_logs with a non-empty
      agentgateway_group, queried with datetime(started_at) not a bare string compare
- [ ] Standing detection documented: any request_logs row with empty/'unknown'
      agentgateway_group is a client that needs restarting

title: weekly-report: the skill's Asana gids and Google Doc id are unverified
description:
Flagged honestly by the dotfiles-gify fix agent, 2026-07-26, as explicitly NOT verified.

The weekly-report skill hardcodes Asana gids (WS, ME, section 1208440192743649, the LinkedIn custom field 1208440192743659) and a Google Doc id. The agent did not verify them because no /tmp/.atok existed, and minting one triggers an OAuth refresh that REWRITES a token store — a write side-effect it had been told not to take. That is the correct call, and it leaves a real gap: the AirTable half of this skill had TWO independent schema drifts (a renamed column AND two field names missing apostrophes, which AirTable silently omits rather than erroring). There is no reason to assume the Asana half is cleaner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- every hardcoded gid and doc id in the skill is resolved against the live API and confirmed to point at what its name claims
- anything stale is corrected
- a note on how these get re-verified periodically, since this class of drift is silent by construction

Resolved every hardcoded id against the LIVE API via the fleet proxy, read-only —
no OAuth token store rewritten, which is what stopped the previous agent.

VERIFIED CORRECT:

  METHOD NOTE: querying it via /sections/<gid>/tasks returns 'Asana resource not

NOT VERIFIABLE THROUGH THE PROXY (honest gap, not a pass):
- WS=1178181021060349 and ME=1208749853950521. The proxy exposes only
  attachments/projects/search/sections/tasks — no workspaces or users route.
  Used only as query scoping, so a wrong value surfaces as EMPTY results rather

RE-VERIFICATION (the third acceptance criterion): this drift is silent by

title: two skill frontmatters fail a STRICT yaml parse — a stricter reader silently loses the whole routing entry
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
python3 -c "import yaml,re; ..." over agents/skills/*/SKILL.md frontmatter:

  desk      ScannerError: mapping values are not allowed here
  dispatch  ScannerError: mapping values are not allowed here

Cause: an unquoted `: ` (colon-space) inside an unquoted YAML scalar. In `desk` it is
`...resourcing memo to Andrew: what to fund...`; in `dispatch` it is
`` `subagent_type: "subagent"` ``. YAML reads the second colon as a new mapping key.

Also found: `beads` and `daemon` have **no `when_to_use` field at all**.

## Why it matters
Claude Code's frontmatter parser is LENIENT, so this has never bitten -- both skills
route fine today. But `description` + `when_to_use` ARE the routing table: they are
what the model sees when deciding whether to load a skill. Any stricter reader (a lint,
a future parser, an external tool, a doc generator) silently drops the field rather
than erroring -- so the failure mode is a skill that quietly stops being routable, with
no error anywhere. Same silent-success class as dotfiles-cxle.

Found by the dotfiles-wstl frontmatter-compression agent, which hit it because it ran a
strict YAML check BEFORE trusting its own A/B -- and discovered its first two edits had
INTRODUCED two new instances. Three pre-existing instances (cdn, dive, scrub-secrets)
were fixed as part of that compression; these two were out of its scope.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `desk` and `dispatch` frontmatter quoted so a strict `yaml.safe_load` succeeds
- [ ] Decide whether `beads` and `daemon` need `when_to_use` (they may be fine relying
      on `description` -- confirm the routing behavior rather than adding text by reflex)
- [ ] A strict-parse check wired into post-write-skill.sh or the pre-commit doclint, so
      the next unquoted colon is caught at write time rather than by an audit
- [ ] The check must FAIL on a planted bad frontmatter before it is trusted (repo rule 1)

title: finding: the Opus-5 guide's remove-list is NARROWER than '80%' but hits /scrutinize HARDER than AGENTS.md's 2026-07-27 reading admits
description:
## Context

Fetched the live vendor guide 2026-08-01 (platform.claude.com .../prompting-claude-opus-5)
during the dotfiles-w8xw audit. Two corrections to standing harness beliefs.

### 1. There is no "80%" in the guide. The remove-list is SPECIFIC, not blanket.

Zig's framing ("Anthropic removed 80% of Opus 5's harness instructions") is
directionally right about the CLASS but wrong about the scale of what the vendor
actually prescribes. The guide opens with: "It performs well out of the box on
existing Claude Opus 4.8 prompts." It then names ~6 targeted removals:
  - explicit verification instructions
  - self-correction / re-check instructions ("double-check", "re-verify")
  - subagent-verification instructions
  - prompt-side VISION workarounds tuned for prior models
  - any rule instructing the model NOT to think/reason (increases tag leakage)
  - carried-over EFFORT defaults (re-run a sweep instead)
and adds ~4 things to ADD (conciseness, written-deliverable length calibration,
scope constraint, delegation caps).

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE AUDIT: "cut 80%" is not the vendor's recommendation and should
not be the report's frame. The real cut in THIS harness comes from local staleness,
cross-skill duplication and hook-duplicating prose -- which the vendor guide says
nothing about and which is likely the LARGER win.

### 2. The verification sentence is stronger than AGENTS.md records.

AGENTS.md's "Verification: no self-checking, but always evidence at the checkpoint"
section (Zig's call, 2026-07-27, bead explore-8hs7) keeps /scrutinize on the reading
that the guide "never measures" separate fresh-context adversarial review. Verbatim
from the live guide:

  "If your prompt contains explicit verification instructions ('include a final
   verification step for any non-trivial task,' 'USE A SUBAGENT TO VERIFY'), remove
   them: instructions like these cause over-verification on Claude Opus 5, and
   removing them reduces wasted tokens with no loss in quality. THE SAME APPLIES TO
   LEGACY HARNESS SCAFFOLDING THAT ADDS SEPARATE VERIFICATION STEPS."

and in the delegation section:

  "do not use subagents to verify or double-check your own work."

So "use a subagent to verify" and "legacy harness scaffolding that adds separate
verification steps" ARE named. The 2026-07-27 claim that the guide "never measures
the second" is not supportable as written.

NOT proposing /scrutinize be deleted. The conflicted-judge argument in AGENTS.md is
an INCENTIVE argument the vendor never addresses, and the harness has hook-enforced
scrutiny verdicts that a prose change won't move. But the tension is real, it is
Zig's call, and it should be settled by EVIDENCE (how often has /scrutinize actually
changed an outcome?) rather than by re-reading the guide. That evidence sweep is
the sibling bead.

### 3. The harness's dominant instructional idiom may be the weaker one.

  "Positive examples of the communication style you want tend to be more effective
   than instructions about what not to do."

Stated in the narration context, but the harness is overwhelmingly anti-pattern-
driven: every SKILL.md carries a large "Anti-patterns / never do X" block, and
TOOLKIT.md is literally keyed on "the single most load-bearing anti-pattern". If the
generalization holds, a large fraction of the harness's words are in the less
effective form. Worth an A/B before acting -- flagged, not concluded.

### 4. Opus 5 is itself a cause of the bloat being audited.

  "files that Claude Opus 5 writes to disk (reports, Markdown documents, summaries)
   are often longer than on prior models" -> add explicit length calibration.

/desk at 9,772 words, and TOOLKIT.md's note that the old elevate memo grew
1,460->2,190 words, are this documented behavior. A one-line length-calibration
instruction in the always-loaded tier is a cheap structural fix that stops
re-accumulation -- otherwise any cut we make grows back.

title: vps: make the standing fleet forward DURABLE on the box (it is currently a leftover process)
description:
## Context

Zig decided the box keeps a STANDING forward to zig-computer's fleet proxy
(decision dotfiles-5q7c). But the forward that exists today is not standing by
design — it is pid 1220000, a leftover from a 2026-07-28 self-heal verification
run. Nothing re-establishes it after a reboot, an ssh drop, or a network blip.

That makes the property aspirational: the fleet believes the box always has
proxy access, and the first thing to notice otherwise will be a tick. With the
dotfiles-wv2a fix in place a dropped forward is no longer fatal (the dispatcher
falls back to opening `-R` itself), so this is about honoring the decision and
about the INTERACTIVE /vps path, which has no such fallback.

`ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh ensure` is already idempotent and no-ops on a healthy
port, so it is safe to run on a schedule.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A systemd --user unit on marketing-vps (under the `andrew` account) runs
      `~/dotfiles/agents/scheduler/ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh ensure` on a timer.
      Interval: minutes, not hours — it must heal well inside a tick's window.
- [ ] `WantedBy` / `Persistent` shaped so it also fires after a reboot, and
      lingering is enabled for the account (`loginctl enable-linger andrew`) so
      user units survive logout. VERIFY linger is actually on; do not assume.
- [ ] The unit does NOT mask a real fault: a `2` (upstream answers non-200 =
      BLOCKED) must not be retried into a false heal. ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh
      already implements the three-valued contract; the unit must not paper
      over its exit code.
- [ ] The unit file is committed to ~/dotfiles (templates dir alongside the
      other scheduler units) even though it is installed on the box, so a
      rebuild is not archaeology. Note in the bead where it is installed.
- [ ] EVIDENCE: kill the forward on the box, show the timer restoring it inside
      one interval, with `curl 127.0.0.1:7100/api/health` -> 200 before and
      after. Paste the commands and output.

## Notes

Shared box — ben, kevin, mike, ubuntu also have accounts. Never `pkill` on port
7100; ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh's teardown is pidfile-scoped for that reason.

title: spec: phase 1 local coding-agent stack on pico (Qwen3-Coder + claude-code-router + Ollama)
description:
## 1. Overview

Phase 1 deployment of a Claude-Code-style coding agent backed by a local model on pico (Mac Studio M1 Max, 64 GB). Selects Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct as the model, Ollama as the server (current, with 3 env tweaks), claude-code-router as the protocol-translation proxy, and keeps the user on Claude Code as the daily-driver harness. Pi Coding Agent is installed alongside as the kernel for future custom-harness experiments.

What this spec does NOT cover (deferred to a Phase 2 spec):
- LM Studio / MLX A/B test for the 2× decode win
- Aider as the diff-format coding-quality fallback
- GLM-4.5-Air for "quality > speed" runs
- Phoenix observability hookup
- Bespoke per-use-case harnesses (chat / batch / etc.)

## 2. Current State / Baseline

Pico runs Ollama 0.24.0 via a custom LaunchAgent (`com.zig.ollama`). Current env (verified live 2026-05-25):

```
OLLAMA_HOST=100.72.47.4:11434     # tailnet bind, NOT loopback
OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1
OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0
OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=24h
```

Service is healthy: cold model load ~15s, warm calls ~45-200ms TTFT, ~62 tok/s on the existing qwen2.5:7b. Pre-pulled models: `qwen2.5:7b` (4.6 GB base, NOT coding-tuned), `llama3.2:3b` (2.0 GB, too small for coding).

Plist source-of-truth: `~/dotfiles/ollama/com.zig.ollama.plist` with `TAILSCALE_IP_PLACEHOLDER` substituted at install time by `mac.setup.sh` lines 65-74.

Claude Code currently uses Anthropic-hosted Sonnet 4.6 — no local-backend wiring exists yet.

## 3. Changes and Decisions

| # | Change | Decision | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3.1 | Add `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=131072` | Single biggest fix. Default 4K silently truncates and breaks tool loops. 128K matches harnesses-agent recommendation and gives serious coding-session capacity | both serving + harnesses agents flagged independently |
| 3.2 | Add `OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=2` | 64 GB has headroom for 2 concurrent slots | serving agent |
| 3.3 | Add `OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=2` | Allows primary + fallback (or embedding) resident simultaneously | serving agent |
| 3.4 | Pull `qwen3-coder:30b` | MoE 30B-A3B (3.3B active) — right architecture for M1 Max's bandwidth profile. 51.6% SWE-bench Verified, tool-calling fixed Aug 2025, ~40-55 tok/s on Ollama | models agent ranking |
| 3.5 | Install `claude-code-router` on pico | Translates Anthropic protocol → Ollama OpenAI-compat. CCR-on-pico keeps the chatty proxy↔model traffic on loopback; one tailnet hop for CC→CCR | harnesses agent |
| 3.6 | New LaunchAgent `com.zig.ccr` | Match existing zig-zone service discipline (own LaunchAgent so env vars don't get clobbered) | mac.setup.sh convention |
| 3.7 | Install Pi alongside (no LaunchAgent) | Pi is interactive CLI; install for experimentation + as fork kernel for bespoke harnesses | user directive + harnesses agent |
| 3.8 | CC client config: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://100.72.47.4:<ccr-port>` | Single env var on the CC client side; reversible (unset to go back to hosted) | claude-code-router docs |

## 4. Formal Specification

### 4.1 Ollama env (plist update)

Target file: `~/dotfiles/ollama/com.zig.ollama.plist` (then re-deploy to pico).

Add to the existing `<dict>` under `EnvironmentVariables`:

```xml
<key>OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH</key><string>131072</string>
<key>OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL</key><string>2</string>
<key>OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS</key><string>2</string>
```

Re-deploy: copy plist to pico, `launchctl unload` + `launchctl load -w`. Verify env via `launchctl list com.zig.ollama` and a smoke test.

### 4.2 Model pull

On pico (or via tailnet API):
```
ollama pull qwen3-coder:30b
```

Expected: ~19 GB download. Disk check before: `df -h /opt/homebrew` (Ollama default model store) should show ≥30 GB free.

### 4.3 claude-code-router install

On pico:
```
brew install node       # if not present (pico's Phoenix path requires Python; check Node first)
npm install -g @musistudio/claude-code-router
mkdir -p ~/.config/claude-code-router
cp ~/dotfiles/ccr/config.json ~/.config/claude-code-router/config.json    # new dotfiles file
```

Config (`~/dotfiles/ccr/config.json` — new file in dotfiles):
- One provider entry pointing at `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1` (Ollama OpenAI-compat endpoint)
- Routes: `default` → `qwen3-coder:30b`, `background` → `qwen3-coder:30b` (only one model in Phase 1)
- Bind: `0.0.0.0:3456` (will be tailnet-only via firewall, OR `100.72.47.4:3456` if CCR supports explicit bind)

### 4.4 New LaunchAgent: com.zig.ccr

New file: `~/dotfiles/ccr/com.zig.ccr.plist`. Same pattern as `com.zig.ollama.plist`:
- `Label`: `com.zig.ccr`
- `ProgramArguments`: `["/opt/homebrew/bin/ccr", "start"]` (or wherever the npm global binary lands)
- `EnvironmentVariables`: `HOST=100.72.47.4`, `PORT=3456` (or per CCR's env contract)
- `RunAtLoad: true`, `KeepAlive: true`
- `StandardOutPath` / `StandardErrorPath`: `/opt/homebrew/var/log/ccr.log`

### 4.5 mac.setup.sh additions

After the Ollama LaunchAgent block (~line 74 in current `mac.setup.sh`):

```bash

npm install -g @musistudio/claude-code-router
mkdir -p ~/.config/claude-code-router
sed "s/TAILSCALE_IP_PLACEHOLDER/$(tailscale ip -4)/" \
    ~/dotfiles/ccr/config.json \

# --- Pi Coding Agent (alongside CC, for experimentation + custom-harness reference) ---
# Pi is interactive CLI; no LaunchAgent. Install once; user invokes manually.
brew install pi-agent || npm install -g @pi-dev/pi   # verify which is canonical before shipping
```

### 4.6 CC client config

On whichever host runs CC (zig, metis, or both):

Persist via shell init OR a CC project-local override. Reversible: unset to fall back to hosted Sonnet.

## 5. Test Cases (≥10)


## 6. Open Questions

- OQ-01 (P1): **Where does the CC client run** — only on zig, only on metis, or both? Affects whether ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is set in dotfiles shell init (which propagates to both) or per-host. *Recommendation: set per-host via shell init; CC project-local override available for any project that should always use hosted Sonnet.*
- OQ-02 (P1): **What's the CCR config schema** for routing per "agent / planner / background" model slots? Phase 1 only has one model, so all routes point at qwen3-coder:30b — but the schema needs to be right for Phase 2 to add Devstral/GLM cleanly. *Recommendation: read CCR's docs at impl time; design Phase 1 config to be Phase-2-extensible.*
- OQ-03 (P2): **Does CCR bind to a specific IP** or only 0.0.0.0? If 0.0.0.0, need to confirm pico's firewall blocks 3456 from non-tailnet sources (pf rules or macOS firewall config). *Recommendation: check CCR env contract first; if no explicit bind, document the firewall step.*
- OQ-04 (P2): **Pi install path** — `brew install pi-agent` vs `npm install -g @pi-dev/pi` vs `gh repo clone pi-dev/pi && bun install`. Verify canonical install before shipping mac.setup.sh edits. *Recommendation: read Pi's README at impl time.*
- OQ-05 (P3): **OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE — keep q8_0 or revisit?** For a 19 GB model + 128K context + Q8 KV, memory budget is tight. Serving agent said keep q8_0; but if context-length increase causes pressure, may need to drop to q4_0 KV. *Recommendation: keep q8_0 in Phase 1; benchmark memory footprint as part of testing; downshift only if OOM.*
- OQ-06 (P3): **Do we want an embedding model resident** (e.g. `nomic-embed-text`) for CC retrieval-style features? Phase 2 candidate. *Recommendation: defer to Phase 2; MAX_LOADED_MODELS=2 leaves the slot.*

title: pulse: a dirty checkout must NOT block a tick — proceed, work in the mess, commit your own paths, flag the rest
description:
## Context

Zig, 2026-07-30: *"pulses shouldn't trigger a tripwire if state is dirty. they
should proceed, so they can work in messy repos. then they can check in their
work when they're done and leave the dirty or flag it. then it won't do the
clunky lin-22h parking thing. but yea it shouldn't try to nuke or clean up repos
when they're dirty, they're all WIPs."*

This inverts a currently load-bearing gate, deliberately. Today it cost a full
fleet outage AND a clumsy workaround, both traceable to the same rule:

- An agent on the box edited `benchmarks-2026.md` in `~/linearb` and did not
  commit. `vps-repo-refresh.sh`'s read-only tripwire saw a dirty tracked file,
  wrote NO receipt, and `vps-preflight.sh` fail-closed — blocking **every remote
  row on every project**, not just di-thursday.
- Its remedy text says the file "MUST be reverted" with `git checkout --`. That
  advice would have destroyed verified benchmark-canon work. It survived only
  because the diff was inspected first.
- The orchestrator then could not park the change in zig-computer's working tree
  either, because **`vps-preflight.sh` blocks on uncommitted tracked changes on
  THIS machine too** — so the change had to be encoded into bead `lin-22h` as a
  patch and the tree restored. That is the "clunky parking thing".

## The rule

**Dirty is normal. Dirty is WIP. Dirty never blocks and never gets cleaned up.**

## Required changes

**1. `vps-repo-refresh.sh` — dirty tracked files become a WARN, not a failure.**
The refresh still writes its receipt. The receipt gains a `dirty` field listing
the paths per repo, so downstream can see the state rather than infer it.

**2. `vps-preflight.sh` — same on the zig-computer side.** "uncommitted tracked
changes will NOT reach the VPS" becomes a warning carried forward, not a block.
This is the specific gate that forced the `lin-22h` parking.

**3. NOTHING resets a dirty file. Ever.**
- Remove/neuter the `git checkout --` on harvest paths in step (b). Preserving a
  copy first does not make a reset acceptable under this rule.
- Nothing suggests `git checkout --` or `reset --hard` in any failure text.
- Re-word the tripwire message, which currently instructs the reader to revert.

**4. The pull must tolerate dirt.** `git pull --ff-only` can refuse when incoming
changes touch dirty files. That is NOT a failure now — the tick proceeds against
the older tree. But it MUST be recorded (see 5), because a tick running stale
code is the one thing that produces confidently-wrong output.

**5. Flagging is the price of proceeding — this is the load-bearing half.**
Zig's own standing principle: *"Missing output he catches. WRONG output he
cannot."* Removing the block removes the thing that made staleness impossible, so
the replacement must make staleness VISIBLE:
- the receipt records dirty paths + whether the pull actually advanced;
- the dispatcher surfaces that into the tick's `DISPATCH.md`, so the tick knows
  what state it is working in;
- the ledger row for that tick carries it, so a later reader can tell whether an
  artifact was produced against a clean, dirty, or stale checkout.
A tick that ran against a stale tree and said nothing is the failure mode this
bead must not create.

**6. ⚠️ THE WIP GUARD — the tick commits ONLY its own paths. NAME THE FILES.**
"Proceed on dirty" plus a careless stage equals a tick sweeping Zig'''s unrelated
work-in-progress into its own commit — strictly worse than losing a tick.

The first draft of this guard forbade `git add -A`, `git add .`, and
`git commit -a`, and **that list was incomplete**. Corrected 2026-07-30 by the
marketing-vps agent, which had just been bitten by the gap: the call that staged
12 deletions on the box was `git add refs/doc-scripts` — **a DIRECTORY**, none of
the three forbidden forms.

Verified locally in a scratch repo: with a file deleted from `d/`, plain
`git add d` stages `D d/gone.txt`. `git add <pathspec>` means "make the index
match the working tree there", INCLUDING removals. So any process mutating the
tree behind you — rsync, a sync client, a sibling agent — gets its deletions
folded into your commit under a message claiming you added something.

**The rule is: name the files.** Forbidden: `git add -A`, `git add .`,
`git commit -a`, and **any directory or glob pathspec**. Only explicit file paths.

Belt-and-braces check to run before committing (verified to catch the case above):

    test "$(git diff --cached --diff-filter=D --name-only | wc -l)" -eq 0 \
      || { echo "ABORT: staged deletions I did not intend"; \
           git diff --cached --diff-filter=D --name-only; }

State all of this in `DISPATCH.md` in the same breath as the new permission to
commit.

## Interaction with lin-ekx — ORDERING MATTERS

`lin-ekx` (the peer-framing sweep) is IN FLIGHT and edits
`pulse-dispatch-remote.sh`, its `DISPATCH.md` contract, and the `/vps` skill —
overlapping files. **Do not start this until lin-ekx has merged.** The two are
complements: lin-ekx grants the box the right to commit its own work; this bead
removes the gate that punished it for having uncommitted work in the meantime.

## Scope decision, recorded not assumed

Zig scoped this to **dirty** (uncommitted). `vps-preflight` assertion **A2**
(local HEAD not the published tip — i.e. COMMITTED but unpushed) is a different
axis and is NOT changed here: it means the box would run genuinely different
code. If Zig wants that relaxed too it is a one-line follow-on, but it was not
what he asked for and it trades away more than dirt does.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A dirty tracked file in a managed checkout produces a receipt + a warning,
      and the dispatch proceeds to completion.
- [ ] Uncommitted changes on zig-computer no longer block a dispatch.
- [ ] No code path resets, checks out, or stashes a dirty tracked file; no
      failure text recommends it.
- [ ] A pull refused because of dirt is non-fatal AND recorded.
- [ ] Receipt carries `dirty` paths and pull-advanced status; the tick sees it;
      the ledger row records it.
- [ ] `DISPATCH.md` tells the tick to commit its own authored paths explicitly
      and forbids `git add -A` / `git add .` / `commit -a`.
- [ ] Tests for: dirty-but-proceeds, pull-refused-but-proceeds, receipt contents,
      and an assertion that no reset command exists in the refresh path.
- [ ] EVIDENCE: dirty a tracked file on the box on purpose, run a real
      `--dry-run` dispatch, show it reaching `dry-run-ok` with the dirty path
      named in the output — then show the file still dirty and unmodified.

title: vps-dispatch: oob-exclude directive — stop rsyncing a path that reaches the box by its own transport
description:
## Context

`require-oob-untracked $HOME/linearb` (the complement rule) pushes every top-level
child of `~/linearb` that git does not own. It cannot tell "git does not own this"
from "a DIFFERENT git owns this", so `lb-granola` — a nested independent repo whose
own remote (`azigler/lb-granola`) the box's PAT CAN reach — was being rsync'd as
out-of-band cargo on every dispatch.

Two problems with that, both real:

1. **Freshness.** As OOB cargo the corpus only moved when an unrelated pulse tick
   was dispatched. Measured 2026-07-28: a meeting delivered `17:08:48Z` reached the
   VPS at `18:44:39Z`, 1h36m later, and would have waited days over a quiet weekend.
2. **Two writers.** `rsync -az --delete` over a git working tree dirties it relative
   to HEAD — the same "git and rsync would fight over the same files" argument the
   complement rule's own comment already makes.

Adds an explicit `oob-exclude <path>` directive, pre-scanned so it is order-independent,
and declares lb-granola with it. The VPS now pulls the corpus itself every 2 min
(`~/bin/lb-granola-pull.sh`). Cross-ref: `lbg-y1y` in the lb-granola repo.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `oob-exclude` directive parsed and honored by the complement rule in
      `pulse-dispatch-remote.sh`; declared for lb-granola in `vps-repo-manifest.txt`.
- [x] Order-independent (pre-scan), so the manifest never depends on directive order.
- [x] Regression test: the complement rule STILL ships an untracked child that has its
      own `.git` (the imc-aug26 case), `oob-exclude` drops only the declared child, and
      order does not matter.
- [x] Full suite green (91 PASS / 0 FAIL); negative control confirmed 90/1 with the
      inferred rule injected.

## Notes

Deliberately an EXPLICIT directive, not the tempting inference
`[ -e "$_c/.git" ] && continue`. That inference is wrong and was verified wrong:
`imc-aug26` has its own `.git` AND is untracked by the umbrella, but its remote is
`lb-marketing/*`, which this box's PAT 404s on — rsync is its ONLY possible transport.
Inferring would have silently stranded the August IMC folder, producing exactly the
failure the complement rule's own comment warns about ("a tick drafts confidently
WITHOUT campaign context — wrong output, not missing output"). The regression test
above exists specifically to fail if someone later "simplifies" it back.

title: tailnet acl: add Taildrop file-sharing grant (bi-directional server↔user)
description:
## Context

Discovered while delivering `stable-diffusion-handoff.md` to the iPhone
via `tailscale file cp /tmp/stable-diffusion-handoff.md iphone-15-pro:`:
the command refused with `cannot send files: peer is owned by a
different user`. Tailscale's default-deny ACL treats Taildrop as a
per-user feature — devices owned by the same user can drop to each
other, but cross-owner (and tag→user) transfers are blocked by default.

zig-computer + pico are tagged `tag:server` (machine identities, no
user). iPhone + metis are owned by `azigler@`. Without a grant, no
file-sharing between them.

## Fix

Added a `grants` block to `tailscale/acl.jsonc` using the
`tailscale.com/cap/file-sharing` capability. Combined src+dst arrays
cover the full server↔user matrix in one rule. Capability-only grant
(no L3 traffic implication beyond what existing acls allow).

After applying via Tailscale admin console paste:
```bash
tailscale file cp <file> iphone-15-pro:    # tag:server → user
tailscale file cp <file> zig-computer:     # user → tag:server (from metis / iPhone)
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `tailscale/acl.jsonc` updated with `grants` block
- [x] Comment block documents the rationale + capability syntax
- [ ] User pastes updated acl.jsonc into Tailscale admin console
- [ ] `tailscale file cp /tmp/stable-diffusion-handoff.md iphone-15-pro:`
      succeeds from zig-computer (verification target)
- [ ] Inverse direction tested optionally (drop from iPhone Tailscale
      app to zig-computer)
notes:
## CLOSED 2026-05-24 — WON'T FIX (Tailscale design limitation)

Tailscale's admin policy editor rejected the grants block with:
"Error: capability name must not be in the tailscale.com domain" —
the namespace is reserved for built-in, non-user-configurable features.

Confirmed via Tailscale docs (kb/1106/taildrop): "Taildrop is currently
limited to sending files between your own personal devices. You cannot
send files to devices owned by other users (even users on the same
Tailscale network)." Hard-locked by design; no ACL grant, nodeAttr,
or admin toggle.

Workarounds documented in zig-zone runbook gotcha #23:
- HTTP over tailnet IP (one-off): `python3 -m http.server` bound to
  `tailscale ip -4`, fetch from any tailnet device
- SSH relay through a user-owned tailnet device (scp → device A,
  Taildrop → device B)
- Untag the source (re-auth as user, breaks the identity model)

ACL revert pushed; comment block updated to document the limitation
so future-me doesn't re-try.

title: vps-8a9eb245: full checkout + per-host shell files + system-owned tmux
description:
## Context

This box (vps-8a9eb245) had a SPARSE checkout of dotfiles (cone: `agents`,
`claude` only), so the shell tier was still served by `~/marketing-vps` — a
coworker-facing repo, not Zig's own:

    ~/.zshrc     -> /home/andrew/marketing-vps/config/zsh/.zshrc
    ~/.p10k.zsh  -> /home/andrew/marketing-vps/config/zsh/.p10k.zsh
    ~/.tmux.conf -> /home/andrew/marketing-vps/config/tmux/tmux.conf

Both `zsh/.zshrc` and `bash/.bashrc` source `$HOME/.$(hostname -s).{zsh,bashrc}`,
and `sync.sh` symlinks those from `zsh/`/`bash/` when present. Neither existed
for this host, so even a full checkout would have left the box with no PATH /
toolchain env.

tmux ownership (verified): server PID 83840 sits in
`/user.slice/user-1002.slice/session-140.scope` — an abandoned LOGIN-SESSION
scope. It survives logout only by policy default (`KillUserProcesses=no` +
`Linger=yes`), not by ownership. Panes DO escape (tmux 3.6 is linked against
libsystemd and moves them to `user@1002.service/tmux-spawn-*.scope`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `git sparse-checkout disable` — full working tree
- [ ] `zsh/.vps-8a9eb245.zsh` written, matching this box's real toolchains
- [ ] `bash/.vps-8a9eb245.bashrc` written
- [ ] `tmux/tmux.service` — systemd USER unit, installed + enabled (NOT started;
      Zig restarts the server himself)
- [ ] `download.sh` + `sync.sh` run clean
- [ ] `zsh -l -i -c exit` exits 0 with no errors — login shell not broken
- [ ] `~/.zshrc` + `~/.tmux.conf` resolve into `~/dotfiles`, not `~/marketing-vps`
- [ ] hourly `vps-repo-refresh.timer` still does an ff-only pull of `~/dotfiles`
- [ ] `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` removal kept in `claude/settings.json`; the pico proxy
      moved to `zsh/.zig-computer.zsh` so zig-computer keeps it
notes:
CLOSED with one criterion installed-but-unproven; that gap is now CLOSED TOO.

tmux ownership PROVEN 2026-07-28 00:29 — Zig ran the cutover himself:

  Name:   tmux: server                 (pid 403325)
  PPid:   83760  ->  /usr/lib/systemd/systemd --user
  cgroup: /user.slice/user-1002.slice/user@1002.service/app.slice/tmux.service

The proof is the SERVER PROCESS's cgroup + parentage, not the unit's
ControlGroup string — a unit always has a cgroup; the question was whether the
daemonized server landed in it, and it did. Direct parent is the user manager.
Old session-140.scope is gone; no session-*.scope remains under user-1002.slice.

Unit: enabled + active, SubState=exited, Result=success (correct for
Type=oneshot + RemainAfterExit). Boot: default.target.wants symlink present,
Linger=yes.

`app.slice` in the path is expected — systemd >= 251 files user services there.
The load-bearing element is `user@1002.service/` before it.

Unplanned benefit: continuum/resurrect are active for the first time (the old
server never loaded them; ~/.tmux/resurrect did not exist). Layout now survives
reboot, not just disconnect.

title: vault mirror: a git checkout reproduces CONTENT but not identity or time
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Zig, on vps-8a9eb245 after the full-mirror pull:
1. Open `~/linearb/pipeline-website` — no transcript history, though the vault
   demonstrably has it.
2. Look at any mirrored transcript list — everything reads "1 day ago"; all
   recency ordering is gone.

## Context

Two independent defects, one root cause: **a git checkout is not a faithful
mirror.** It reproduces file CONTENT but carries neither the local IDENTITY a
lookup needs nor the TIME the file actually has.

### 1. Identity — 78 projects present but invisible

Claude Code resolves history by a slug derived from `$PWD`, so a box whose unix
user is not the primary's looks for `-home-andrew-foo` while the vault holds
`-home-ubuntu-foo`. `session-start.sh` creates that symlink — but only for the
project a session is STARTING in. That is too late to browse history you have
not opened, and useless for "is my old work here?".

Measured: 91 canonical slugs, 13 aliases. **78 projects fully on disk and
completely unreachable.** The earlier fix made the transform universal but kept
it LAZY; laziness was the remaining half of the bug.

### 2. Time — the whole back catalogue collapsed to one day

git does not record mtimes, so every pulled file is stamped at checkout. The real
time is already IN the file: each session line carries an ISO `timestamp`, and
the last is when the session ended. Strictly better than the git commit date,
which records when the vault happened to sync — on one pipeline-website session
the content ended 2026-07-14 but was committed 2026-07-26, a 12-day error.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `agents/vault/restore-mtimes.py` — derives mtime from embedded timestamps.
      Tail-first byte regex (files reach tens of MB; JSONL is append-ordered);
      never parses JSON, so a truncated final line in a live session cannot trip
      it; skips symlinked dirs so aliases cannot double-visit; only `os.utime`.
- [x] Backfill: 7,334 files corrected, largest 183 days. Idempotent (re-run = 0).
- [x] Derivation cross-checked against a full JSON parse — exact match.
- [x] 78 aliases created; pipeline-website resolves to its 2 transcripts.
- [x] Both made durable in `vault-sync.sh` step 1a, peer-guarded, so a slug the
      primary invents is aliased and correctly stamped on the next hourly pull.
- [x] NEGATIVE CONTROLS (not just "ran clean"): deleted 2 aliases -> sync logged
      `aliased 2 new slug(s)` and restored both; forced an mtime to now -> sync
      restored 2026-07-14 23:50:53.

## Notes

`--since 180` bounds the hourly pass to what a pull just touched; a full backfill
stays a manual `restore-mtimes.py` run. 161 files carry no timestamp at all and
are left alone rather than guessed at.

title: dotfiles runs two durable sessions but has no refs/.handoff-per-window — the notes overwrite each other
description:
## Context
`refs/session-handoff.md` is a single file and `/offboard` overwrites it. `dotfiles` now
demonstrably hosts MORE THAN ONE durable session: this repo is worked from zig-computer
AND from marketing-vps, which is a second writer by design (agents/infra.md).

Nothing is lost — both notes are in git history — but the resume doc is what `/onboard`
actually reads, and it silently presents one session as if it were the whole picture.
The failure mode is not deletion; it is a partial view that looks complete.

## Steps to Reproduce
Observed live 2026-08-04, no synthetic repro needed:

    git log --oneline --all -- refs/session-handoff.md | head -4
      26d08d8  offboard: handoff note (899c6004)          <- marketing-vps session
      4173df7  offboard: note the live second writer
      8f83a4b  offboard: handoff note (188ce668)          <- zig-computer session

    ls refs/.handoff-per-window     -> No such file or directory
    head -1 refs/session-handoff.md -> "# Session handoff — 2026-08-04 899c6004 (marketing-vps)"

Session 188ce668 wrote its note; session 899c6004 wrote its own; the merge took the
latter. The working file now carries only one of the two.

## The documented fix, and why it is not a plain `touch`
`/offboard` already supports this: a project running >1 durable session opts in with
`refs/.handoff-per-window`, and `agents/lib/handoff-path.sh` scopes the note to
`session-handoff--<window>.md`, keyed by the **tmux window name**.

⚠️ Whether WINDOW is the right key here is the open question. `~/explore` uses it for two
windows on ONE machine. dotfiles collides across two MACHINES, and both boxes run a tmux
session called `work` — the same namespace collision `dotfiles-ogkz` had to fix for
agentgateway attribution by adding a machine dimension. Two same-named windows on
different hosts would still clobber each other.

`handoff-path.sh` gained `HANDOFF_WINDOW` and a "stop serving another window's handoff"
fix on 2026-08-04 (`ac0c5f8`, `5981654`) — read those before designing.

## Options
1. opt in as-is, accept window-name collisions across hosts
2. key on `<hostname>--<window>` (mirrors the agentgateway `group`/`user` split)
3. stay single-file and have `/offboard` APPEND a bounded number of prior notes

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] two sessions on DIFFERENT hosts offboard without either note disappearing
- [ ] `/onboard` reads the right one, and can see that others exist
- [ ] a same-named window on two hosts is PROVEN not to collide
- [ ] `agents/lib/test-handoff-path.sh` covers the cross-host case
notes:
## The decision HARVEST collides too, not just the note (2026-08-04)

Observed at the second offboard of session 188ce668. Step 2.5 harvests `-t decision`
beads created since `.claude/last-offboard-session` was stamped. With two sessions
sharing one project, that marker is also shared, so the harvest returns the OTHER
session decisions as if they were this one:

    cut: Mon Aug  4 (marker rewritten by the other session)
    - dotfiles-9o46  kill switch ...        <- marketing-vps session, NOT mine
    - dotfiles-volw  isolation guard ...    <- mine

The marketing-vps handoff hit the mirror image and said so explicitly: its harvest went a
WEEK wide and surfaced eight decisions of which one was its own.

So the fix has to cover BOTH artifacts that key off session identity — the handoff note
AND the last-offboard marker — or the harvest keeps reporting another session work as
this one. That is worse than the note collision: a wrong handoff is visibly one
session view, whereas a contaminated decision list reads as an accurate record of what
this session decided.

Both markers resolve through `agents/lib/handoff-path.sh`, so whichever key is chosen
(window, or `<hostname>--<window>`) should apply to `offboard_pending_path` and
`last_offboard_path` as well as `handoff_path`.

## ABSORBS dotfiles-9w9l (2026-08-05)
`dotfiles-9w9l` (P3, open since 2026-07-28) is the SAME defect, found first:
"handoff-path: window keying cannot distinguish two MACHINES — same-day offboards collide."
I filed this bead without scanning the backlog and rediscovered it. 9w9l is closed pointing
here; this bead keeps the measured evidence (the live 2026-08-04 collision, the contaminated
decision harvest, the three keying options) and 9w9l's P3 is superseded by P2.

9w9l's own worked example is worth keeping, because it shows the workaround people reach for:
a marketing-vps session working on **lb-granola** could not write `refs/session-handoff.md`
without clobbering a NEWER zig-computer note, so it wrote
`refs/session-handoff--marketing-vps.md` beside it by hand and explained why in the header.
That is the correct instinct implemented manually, in a third repo, by one session that
happened to notice. It is evidence the fix belongs in `handoff-path.sh`, not in each
session's judgement.

title: tools/githooks/pre-commit advertises ~90s for the scrutiny-guard harness; it measures ~130s
description:
## Context
Raised by the dotfiles-3137 agent as adjacent. `tools/githooks/pre-commit` tells the
committer the scrutiny-guard mutation harness takes roughly 90 seconds. Measured on
zig-computer during dotfiles-3137: **~130s**, for BOTH the old and the new harness — so
this is not a regression from the hardening, it is drift. The underlying suites grew
(85 + 61 cases).

A wrong duration in a gate message is a small thing that behaves badly: the committer
waits for 90s, concludes the hook has hung at ~100s, and interrupts a gate that was
working. That is the same shape as CLAUDE.md rule 2 — a documented claim that agents and
humans act on.

## Steps to Reproduce
    cd ~/dotfiles
    grep -n "90s\|~90" tools/githooks/pre-commit
    time bash agents/hooks/test/mutate-scrutiny-guards.sh
    # measured ~130s (load ~8.7); the advertised figure is ~90s

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] the advertised figure matches a fresh measurement, taken on an idle-ish box
- [ ] the message says what it is timing (the harness, not the whole hook) so the next
      drift is attributable
- [ ] the same check applied to the other advertised duration in that file, if any
- [ ] whatever number lands was RUN, not estimated (rule 2)
notes:
## A SECOND stale/absent duration, and the aggregate nobody has looked at (2026-08-05)

The original finding: pre-commit advertises ~90s for the scrutiny-guard harness, measures ~130s.

Added by dotfiles-nnmm: a THIRD mutation gate now runs on pre-commit, for the pulse-inject
seat logic. Measured on a 12-core box and documented honestly in the hook itself:

    test-pulse-inject.sh (full, 113 cases)        107s
    mutate-pulse-seat.sh (5 mutants + baseline)   252s   -> the gate announces "~4.5 min"

Zig 2026-08-05: **~6 min on those three files is acceptable for now.** So this is not a
request to make it faster. It is a request to make the ADVERTISED numbers true, and to
look at the total once.

The aggregate, which no single bead has ever owned:

    ensure-fleet-tunnel      ~63s   (its own trigger paths)
    scrutiny-guards          ~130s  (advertised ~90s  <- the original defect)
    pulse-inject seat        ~252s  (advertised ~4.5 min, close enough)

Each was individually justified when added. Three gates arrived in ~4 days. The risk is not
any one of them — it is that a committer who waits past an advertised figure interrupts a
gate that was working, and that the next addition is argued on its own merits again.

## Acceptance Criteria (superseding the original, which only covered the scrutiny figure)
- [ ] every advertised duration in tools/githooks/pre-commit matches a fresh measurement
- [ ] each message says WHAT it is timing, so the next drift is attributable
- [ ] the file states the worst-case total for a commit touching several trigger sets
- [ ] numbers are RUN, not estimated (CLAUDE.md rule 2)

title: bug: harnessd renders every pulse bounce as 'blocked on Andrew' regardless of reason
description:
Found by the dotfiles-mrta fix agent, 2026-07-26.

dotfiles-mrta added a second bounce reason: a readiness timeout now records
reason:"not_ready" instead of silently eating the tick. But
~/harnessd/bin/harness_state.py:268-272 hardcodes
  detail = "tick bounced — window blocked on Andrew"
regardless of the reason field.

The STATE is right (bounced, correctly overriding the false "tick in flight") —
only the prose lies. A not_ready bounce (cold boot, Claude not up yet) will be
reported to Zig as "blocked on Andrew", which is a different situation demanding
a different response.

Also stale: read_pulse_bounces_live's docstring at :806 still says "one JSONL
object per 🔔-deferred tick", which is no longer the only kind.

Fix: branch the detail string on reason. Small.

Relates: dotfiles-mrta (closed), dotfiles-cxle (the flag-written-where-nothing-
reads generator — this is the inverse: the reader ignoring a flag that IS written).

title: ccr: pin to 1.0.73 — v2.0.0 has regression (routing returns 'Provider undefined' for all requests)
description:
## Problem
@musistudio/claude-code-router v2.0.0 (released 2026-05-25, npm-default
since) has a routing regression: every request returns 404 'Provider
"undefined" not found' regardless of model name, request shape, or
endpoint. The Router.default / Router.background / etc. config is read
(providers register successfully at startup) but the request handler
can't resolve them.

Downgrade to 1.0.73 (last 1.x) restores full routing.

## Steps to Reproduce on 2.0.0
1. npm install -g @musistudio/claude-code-router@2.0.0
2. ccr restart
3. curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3456/v1/messages \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
     -d '{"model":"claude-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ok"}],"max_tokens":5}'
4. Returns 404 'Provider "undefined" not found' (any model name fails)

## Fix
- npm install -g @musistudio/claude-code-router@1.0.73
- ccr restart
- Avoid `npm install -g @musistudio/claude-code-router` (latest) until 2.x is verified

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CCR pinned to 1.0.73 (current state — DONE 2026-06-01 this session)
- [ ] Note in dotfiles README or CLAUDE.md warning against 2.x upgrade
- [ ] When 2.x routing regression resolves upstream, re-evaluate

title: CLAUDE.md rule 2: run the example VERBATIM — extract it from the committed file, don't retype it
description:
Standing-practice proposal promoted out of the 2026-08-03 handoff (offboard Step 2.6). Filed rather than edited: rule 1 already took an addition this session, and a second rules change to the same always-loaded file in the same session deserves Zig's eye.

## Context
Rule 2 says: "Before committing an example, run it." That is right and it has a gap —
it does not say run WHAT. Running a retyped or paraphrased version of the example proves
the idea works; it does not prove the bytes in the file work. The two diverge exactly
when a quoting or substitution detail is the thing that breaks, which is the common case
for shell examples in this repo (see rule 7: `$0`/`$N` are rewritten in a rendered
SKILL.md before the agent ever sees them, invisibly to grep and to review).

## The practice worth encoding
Extract the block from the COMMITTED file — by regex or line range — and execute that.
Done twice today and it is meaningfully stronger:
  - dotfiles-xugk: the /commit fix block was pulled out of the committed SKILL.md by awk
    and run under zsh against a throwaway repo. Push rejected -> fallback fired -> merge
    -> push landed -> ls-remote MATCH.
  - dotfiles-3afr: the cited harness path was run rather than eyeballed (28/28).

Neither found a divergence this time. That is not an argument against it — it is what a
guard looks like when it holds.

## Cost
Small. It is a few lines of awk/sed in the verification step, and it replaces a
retyping step that was going to happen anyway.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] rule 2 says to run the example AS COMMITTED, extracted rather than retyped
- [ ] it stays one sentence — rule 2 is already long and this is a refinement, not a
      new rule
- [ ] the worked example cited actually happened
