title: human: controlled reboot test of pico — harness-wide, and there is NO way back in if it fails
description:
## Context

Filed 2026-07-26 from the vs14d session. pico's boot persistence was audited
end-to-end and the one blocking gap is fixed, but **nothing has actually been
rebooted** — six things are unprovable without doing it, and the test is
fleet-wide rather than a vs14 concern.

## Why this is not a casual reboot

**1. It takes down the LLM control plane for every Claude Code session.**
`~/.claude/settings.json` on zig-computer sets
`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL = http://100.72.47.4:17017/claude`. Every session, including
whichever one is running the test, routes inference through `agentgateway` on
pico. If it does not come back, **Claude Code cannot be used to diagnose why.**

**2. There is NO out-of-band access to pico.** Measured: `ip route get
100.72.47.4` → `dev tailscale0`, and that is the only path. pico is a home Mac
behind NAT with no public IP; zig-computer is a VPS on a different network.
Screen sharing binds `*:5900` but is still only reachable over the tailnet from
here. **If tailscaled does not come back, pico is unreachable and recovery
requires physically walking to the machine.**

**3. It takes two public sites down** — `vs14.zig.computer` (via pico:8080) and
`webmention.andrewzigler.com` (via pico:14829) — plus the inference stack,
postgres, the seven containers, Keycloak (so admin login), and the homeowner's
LAN route to the picod portal.

## What is already proven, and what is not

**Fixed and verified before this bead:**
- `homebrew.mxcl.nginx` had NO KeepAlive and died at the last reboot
  (`bind() to 100.72.47.4:8080 failed (49)` at 15:52:32 on May 28, pid 364
  racing tailscaled at pid 367) and stayed dead **14 days** until a brew upgrade
  restarted it. `KeepAlive` + `ThrottleInterval=10` added and loaded.
- zig-computer's nginx had the same race one layer up — it does not bind a
  tailnet address, but it resolves `pico.tailfb4637.ts.net` in `proxy_pass` at
  config-load time via MagicDNS, and shipped `Restart=no`. Drop-in added:
  `After=/Wants=tailscaled.service`, `Restart=on-failure`, `RestartSec=10`.
- A duplicate `homebrew.mxcl.tailscale` LaunchAgent was crash-looping
  **242,422** times (EX_CONFIG — tailscaled needs root, the agent runs as pico).
  Booted out and disabled; the system daemon that actually owns the tunnel
  (pid 367, runs=1) untouched.
- Auto-login enabled on pico, so LaunchAgents now fire at boot.

**Genuine reassurance for the scariest item:** tailscaled is a system
LaunchDaemon and was **pid 367 at the May 28 boot, `runs = 1`, never exited** —
so it demonstrably does come back. That is the one boot-critical service with
real historical evidence.

**Still unprovable without rebooting:** auto-login actually firing (configured
today, never exercised); whether that session is a full Aqua session a `vz` VM
will start in; agentgateway's real boot behaviour (its plist is dated Jul 1, the
last boot was May 28 — it has NEVER been through one); whether nginx's new retry
cadence beats a cold-WAN tailscale handshake; the true recovery ordering; and
**11 of 26 enabled jobs are younger than the 59-day uptime and have never seen a
boot at all.**

## How to run it

`~/vs14d/ops/pico/post-reboot-verify.sh` is the checklist — **35 pass / 1 fail**
when run as a baseline today, the single red being the nginx gap now closed.
Run it before, reboot, run it after, diff.

Suggested conditions:
- [ ] A window where Zig is physically able to reach pico, since that is the
      only recovery path
- [ ] Not during a live Claude Code session doing anything that matters
- [ ] Baseline `post-reboot-verify.sh` captured immediately beforehand
- [ ] Know that `/etc/kcpassword` was hand-written (sysadminctl failed with
      SACSetAutoLoginPassword error:22) and round-trip verified but **never
      tested by an actual boot** — if auto-login does not fire, the LaunchAgents
      do not fire either, and that is the likeliest failure

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Reboot performed in a controlled window
- [ ] `post-reboot-verify.sh` re-run; every previously-passing check still passes
- [ ] agentgateway confirmed serving `:17017` and a Claude Code session works
- [ ] Both public sites 200; Keycloak login exercised; containers all healthy
- [ ] Anything that did not return gets a plist or a documented manual step
- [ ] The six unprovable items above converted into measured facts
notes:
UPDATED 2026-07-26 after the homework was finished and re-measured.

BASELINE IS NOW GREEN: `~/vs14d/ops/pico/post-reboot-verify.sh` reports
**36 pass / 0 fail / 0 warn — "GREEN. Every critical service returned."**
(It was 35/1 when written; the single red was the nginx KeepAlive gap, now
closed.) Re-run by hand rather than assumed.

RECOVERY PATH — CORRECTED BY ZIG, and the original framing was too dire.

I wrote "there is NO way back in." That is only true in ONE direction. The
asymmetry, verified:

  zig-computer -> pico   requires the tailnet. `ip route get 100.72.47.4` ->
                         `dev tailscale0`, and pico is behind NAT with no public
                         IP. If tailscaled does not come back, this direction is
                         genuinely dead.
  pico -> zig-computer   does NOT. pico holds ~/.ssh/id_ed25519, routes to the
                         internet via 192.168.1.1 on en0, and zig-computer's
                         sshd listens on 0.0.0.0:22 with a public IP
                         (51.81.33.136). That path does not involve tailscale at
                         all.

And Zig has PHYSICAL access to pico, which is the decisive point: worst case is
inconvenience, not loss.

Worth considering (not required): a boot-time reverse tunnel from pico to
zig-computer would turn that outbound asymmetry into a real out-of-band channel
and remove the tailscale dependency from recovery entirely. Optional — physical
access already covers it.

THE SIX THINGS ONLY A REBOOT CAN SETTLE, and why each is unprovable:

1. **Whether auto-login fires at all.** Configured today; `/etc/kcpassword` was
   hand-written because `sysadminctl` failed with SACSetAutoLoginPassword
   error:22. Round-trip verified (the file decodes back to the typed password)
   but that only proves the ENCODER is self-consistent, not that macOS agrees
   with it. macOS reads that file exactly once, at boot. The entire LOGIN tier
   rides on it — agentgateway, postgres, the VM, seven containers, the vs14
   site, go-jamming.
2. **Whether that session is a full Aqua session a `vz` VM will start in.**
   Distinct from (1): the session can exist and still be the wrong KIND. colima's
   VM needs a graphical session context; a LoginWindow-tier session would let
   LaunchAgents run and still fail to start the VM. Only observable after a real
   login.
3. **agentgateway's actual boot behaviour.** Inferred entirely from its plist
   semantics (RunAtLoad + KeepAlive{SuccessfulExit=false}, throttle 10s). Its
   plist is dated Jul 1; the last boot was May 28 — **it has never been through
   one.** And this is the LLM control plane for every Claude Code session.
4. **Whether nginx's new KeepAlive actually wins the race.** It will certainly
   retry; whether the retry cadence converges before or after tailscaled
   completes a control-plane handshake over a COLD WAN is a timing property of
   the real network on the real morning. Retry is unbounded so it should
   converge — "should" is doing the work in that sentence.
5. **The true recovery ordering and total time to green.** The predicted
   sequence is assembled from throttle values and interval settings, not
   measured. Nothing declares these dependencies to launchd; five services bind
   the tailnet address and survive only because KeepAlive retries until it
   appears. That is robustness by accident, and accidents have timing.
6. **Whether the eleven jobs created since May 28 behave at boot.** Enabled and
   never boot-tested: com.zig.agentgateway, com.zig.colima, com.zig.gojamming,
   com.zig.harness, com.zig.ss14-backup, com.zig.vs14-autoheal,
   com.zig.vs14-postgres-retention, homebrew.mxcl.postgresql@17,
   com.zig.ha-portal-proxy, com.zig.ollama, com.canonical.multipassd.
   **Eleven of twenty-six enabled jobs are younger than the 59-day uptime.**
   That is the real shape of the risk: not one suspect service, but a
   configuration whose MAJORITY has never been exercised by the event we are
   about to trigger.

The common thread: every one is a property of the boot TRANSITION, and a running
system carries no evidence about a transition it has not made. This is the
irreducible residue after the audit — which is exactly why it is a scheduled
test rather than more analysis.

ALSO FOUND, not blocking, but the same family: `com.zig.tmux` is crash-looping
at ~241,920 runs (exit 1). That is the THIRD such loop on pico — the tailscale
duplicate agent had 242,422 and vs14-web had 237,737 before it was fixed today.
Three jobs in permanent restart loops that nobody noticed is a pattern
(dotfiles-cxle), not three coincidences. Filed separately.

title: guard: session-start should assert ~/.claude/settings.json is still a symlink (it silently reverts)
description:
## Why

`dotfiles-2wqv` restored the `~/.claude/settings.json` symlink after it had been a
regular file since ~2026-07-10. **It will almost certainly break again.** Claude Code
writes that file atomically (temp + `rename`), and `rename()` replaces a symlink with
a regular file. Anything that makes Claude Code write global settings does it:
accepting a permission, changing effort in the menu, toggling fast mode.

The failure is **completely silent**, and the damage compounds — the file keeps
working, so nothing alarms, while the tracked template quietly falls behind. Last time
it drifted 5 settings, including `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` (the proxy carrying ALL API
traffic) and the Agent isolation hook. It also left `effortLevel: xhigh` in the
template, which is the Opus 5 WebSearch-killer — so a fresh machine or a `sync.sh`
restore would have silently reinstalled a broken config.

This is a **checkable invariant**, which per the harness's own policy means it belongs
in a hook, not in a habit.

## Sketch

In `agents/hooks/session-start.sh`: if `~/.claude/settings.json` is NOT a symlink
(`[ ! -L ]`), emit a visible warning naming the fix (`bash ~/dotfiles/sync.sh claude`)
AND the merge-first caveat.

**Do NOT auto-repair.** Blindly re-symlinking would DESTROY whatever Claude Code or a
human added to the live copy since the break — that is the entire lesson of
dotfiles-2wqv, where live was a superset by 5 settings.

Cheap refinement: when it has reverted, `diff` live vs template and print which KEYS
diverged, so the merge is mechanical rather than archaeological.

## Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] session-start warns when `~/.claude/settings.json` is not a symlink
* [ ] the warning names the exact remediation AND the merge-first caveat
* [ ] it does NOT auto-repair
* [ ] verified by temporarily replacing the symlink with a copy, confirming the warning fires, then restoring
* [ ] no measurable startup cost (runs on every session)
notes:
## Fixed — 2026-07-26 (Opus-5 audit Wave 1)

session-start.sh:104-149 — warns on [ ! -L ], names the diverged keys via jq, prints the remediation merge-first, never auto-repairs, exempts worktrees. New test file, 19 cases.
The bead's own acceptance criterion (verify by replacing the live symlink with a copy) was DELIBERATELY NOT followed literally — that is an instruction to mutate live global config as a test step. Everything runs under a temp $HOME, and case 9 asserts the real ~/.claude/settings.json is in the same state after the run as before.
close_reason: Fixed and pushed in Wave 1 of the Opus-5 audit.

title: pulse-dispatch-remote: the preflight block message asserts a cause it never checked and points at stderr that was never captured — a 2-day-old failure with an empty diagnostic trail
description:
## Context

`pulse-di-thursday.service` failed 2026-07-30 13:00:18 UTC and sat in
`systemctl --user --failed` for **two days**. The unit behaved impeccably — fail-closed,
nothing dispatched, no remote tokens spent, no misleading ledger row, a
`PULSE_DISPATCH_RESULT=failed-preflight` marker on the terminal path. The
unattended-reporting contract (`dotfiles-cxle`) did its job.

**The defect is that the diagnostic it produced is empty and wrong.**

### (a) The message asserts a cause it never checked

`agents/scheduler/pulse-dispatch-remote.sh:1048-1050` fails with a hardcoded string on
**any** non-zero preflight exit:

```bash
if ! "$PREFLIGHT" "${PF_ARGS[@]}"; then
  fail failed-preflight 73 "vps-preflight blocked (assertions A1 empty-submodule / A2 stale-HEAD).
```

`vps-preflight.sh` exits non-zero from at least four paths that have nothing to do with
A1 or A2: `exit 64` (unknown arg), `exit 65` (manifest not found), `exit 69` (jq
missing), `exit 69` (ssh missing). All four would be reported as an A1/A2 assertion
failure. The exit code is discarded rather than switched on.

### (b) It points at stderr that does not exist

The message says *"Its stderr above names the exact repo and remedy."* For this run there
is no such stderr. Full-precision journal, the entire preflight window:

```
13:00:16.456050  sync T1 + preflight A1+A2: refreshing marketing-vps and judging the receipt locally
13:00:18.111919  PULSE-DISPATCH: BLOCKED — vps-preflight blocked (assertions A1 ... / A2 ...)
```

**1.65 seconds of execution, zero output.** No global stderr redirection exists in the
dispatch script, and every `exit` in `vps-preflight.sh` is preceded by a `>&2` message —
so this should have been impossible.

### (c) And it did not take the path the message names

`vps-preflight.sh:176` — `block() { write_report; printf 'VPS-PREFLIGHT: BLOCKED...' >&2; exit "$2"; }` — **writes the report BEFORE printing.** The run directory
`~/.local/state/pulse-dispatch/20260730T130008Z-di-thursday/` contains no
`checkout-state.json`, while later successful runs
(`20260731T190650Z-di-friday`, `20260731T233702Z-di-monday`) do. So the preflight
**did not exit via `block()`** — i.e. not via A1 or A2 — and the message claiming it did
is false on this exact run. What it did do is still unknown, which is the point.

### (d) The artifact a reader would open repeats the false pointer

`surface-blocked.json` — the one durable file an operator opens — carries
`"detail": "...Its stderr above names the exact repo and remedy."` It forwards the
pointer without the payload.

### Why it went unnoticed for 2 days

It escalated into two surfaces with no reader: `systemctl --user --failed` (see the
sibling finding — nothing on this box reads it) and an AskUserQuestion delivered to tmux
window `work:di`, which no longer exists. So even a diligent operator following the trail
finds nothing. The condition self-resolved: `di-friday` ran clean on 07-31. That is what
makes it easy to keep not noticing.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `systemctl --user show pulse-di-thursday.service -p Result -p ExecMainExitTimestamp`
   -> `Result=exit-code`, `ExecMainExitTimestamp=Thu 2026-07-30 13:00:18 UTC`.
2. `journalctl --user -u pulse-di-thursday.service --since '2026-07-30 13:00:00' --until '2026-07-30 13:00:25' -o short-precise`
   -> 1.65 s between the preflight announcement and the BLOCKED line, with no output between.
3. `ls ~/.local/state/pulse-dispatch/20260730T130008Z-di-thursday/` -> no
   `checkout-state.json`. Compare `20260731T190650Z-di-friday/`, which has one.
4. `sed -n '176p' agents/scheduler/vps-preflight.sh` -> `block()` writes the report first,
   so (3) rules out the cause the message names.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The preflight's stdout+stderr are **captured to a file** in `$LOCAL_STATE`
      (e.g. `preflight.err`, beside the existing `rsync.err` / `tunnel.err`) as well as
      reaching the journal. A tee, not a redirect — do not trade one lost copy for another.
- [ ] The `fail` message switches on the preflight's **actual exit code**. 64/65/69 are
      usage / manifest / missing-dependency and must not be reported as A1/A2. An
      unrecognised code says so rather than guessing.
- [ ] `surface-blocked.json`'s `detail` carries the **captured stderr tail and the exit
      code**, not a pointer to them. It is the artifact a reader opens.
- [ ] Determine what actually exited non-zero at 1.65 s with no output and no report —
      the reproduction above is the starting point. If it turns out to be unreachable
      after the capture lands, record that as a `-t decision` rather than closing silently.
- [ ] A negative control: force a preflight failure and confirm the operator can name the
      cause from `surface-blocked.json` **alone**, without the journal.

Related: `dotfiles-cxle` (the contract this obeys on the reporting axis and violates on the
diagnostic one — a verdict marker is necessary, not sufficient), `explore-z7eq` (the
unread alarm surfaces that let it sit 2 days), `explore-tkci` (P1 — re-architect the DI
pulses onto the LinearB company seat; this is live evidence for it).

title: SECURITY P0 (escalation): the granola webhook has ZERO auth — a prompt-injection vector into the corpus LinearB agents read as ground truth
description:
Escalates dotfiles-6wdw. Found by the reef/granola design agent, 2026-07-25.

THE FINDING: reef's `authMiddleware` (linearb/reef/polyps/router/src/middleware/
auth.ts, HMAC-SHA256) EXISTS and is wired to EXACTLY ZERO call sites — grep
returns two hits, both inside auth.ts itself. Correct code, never applied.

So today, on http://51.81.33.136:7575/coral/granola/webhook — plain HTTP, raw IP,
world-open in UFW — ANY host on the internet can POST arbitrary JSON and cause
two file writes into ~/linearb/reef/coral/granola/data/.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN THE PIVOT I ORIGINALLY FILED:
That directory is a CORPUS THAT LINEARB CLAUDE AGENTS READ AS GROUND TRUTH
(referenced by .claude/skills/imc/references/di-talk-track.md via a hardcoded
path, and by skills-library/CLAUDE.md). An attacker does not need to breach
anything — they can WRITE INSTRUCTIONS INTO THE CONTEXT of agents doing
confidential client work. This is a prompt-injection vector, not spam.

Secondary: confidential meeting transcripts cross the public internet in
PLAINTEXT on the Zapier -> zig-computer leg. nginx allows 16 MB bodies; the only
brake is an in-memory 100 req/min/IP limit that dies on restart.

No path traversal (timestamp + slugify filenames), so the exposure is content
injection + disk fill, not RCE.

MITIGATION ORDER (Zig has retained :7575 because granola is load-bearing for
LinearB work — do NOT close it before the replacement is live):
 1. FASTEST PARTIAL FIX, available today, hours not days: wire the EXISTING
    authMiddleware to the granola route and add the token to the Zap's header.
    ~15 lines. This does not fix plaintext, but it closes the anonymous-write
    hole, which is the part an attacker can use without any privileged position.
 2. Then the full migration (explore/dotfiles spec, filed separately):
    transcripts.zig.computer over TLS -> a small Go daemon on 127.0.0.1:14390 ->
    ~/linearb/transcripts/. Kills the pico round-trip, adds TLS + constant-time
    token compare, and closes :7575 permanently.

⚠️ DEPENDENCY ON ZIG (blocks step 1): the Zapier action must be
"Webhooks by Zapier -> POST" for a custom Authorization header to be settable.
If the Zap uses a Granola-native integration instead, the header may not be
available and the auth design changes. Resolve by opening the Zap. Same visit:
Granola's trigger likely exposes attendees / meeting time / URL, which the
current payload does NOT carry ({title, transcript, summary?} only) — which is
why every transcript's frontmatter says participants: Me / Them. One edit,
two wins.
notes:
## Verification — 2026-07-26 (Opus-5 audit Wave 1)

Anonymous write is closed on EVERY reachable path. Public cleartext POST to :7575/coral/granola/webhook -> 401. TLS POST to granola.zig.computer -> 401; bare root with no/bogus token -> 404 deny, with lb-granola logging reason=no_token / bad_token / wrong_method. safeCompare() sha256s both sides before ConstantTimeCompare. The bead's 'authMiddleware wired to EXACTLY ZERO call sites' claim was STALE: polyps/router/src/index.ts:91 wires tokenAuthMiddleware to the granola route. The plaintext-transport concern is also resolved — the Zap posts to the TLS vhost, no pico round-trip.

Verified by an independent read-only recon agent against live system state, not
from the bead body. Closing as confirmed-resolved.
close_reason: Verified resolved against live state during Opus-5 audit Wave 1.

title: pulse-ledger-lint: add a duplicate (PT day, row) done-line rule
description:
## Context
pulse-ledger-lint.py checks row-name validity but has NO rule for duplicate done
lines. It reported CLEAN both before and after two genuine duplicate-done groups
were found by hand in the dashboard-dev-interrupted ledger (guest-promo
2026-07-07 and 2026-07-14, where the split newsletter/clips halves each appended
their own done line).

That class matters: caps count done lines, so a duplicate makes a 1/week row read
as 2 fires that week, and it violates the spec's own "one tick, one line, written
last" rule. It is invisible to every existing gate.

The detector is small and already written once as a throwaway: bucket each done
line's ts into the PROJECT timezone (zoneinfo, never a naive `date +%F` on the UTC
stamp — evening ticks mis-bucket forward) and flag any (PT day, row) group with
more than one done.

Important scoping detail learned the hard way: the rule must apply to DONE lines
only. A done + quiet pair on the same day is legitimate — it records two separate
tick fires — and flagging it invites exactly the wrong fix (we briefly collapsed
one and had to restore it).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Ledger with two done lines for the same row on the same PT day
2. python3 ~/dotfiles/agents/scheduler/pulse-ledger-lint.py --project <dir>
3. Reports CLEAN — the duplicate is never surfaced

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Lint flags >1 done per (PT day, row), scoped to done only
- [ ] PT bucketing via zoneinfo, with a regression test for the UTC-evening boundary
- [ ] done+quiet on one day does NOT trip it
- [ ] Runs across every pulse project, not just this one

title: daily-digest writes row:null on every ledger line — 30 invisible ticks
description:
Found 2026-07-26 while wiring the vault-sync alarm into harnessd's manifest.

`/home/ubuntu/explore/refs/digest-ledger.jsonl` has 30 lines and **every single one carries `"row": null`**. harnessd's manifest faithfully mirrors this: the `pulse-daily-digest` loop entry has `"ledger_row": null`.

This is a live instance of the exact defect the 2026-07-25 pass repaired — 23 null rows across 3 ledgers, traced to `pulse/SKILL.md` documenting `"row":null` in its own example (the "documented example IS the defect" class, dotfiles-mlti). That fix repaired the existing rows and the SKILL's example. **This ledger was missed**, and has kept writing nulls since.

WHY IT MATTERS: cap counters and every per-row analytic key on the row name. A null row is an invisible tick — it cannot be counted against a cap, cannot be attributed, and cannot be distinguished from a different loop's line in the same file. The only sanctioned escape hatch is the literal string `"unattributed"`, never null and never a guessed name.

Note this is NOT the same as the pulse ledger: /daily-digest writes its own `digest-ledger.jsonl`, which is likely why the earlier repair pass missed it — it was scoped to `pulse-ledger.jsonl`.

## Steps to Reproduce

    python3 -c "import json,collections;print(collections.Counter(json.loads(l).get('row') for l in open('/home/ubuntu/explore/refs/digest-ledger.jsonl') if l.strip()))"

Returns {None: 30}.

## Acceptance Criteria

- /daily-digest writes a real row name on every ledger line
- the 30 existing null rows are repaired (inferred with evidence, or the literal "unattributed" where genuinely unknowable)
- harnessd's manifest entry for pulse-daily-digest carries the real ledger_row instead of null
- pulse-ledger-lint.py (already promoted to dotfiles/agents/scheduler/) is pointed at digest-ledger.jsonl too, so this ledger is covered by the same guard
- a sweep for any OTHER ledger the original repair missed
notes:
## Fixed — 2026-07-26 (Opus-5 audit Wave 1)

Emitters fixed FIRST, then backfill — 4 sites: explore/.claude/skills/daily-digest/SKILL.md,
explore/bin/friction_ledger.py (new LEDGER_ROW constant), dotfiles recall-distill/SKILL.md,
and a new declarative 'Non-pulse ledger rows' table in explore/refs/pulse.md that makes the
row names CANONICAL (the lint discovers valid row names from any markdown table in that file;
verified pulse-cap.py / pulse-stall.py / ledger_streak.py do NOT parse those tables, so it
cannot make anything fire).

Backfill by textual insertion after ts — every other byte preserved (the three files use
different separator styles), with a per-line JSON round-trip assertion: digest-ledger 30
lines, friction-ledger 1, recall-distill-ledger 2. The last two were tracked by NO bead and
are the real answer to the bead's 'sweep for any OTHER ledger' criterion.

Verified: no ledger under refs/ has a null/empty/missing row; pulse-ledger-lint.py --selftest
passes; pulse-ledger.jsonl and digest-ledger.jsonl both lint CLEAN; pytest bin -q -> 106 passed.

title: bug: pulse-dispatch-remote leaks a tmux window per dispatch (lexicon glyph breaks the name match)
description:
## Context

The remote window lookup matched `#{window_name}` by splitting on whitespace and
comparing `$2`. The tmux-status hook PREFIXES the window name with a lexicon
glyph (🧠/✅/🔔/🌀), so `$2` is the GLYPH, never the row name. Every window that
had ever run a tick failed to match, and each dispatch silently created ANOTHER
window. Zig caught two live `weekly-report` windows on marketing-vps.

pulse-inject.sh had already solved this locally with `strip_lexicon()` and a
comment naming the trap; the remote script's comment claimed "same contract as
pulse-inject.sh" but the code never ported it.

Second defect found while fixing it: `\t` in a tmux `-F` format is NOT expanded
by tmux. pulse-inject.sh only works because bash `$'...'` expands it before
tmux sees it; that does not survive the ssh quoting round-trip, so a tab-
delimited fix emits a literal backslash-t and silently matches nothing.

Fixed: split on the first space (window_id never contains one), treat the
remainder as the name, strip a leading non-alphanumeric run. Generic strip
rather than a fixed glyph list so a new lexicon glyph cannot reintroduce it.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Dispatch any row to marketing-vps; the window is created with a plain name.
2. Let the tick run — the status hook decorates it to "✅ <row>".
3. Dispatch the same row again.
4. `ssh marketing-vps "tmux list-windows -t '=work'"` shows TWO windows for that row.
5. Repeat: one additional window per dispatch, unbounded.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The matcher strips the lexicon glyph before comparing
- [x] No `\t` in the tmux -F format sent over ssh
- [x] Verified against live decorated windows: weekly-report -> @6, di-tuesday -> @5, dotfiles -> @0, vps-di -> @10
- [x] A genuinely absent row still returns empty so the window gets created
- [x] The leaked duplicate window on marketing-vps removed

title: a1111: upcast_attn insufficient for SDXL inpaint on MPS — escalate to --no-half
description:
## Context

Follow-up to dotfiles-43l (closed earlier today). 43l added
`upcast_attn: true` to config.json — the Settings-only toggle that the
NaN error message itself recommended. The fix was applied as documented
(file installed, LaunchAgent kickstarted, A1111 booted clean), but user
re-tested inpaint immediately after and the NaN still fires:

```
NansException: A tensor with NaNs was produced in Unet. ... Try setting
the "Upcast cross attention layer to float32" option in Settings >
Stable Diffusion or using the --no-half commandline argument to fix this.
```

Verified `~/stable-diffusion-webui/config.json` contains
`{"upcast_attn": true}` and the file is at the correct location. The
setting key matches A1111 source (`shared_options.py:182`). Despite all
that, the NaN check still trips on inpainting attempts. Likely cause:
on MPS, SDXL inpainting has additional fp16 underflow paths beyond the
cross-attention layer that the upcast doesn't cover.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. A1111 on pico per rp0 + 43l (config.json has `upcast_attn: true`)
2. Load SDXL base 1.0
3. Open Img2Img → Inpaint
4. Upload image, draw mask, generate (any prompt, default settings)
5. After ~14s, NansException fires

Repeatable: user has seen it on multiple consecutive inpaint attempts
since 43l's fix.

## Fix

Escalate from "upcast just the cross-attention layer" to "--no-half"
(full fp32 throughout the model). The error message lists this as the
alternative recommended remedy. Trade-off: SDXL memory footprint
doubles from ~6.5GB to ~13GB — fine on M1 Max with 64GB RAM.

Changes to `~/dotfiles/a1111/webui-user.sh`:
- Drop `--upcast-sampling` ("no effect with --no-half" per A1111's
  own help text)
- Add `--no-half`
- Keep `--no-half-vae` (was already there; redundant under --no-half
  but harmless)
- Keep `upcast_attn: true` in config.json as belt-and-suspenders;
  technically moot but doesn't hurt

## Regression guard

- Structural: webui-user.sh in dotfiles carries --no-half as part of
  COMMANDLINE_ARGS. Fresh-Mac rebuild (mac.setup.sh) installs the
  current webui-user.sh, so the fix is durable.
- Documentation: long-form comment in webui-user.sh explains WHY
  --no-half over --upcast-sampling (because the lighter path tested
  insufficient for SDXL inpaint on MPS in this real-world test).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] webui-user.sh updated with --no-half
- [x] Pico's live webui-user.sh synced
- [x] LaunchAgent kickstarted, A1111 boots clean with new flag
- [ ] User re-tests inpaint, confirms NaN no longer fires
- [ ] Performance impact (memory + iteration speed) acceptable
notes:
## CLOSED 2026-05-24 — verified by user

User retested SDXL inpaint after --no-half landed; inpaint works, no
NaN. Performance impact deemed acceptable in the field (no complaint
on speed/memory; M1 Max 64GB carries the doubled SDXL footprint
without strain).

title: decision: upgrade default opus alias 4.8[1m] → opus-5[1m] (all pulse loops + interactive)
description:
Context: Zig asked "upgrade all system pulses to opus 5" (2026-07-25). The explore vibe-explore tick #117 (and every pulse loop) had been running claude-opus-4-8[1m]. Investigation: pulse sessions launch bare `claude` (pulse-inject LAUNCH="claude"; the claude identity-wrapper function adds no --model), so they inherit CC's default opus alias. That alias is pinned by ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL, set from CC_GW_MODEL in ~/dotfiles/bash/.bash_aliases and injected into ~/.claude/settings.json .env by cc-gw (see dotfiles-w1r for why the pin exists: it survives resume behind the pico gateway, which disables CC's auto-1M-upgrade; [1m] is a beta header, not a distinct model).

Decision: changed CC_GW_MODEL "claude-opus-4-8[1m]" → "claude-opus-5[1m]" AND updated the live ~/.claude/settings.json .env.ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL to match. Preserved the [1m] (1M-context) suffix rather than dropping to plain opus-5 (200K), to keep the current context posture. Verified claude-opus-5[1m] resolves + is served through the gateway (headless -p PONG, exit 0).

Why: it's the single lever for the opus-alias default that ALL bare-`claude` launches inherit — there is no per-pulse model config to flip; pulses and interactive sessions share this default. Preserving [1m] avoids a silent context downgrade. Only changes the `opus` ALIAS, so explicit /model and --model picks still win (same property dotfiles-w1r relied on).

Scope note: this upgrades the opus default for EVERYTHING that doesn't explicitly pick a model — pulses AND Zig's interactive sessions — because that's the only lever. Judged in-scope with intent (opus-5 is strictly the better default). 

Reversibility: trivial. `cc-direct` scrubs the pin; or edit CC_GW_MODEL / settings.json .env back to 4-8[1m] (backup at ~/.claude/settings.json.bak-opus5-*). One-line revert.

Effect timing: env is read at CC launch, so this takes effect on the NEXT launch of each session. Currently-live durable pulse windows (explore, elevate, daily-digest) keep 4.8[1m] until restarted or switched via /model claude-opus-5[1m]. Left the live-window switch as a follow-up for Zig (restarting warm sessions, incl. his interactive one, is his call).

## Problem
Daily autonovel Phase 1 cron (`f63079296927`, runs 09:00 UTC) has been failing since Wave 18:

    Last run:  2026-05-28T09:00:22.509161+00:00  error: Script exited with code 2

Phase 1 (the supposedly-working autonovel pipeline per handoff) hasn't actually run since at least the Wave 18 SSoT cleanup. Each invocation exits 2 immediately.

Wave 18 deleted duplicate profile-local skill dirs from `~/.hermes/skills/` to fix the Hermes `--skills` ambiguous-paths resolver bug. The autonovel-phase1-smoke SKILL was canonized into `external_dirs` (lives at `~/explore/autonovel/hermes-skills/autonovel-phase1-smoke/runner.py`).

Update `~/explore/autonovel/cron/run-autonovel.sh` (or wherever the runner-path is hardcoded) to point at `~/explore/autonovel/hermes-skills/autonovel-phase1-smoke/runner.py` directly. SSoT model: external_dirs is canonical.

title: offboard: the decision harvest drops decisions RESOLVED this session but created earlier
description:
## Context
Found 2026-08-02 running /offboard in ~/coding-jams/ifcomp/2026. The harvest
reported 4 decision beads. Three more — ifcompd-xku (authoring system),
ifcompd-x7s (collaboration model), ifcompd-fmr (repo visibility) — were the
session's MOST consequential decisions, each recorded with full reasoning and
closed during the session. All three were invisible to the harvest.

Cause: Step 2.5 filters on `created_at >= SINCE_EPOCH`. Those beads were created
by a prior session and only RESOLVED in this one.

This is `explore-7ogz` one layer over. That fix added `-a` so a decision created
AND closed inside the session is visible. It did not cover a decision created
BEFORE the session and closed inside it — which is arguably the more common shape,
because a decision bead usually outlives the session that files it. Same silent
failure: the harvest just prints fewer lines, which reads like "fewer decisions".

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Session A: `br create -t decision "..."`. End session.
2. Session B: `br close <id> -r "..."`. Run /offboard.
3. The harvest omits it. The handoff records the session's biggest call as absent.

## Fix options
- Filter on `updated_at`/`closed_at >= SINCE_EPOCH` **in addition to** created_at
  (a decision touched this session is a decision of this session).
- Or emit two groups: "filed this session" and "resolved this session".
  Probably better — they are different things and the handoff reader wants both.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A decision created in a prior session and closed in this one appears in the harvest
- [ ] The receipt line counts both groups, so a zero is still distinguishable from a failed query
- [ ] /offboard SKILL.md Step 2.5 updated

title: spec: /pulse — generic per-project heartbeat (extract autonovel /heartbeat; pilot: weekly-reporting)
description:
## 1. Overview  (REVISED 2026-06-09 post-/check — decisions in --notes)

/pulse is a global skill that turns any beads-disciplined project into a self-driving loop: a scheduled tick lands in a DURABLE interactive Claude session -> cheap onboard -> route -> at most ONE unit of work with full discipline -> offboard -> done until the next tick. It generalizes autonovel's /heartbeat (routing table, one-dispatch-per-tick, rate caps, anti-entropy — spec bd-49j) into a project-agnostic skill. It is the Claude-native realization of what Hermes promised (durable, autonomous, learning over time); /heartbeat is the parent and is SUPERSEDED by /pulse after the pilot (autonovel migrates onto a thin routing table; learnings fold back at migration).

## 2. Baseline

- autonovel /heartbeat: proven loop (<=1h tick, routing table, one dispatch/tick, caps).
- weekly-reporting: 4 editorial jobs on systemd user timers driving the Agent SDK — outside the bead/handoff brain. Hermes uninstalled 2026-06-06.
- /onboard//offboard cheap (TOOLKIT ~3k tokens); refs/session-handoff.md + .offboard-pending give continuity; bv --robot-next picks work deterministically; tmux lexicon (🧠/✅/🔔) + AskUserQuestion convention give visibility.
- Ruled out: cloud /schedule (no local harness); claude -p headless (draws from the separate monthly Agent SDK credit pool per docs effective 2026-06-15, and is unwatchable/unsteerable); raw /loop as durability layer (~1-week expiry).

## 3. Changes  (architecture per OQ-1/OQ-3 decisions)

a) SCHEDULER (shipped, wave 1 dotfiles-x1q): agents/scheduler/pulse-inject.sh — systemd user timer fires the injector; it ensures the tmux session exists (detached creation survives reboot), finds/creates the dedicated scheduler window (lexicon-aware matching) anchored in the project dir, ensures an INTERACTIVE claude session is running (launch + bounded poll), and send-keys the tick command. Per-project unit templates in agents/scheduler/templates/. The session is durable across ticks; Andrew can watch/steer it any time; usage is normal subscription.
b) /pulse SKILL (wave 2): per-project opt-in via refs/pulse.md routing table — rows {trigger, condition-check, action, cap, priority}; tick procedure = Step 0 honor .offboard-pending -> cheap onboard -> evaluate rows top-down -> fire AT MOST ONE (worktree subagents + scrutinize as normal) -> close/commit/push -> offboard (writes handoff; session persists) -> end tick. Quiet tick = log + end.
c) Blocked-on-Andrew protocol: never block on AskUserQuestion in a tick — file P1 'human:' bead + push notification, end tick.
d) COMPACT-AWARENESS (wave 4, per OQ-3): (i) Stop-hook context guard — parse session JSONL latest usage (input + cache_read + cache_creation ~= context), above ~85% exit 2 with 'run /offboard now'; an exit-2 Stop makes the session offboard itself. (ii) PreCompact(auto) backstop — block once with 'offboard first' (marker prevents loops), then allow. Both need empirical verification on 2.1.170 first.
e) /offboard: no successor-booking step needed in the timer model — the recurring timer IS the successor; offboard just leaves clean state for the next tick.

## 4. Formal spec (sketch — refine at wave 2 impl)

- Routing row schema: {name, trigger (time|state|queue), check (bash, exit 0 = fire), action (skill invocation or bv --robot-next), cap (per day/week), priority}. First satisfied row wins; caps enforced via a per-project tick ledger (refs/pulse-ledger.jsonl or bead notes).
- Invariants: one dispatch per tick; all work -> beads + commits + push (always-push); handoff note per working tick; quiet ticks logged not committed.
- Window contract: one dedicated 'pulse' window per tmux session (work session row); the lexicon hook labels it like any other window.

## 5. Test cases (>=10 at /test time)

1. Quiet tick: no row fires -> log only, session intact. 2. Time-trigger cap: fires once despite two ticks in window. 3. Queue trigger takes bv --robot-next top. 4. Dispatch failure -> human: P1 bead + push, tick ends cleanly. 5. .offboard-pending honored first. 6. Two satisfied rows -> higher priority only. 7. Cap exhausted -> next row evaluated. 8. Injector cold-start after reboot (no tmux server) -> tick still lands. 9. Handoff written per working tick. 10. Non-opted-in project -> /pulse refuses with setup guidance. (Injector-level cases 1-7 of wave 1 already pass.)

## 6. Open Questions — ALL RESOLVED 2026-06-09 (decisions + readiness in --notes)

OQ-1 tmux-injection (decided) · OQ-2 weekly-reporting pilot (decided) · OQ-3 compact-awareness design (decided, empirical verification in its impl bead) · OQ-4 digest (deferred by design) · OQ-5 heartbeat superseded after pilot (decided) · location: global paragon set (decided).

## 7. Future

- Morning digest (OQ-4): aggregate human: beads / stale in_progress / markers / 🔔 states across projects; landing spot TBD (Asana vs local+push vs Slack agents). After pilot.
- Fleet control-tower window; per-project lessons bead (the Hermes durable-memory benefit); Slack-agent 🔔 mirroring.
- Hermes carry-forward: when the local-model arc resumes (pico primed), retry Hermes clean-slate and map this contract onto it (see --notes + auto-memory).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Wave 1 scheduler shipped with tests (DONE — dotfiles-x1q, 7/7)
- /pulse SKILL.md ships in dotfiles + TOOLKIT entry
- weekly-reporting pilot: >=1 editorial job runs end-to-end on a pulse tick (bead + commit + push + handoff, no Andrew prompt)
- Tick lands after a reboot (timer Persistent=true + injector cold-start)
- Blocked work surfaces as human: P1 bead + push, never an interactive wait
- Compact-awareness verified empirically before its hook ships
notes:
## Decision: OQ-1 (successor-booking primitive) — DECIDED 2026-06-09 (Andrew)

**Decision:** tmux-injection scheduler. NOT claude -p headless.
**Rationale:** (a) headless -p pulls from the monthly use-it-or-lose-it consumption credits rather than normal interactive subscription usage (Andrew's understanding; flag if docs say otherwise — see OQ-3 research item 4); (b) headless is invisible — Andrew can't watch thinking, steer, or give feedback mid-run. An interactive session in tmux is visible to him AND the agent, persistent, steerable, uses the normal subscription, and inherits the 🧠/✅/🔔 lexicon.
**Architecture:** systemd user timer -> injector script -> (1) ensure a DEDICATED window exists in the work session's labeled row (the scheduler window); (2) ensure an interactive claude session is running there in a scaffolded harness folder; (3) tmux send-keys the kick-off command (e.g. '/pulse tick' or the project-specific flow). The window/session is durable; ticks are injected prompts, not new processes.
**Bake-in:** global — injector script + timer templates live in dotfiles (proposed: dotfiles/agents/scheduler/), rigid and deterministic.
**Spec impact:** Sections 3-4 — successor booking becomes 'recurring timer + injector targets the durable window'; per-tick offboard still writes the handoff but the SESSION persists between ticks. Re-dispatch /spec to fold in.

## Decision: OQ-2 (pilot scope) — DECIDED 2026-06-09 (Andrew)

**Decision:** weekly-reporting is the pilot — it already has systemd timers + recurring editorial jobs, and the weeklies tab IS this problem. First migration: the weekly-report skill flow Andrew currently runs by hand. Exact job order picked at impl time from weekly-reporting's four-job list.
**Explicitly NOT the starting point:** research arcs (Andrew is on a break from model/pico/local-coding/LSRA work).

## OQ-3 (compact-awareness) — RESEARCH IN FLIGHT 2026-06-09

guide-agent dispatched: hook-payload visibility of context-window %, PreCompact semantics (timing, blockability), 'context low' signals, AND the claude -p billing question from OQ-1. Decision block appended when it returns.

## Decision: OQ-4 (morning digest) — DEFERRED 2026-06-09 (Andrew)

Later, after pulse proves the per-project loop. Aggregation inputs + landing spot stay open. 'We're getting to this... come back to later once we get more of this implemented.'

## Decision: OQ-5 (autonovel fold-in) — DECIDED 2026-06-09

autonovel keeps its specialized /heartbeat untouched until /pulse is stable through the weekly-reporting pilot; then evaluate folding. Don't break the running agent.

## Decision (new OQ): skill location — DECIDED 2026-06-09

**Decision:** /pulse is a GLOBAL paragon skill (dotfiles/agents/skills/pulse/), alongside the scheduler scaffolding in dotfiles.
**Rationale:** it's machine-wide harness infrastructure like /onboard and /orchestrator — the pilot lives in ~/linearb, the pattern's parent lives in ~/explore/autonovel, and Andrew wants it 'baked in on a global level / across the whole machine.' The toybox 3-project graduation rule is for capability skills, not harness infrastructure.

## Context carry-forward: Hermes

Hermes uninstalled 2026-06-06 (mis-setup, obtuse, no benefit; clean-slate retry intended). No local model currently primed and API-key Claude too expensive, so Hermes is parked. WHEN the local-model arc resumes (pico primed), retry Hermes and map /pulse's contract (routing table, one-dispatch-per-tick, human: bead protocol, injection scheduler) onto it instead of starting over. Also recorded in auto-memory (project_hermes_revisit.md).

## Implementation Readiness — 2026-06-09

**P1 OQs decided:** 2/2 (OQ-1, OQ-2)
**P2:** OQ-3 research in flight (blocks ONLY the compact-awareness feature, not the skill skeleton); OQ-4 deferred by design
**P3:** OQ-5 decided
**New decisions:** skill location (global)

### Recommended impl order
1. Scheduler scaffolding: injector script + dedicated-window convention + timer template (dotfiles)
2. /pulse SKILL.md: routing-table contract + tick procedure + human:-bead protocol (+ TOOLKIT entry)
3. weekly-reporting pilot: first job as a pulse row + its timer
4. Compact-awareness: after OQ-3 research lands
Spec revision needed first: fold OQ-1 architecture into Sections 3-4 (re-dispatch /spec).
## Decision: OQ-3 (compact-awareness) — DECIDED 2026-06-09 (research-backed)

**Findings (guide agent, official docs, 2026-06-09):** Hooks do NOT receive context-window % — only the statusline command gets context_window.used_percentage. PreCompact fires before BOTH auto and manual compaction; its payload carries transcript_path but no token counts; it CAN block via decision:"block" / exit 2 (delays compaction). No documented auto-compact threshold, env var, or context-low signal. The session transcript JSONL on disk carries per-turn usage fields. Docs: code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md, hooks-guide.md, how-claude-code-works.md.

**Design (both mechanisms need empirical verification on 2.1.170):**
- (a) PRIMARY — Stop-hook context guard: on Stop, parse the session JSONL (latest assistant entry's input_tokens + cache_read + cache_creation ≈ current context), compute %, and above ~85% exit 2 with 'context nearing auto-compaction — run /offboard now, then continue or /compact deliberately.' An exit-2 Stop keeps the agent working WITH that instruction — the session offboards itself, which is exactly Andrew's ideal.
- (b) BACKSTOP — PreCompact(auto) blocks ONCE with reason 'offboard first' (marker file prevents a block loop), then allows.

**Bonus finding for OQ-1:** docs CONFIRM the billing premise — 'Starting June 15, 2026, Agent SDK and claude -p usage on subscription plans will draw from a new monthly Agent SDK credit, separate from your interactive usage limits' (code.claude.com/docs/en/headless.md). The tmux-injection decision stands on documented ground. tmux send-keys itself is undocumented-but-generic; the injector should use claude --continue/--resume for session resumption in the dedicated window.

## Readiness amendment — 2026-06-09 (post OQ-3 research)

ALL OQs now decided or deliberately deferred: OQ-1 ✓ OQ-2 ✓ OQ-3 ✓ (research-backed design, empirical verification folded into its impl bead) OQ-4 deferred-by-design OQ-5 ✓ + location ✓. Spec revision (fold OQ-1+OQ-3 into Sections 3-4) is the next dispatch, then /test + /impl per the recommended order.
## Amendment: OQ-5 sharpened — 2026-06-09 (Andrew)

Direction confirmed: /heartbeat is the PARENT (pulse is extracted from it); the timing rule is the only reason it stays untouched during the pilot. End state: once /pulse is stable through the weekly-reporting pilot, autonovel MIGRATES onto /pulse with a thin autonovel-specific routing table (mail/daily/write/learn rows), pilot learnings fold in during that migration, and /heartbeat as a separate skill RETIRES. Not "evaluate folding" — superseded after pilot.

## Wave 4 SHIPPED — 2026-06-10 (dotfiles-lb6)

Design UPGRADE over §3d: the statusline (not hooks) receives the OFFICIAL context_window.used_percentage — verified live on 2.1.170 (payload also carries session_id, context_window_size, current_usage; the latter validates the JSONL-estimation formula ≈134k ✓ but estimation is now unnecessary).

- statusline.sh persists pct → /tmp/claude-context-pct/<session_id> per render.
- stop-context-guard.sh (Stop): pct ≥85% (CONTEXT_GUARD_PCT) → exit 2 'run /offboard NOW'. Fires once per session (marker); stop_hook_active loop-protected; released by a FRESH (<30 min, CONTEXT_GUARD_OFFBOARD_FRESH_SECS) last-offboard-session match — staleness check added after live testing caught yesterday's offboard silencing today's guard.
- pre-compact-observe.sh (PreCompact): OBSERVE MODE — logs trigger + would-block to /tmp/claude-compact-observe.log, never blocks. title: /commit tells you to rebase; AGENTS.md says never rebase — and the reflex chain from rebase's refusal is the DESTRUCTIVE verb
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. `grep -n rebase agents/skills/commit/SKILL.md` -> L15 "**Always pull --rebase,
   THEN push** after committing -- unless you're in a worktree"; L96 `git pull
   --rebase origin "$BRANCH"   # ALWAYS. Never push blind.`; L128 defends the choice.
2. `grep -n 'rebase' agents/AGENTS.md` -> L226 "## Two writers, one working tree —
   merge, never rebase, NEVER stash"; L248 "**`git fetch origin && git merge
   --no-edit origin/main`** — NOT `git pull --rebase`."

Both are in the loaded tier. AGENTS.md is always-loaded fleet-wide; /commit's body
loads on invoke, and TOOLKIT.md's /commit entry propagates the REBASE version into
every single /onboard ("**`git pull --rebase` THEN push**").

## Why this is a hazard, not just an inconsistency
AGENTS.md's own measured table (2026-08-01) is:
  git pull --no-rebase -> fails SAFELY
  git pull --rebase    -> fails OBSTRUCTIVELY (rc 128 on ANY unrelated dirty file)
  git stash            -> "succeeds", DESTRUCTIVELY (silently takes the other writer's work)
and it names the trap explicitly: "rebase's refusal is exactly what tempts you
toward it [stash]". So /commit's instruction does not merely disagree -- it routes
the agent onto the rung whose failure mode reflexively suggests the destructive
verb. pre-shared-tree-guard.sh only covers the window where another writer is
PROVABLY mid-run; outside it the verbs are the agent's.

Found in the dotfiles-w8xw audit (audit A). Verified independently by the
orchestrator before filing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Zig decides which rule is canonical (they were written for different
      situations -- multi-machine push races vs a second writer in ONE tree -- so
      the fix may be to scope each, not to delete one)
- [ ] The surviving rule stated in exactly ONE place; the other file points at it
- [ ] TOOLKIT.md's /commit entry updated to match
- [ ] A doclint/hook check so the two cannot silently diverge again

title: finding (CLASS): 'the documented example IS the defect' — 4 confirmed instances, one shared fix
description:
Four independent audits on 2026-07-25 each found an instance of the SAME failure
mode, none aware of the others. In a prompt-driven harness, agents copy examples
verbatim. So a wrong example is not a typo — it is a defect that replicates
itself across every project, silently, forever.

THE FOUR CONFIRMED INSTANCES:

1. agents/skills/pulse/SKILL.md ~L51 — documents the ledger row as
   {"ts":"…","row":null,"outcome":"quiet",…}. Ticks copied it -> 23 rows across
   THREE ledgers (explore 19, di 1, weekly-reporting 3) with row=null, invisible
   to pulse-cap.py and every per-row analytic. Explore's 19 are repaired
   (explore-qdo5); the SKILL fix is in flight.

2. agents/AGENTS.md:281 — the canonical worktree-cleanup snippet is
   `git push origin --delete worktree-agent-XXXX 2>/dev/null || true`. That
   VIOLATES the same file's own rule at :140-154 AND is blocked by the live
   pre-bash-stderr-guard.sh hook. Every orchestrator copying the documented
   cleanup block hits a hook denial. (The auditor was itself blocked by this
   hook mid-audit, for this pattern. So was the orchestrator, later, in the
   same session.)

3. explore/.claude/practices.md ~L89 — MANDATES the cross-link form
   `[name](name/FINDINGS.md)`, which is a BROKEN hyperlink from inside an
   exploration's own folder. The working form is `../name/FINDINGS.md`.
   Compounding harm: gen-index.py's link regex only matched the BROKEN form, so
   authors who wrote a working link had it silently dropped from the graph.
   Result: LINKMAP reported 69 edges / 85 unconnected when the truth is ~384 /
   ~23. The compendium's knowledge graph has been ~18% VISIBLE.

4. vacation-station-14/CLAUDE.md:194 — a copy-me commit template hardcoding
   `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6`. Agents paste a false model attribution
   into real commit history.

WHY THIS CLASS IS SPECIAL (and worth its own guard):
 - It is INVISIBLE to code review — every file is individually well-formed.
 - It is invisible to tests — nothing tests documentation.
 - It SCALES with adoption: the better the docs are followed, the more damage.
 - It survives fixes downstream: repairing 19 ledger rows does not stop the
   next project reproducing them. Only fixing the example does.
 - Three of the four were found only because four separate auditors happened to
   read four different files on the same day. Nothing systematic would catch it.

THE SHARED FIX (proposed by the config auditor; endorsed):
Add a /housekeeping pass that EXTRACTS every fenced code block and inline
command from SKILL.md files, CLAUDE.md files, and AGENTS.md, and LINTS them:
 - shell blocks -> shellcheck, plus a DRY-RUN against the live PreToolUse hooks
   (the hooks are the ground truth for what is permitted; instance 2 would have
   been caught instantly by running the documented command past the guard that
   blocks it)
 - JSON/JSONL examples -> validate against the schema the consumer actually
   parses (instance 1)
 - markdown links in docs that mandate a link FORM -> resolve them (instance 3)
 - grep for hardcoded model ids / dates / versions in copy-me templates
   (instance 4)
This is the mechanical guard for a class the harness has been fixing one
instance at a time, by luck.

Relates: explore-qdo5 (instance 1 repair), dotfiles-b9ii (epic),
dotfiles-uxj9 (cost), explore-1fd8. Zig's standing preference (memory:
editorial-vs-mechanical-enforcement): hooks for checkable invariants. This is
a checkable invariant.
notes:
## Fixed — 2026-07-26 (Opus-5 audit Wave 1)

The four instances needed nothing. The real gap was that the doclint guard was BUILT and wired into nothing — a linter nobody ran.
Now wired into housekeeping/SKILL.md:481-528 (§9.10) plus an exit-tally item: standing, NON-BLOCKING, output framed as a work queue, baseline recorded. The blocking decision is written into the skill prose with the LATENCY argument named as load-bearing (>2 min, because it replays every documented shell statement against four live hooks) — independent of the error count, so it stays correct as the count goes to zero.
close_reason: Fixed and pushed in Wave 1 of the Opus-5 audit.

title: pulse-inject: cold-boot injects before the launched TUI is input-ready → keystrokes eaten (ha-portal submit launched claude but /ha-serve was lost; button press into the warm session worked)
description:
ROOT CAUSE: the cold-boot branch waited for pane_current_command==LAUNCH_BASE (LIVENESS — the process exists) then slept a fixed 3s and injected. Claude Code's process name flips within ~1-4s of exec, but the interactive TUI (heavy project: big CLAUDE.md + MCP + skills + hooks) is not READY for composer input for much longer. send-keys 3s after detection landed in the still-initializing TUI and was SILENTLY dropped.

EVIDENCE (/tmp/pulse-inject.log): 2026-07-08T20:01:06 ha-portal nudge cold-booted window 'ha' (@285): launched claude 20:01:07, injected /ha-serve 20:01:14 (only 7s = ~3s after process detection) — EATEN. Later warm nudges 21:36:40 / 21:42:51 injected 0-1s into the already-running session — worked. Every systemd-timer pulse in the log ('injected into @168/@18', no 'launched claude' line) hits a long-lived WARM session, so /pulse + /daily-digest almost never take the cold branch — which is why the weekly report never showed this. The on-demand ha-portal button has no next-tick retry, so it exposes the race.

FIX (agents/scheduler/pulse-inject.sh): after the liveness poll, poll capture-pane for an input-READY marker (Claude Code composer footer: 'shift+tab to cycle' / '? for shortcuts' / 'for agents' / 'bypass permissions' / 'accept edits on' / 'plan mode on') before injecting, bounded by PULSE_READY_TIMEOUT (default 60s, first-match returns early), then a 2s settle. On timeout, inject anyway (old behavior) so a marker miss degrades to 'try late' not 'never'. PULSE_READY_MARKER overridable; empty disables the gate (non-TUI launches). Verified the default regex matches real ready panes @285/@168/@18.

REGRESSION TEST (test-pulse-inject.sh case 8): slow-TUI launch that prints the marker only after a 4s delay; asserts the cmd lands AND elapsed>=3s (the injector waited for readiness rather than injecting blind). 15/15 pass.

Sibling of dotfiles-q18 (send-keys eaten by a tmux modal). RESIDUAL (not fixed here, noted): stacked warm nudges into a busy session queue multiple /ha-serve commands; and the daemon nudge has no post-inject verify/retry — the readiness gate makes eating unlikely, and maxWorking(480s) still un-wedges the button.
notes: CORRECTION (post-close, Zig): the 'timer pulses reuse a warm long-lived session' claim was WRONG. pulse-inject.log proves weekly-report (pulse-weekly-report.*, same injector) cold-boots a fresh window + fresh claude EVERY week: created window weekly-report @253 (06-30) +4s inject, @279 (07-07) +5s inject — both landed after ready. ha cold-boots: @257 +5s, @276 +6s, @285 +7s (07-08, EATEN). Real root cause = an UNGUARDED timing race (fixed post-detection sleep vs actual composer readiness), variance-driven by boot load + session weight (ha under ~/explore = ~59KB CLAUDE.md vs ~42KB) + attachment (ha=zig-computer ATTACHED 157x71, work=DETACHED). The failing boot waited LONGER (+7s) than the winners (+4/+5s), so sleep length was never the lever — readiness-at-inject-time is. Fix (readiness-marker gate) is unchanged and correct; only the rationale is corrected here + in the code comment.

title: pulse-inject: PULSE_READY_TIMEOUT=60 is thin enough to EAT a tick on a cold boot
description:
Found 2026-07-25 while building --fresh (dotfiles-6ycc), on a disposable rig.

During a cold boot, `claude` took ~60s to paint its composer — right at PULSE_READY_TIMEOUT=60. The readiness gate timed out, logged "WARN: input-ready marker not seen after 60s — injecting anyway", injected into an empty composer, and the tick was EATEN: 0% context, no work, no ledger row.

This is a concrete mechanism for the "fired but no ledger row" class — the same signature the stale-loop detector (harnessd-h14z) alerts on and the same class as the two explore ticks that vanished over 16 days. It is a silent loss: the injector logs a WARN and proceeds, so nothing downstream knows the tick died.

Caveat on severity, stated honestly: this was a FIRST-RUN-IN-A-NEW-PROJECT boot, which is the slowest possible case. No production regression is claimed. But historical measurements suggested +4-7s of headroom, and the real observation was ~60s — the margin is far thinner than assumed.

Note this interacts with --fresh: a /clear'd session re-paints, so readiness timing on a --fresh loop deserves its own measurement rather than inheriting the warm-path assumption.

Also recorded from the same pass (lower priority, no fix proposed): five same-second timer collisions exist — pulse-explore x pulse-di-digest (Wed 13:00), x pulse-di-thursday (Thu 13:00), x pulse-di-friday (Fri 19:00), pulse-daily-digest x pulse-di-tuesday (Tue 14:00), x pulse-di-wednesday (Wed 14:00). No timer sets RandomizedDelaySec. Staggering would NOT fully close this because pulse-retry.timer fires every 2 min and can start a loop service at any moment; the pid tag shipped in dotfiles-0lm3 is what actually solves the attribution harm.

## Steps to Reproduce

Cold-boot a claude session in a project it has never run in, and inject a tick against a 60s readiness timeout. The composer is not ready, the gate warns and injects anyway, and the tick produces nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- an injection that times out on the readiness gate does NOT inject blind — it either retries with backoff or records an explicit blocked/lost outcome in the ledger
- a tick that produces no work is distinguishable in the ledger from one that never fired
- PULSE_READY_TIMEOUT is measured against real cold-boot and post-/clear repaint times, and set from that measurement rather than assumption
notes:
## Fixed — 2026-07-26 (Opus-5 audit Wave 1)

pulse-inject.sh:139-158 (shared record_bounce), :250-320 (the gate), :352-358. Timeout now bounces with reason:"not_ready" and exits 0 instead of silently eating the tick; PULSE_READY_ON_TIMEOUT=inject is the escape hatch. The poll now runs to a WALL-CLOCK deadline — the old seq+sleep 1 overshot (the incident logged 'after 60s' a measured 63s later). Success path logs observed elapsed seconds. +7 tests.
AC3 NOT MET, deliberately and honestly: 'measured against real cold-boot times' needs real Claude Code sessions, which the agent was forbidden to start (see the pulse-measure incident). It mined /tmp/pulse-inject.log instead — only 3 gated cold boots exist since the gate shipped (two at +2s, one timing out at 60s); the other 23 predate the gate. So 60->90 is derived from CONSTRAINTS, not data: past the one observed failure, inside the 120s TimeoutStartSec on pulse-retry.service. The new elapsed-seconds log line is what actually closes this criterion over time.
close_reason: Fixed and pushed in Wave 1 of the Opus-5 audit.

title: vps-preflight: reports 'HISTORIES DIVERGED' and recommends reset --hard for a repo that is merely BEHIND
description:
## Context

Hit TWICE on 2026-07-29, an hour apart, on `~/linearb`. Both times the repo was
strictly behind origin/main with zero local commits, and both times the preflight
called it a divergence and recommended a destructive remedy.

The message:

    $HOME/linearb: local HEAD 7710c543 is NOT the published tip d4ba7d28 — ...
    Remedy: HISTORIES DIVERGED (an upstream rebase does this). If the published
    tip is authoritative: git -C /home/ubuntu/linearb fetch origin &&
    git -C /home/ubuntu/linearb reset --hard origin/main — this DISCARDS local
    commits, so check 'git log origin/main..HEAD' first

The measured reality both times:

    $ git rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...origin/main
    0   1                     # 0 ahead, 1 behind
    $ git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main; echo $?
    0                         # HEAD IS an ancestor -> plain fast-forward
    $ git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD
    (empty)                   # no local commits exist to discard

Correct remedy in both cases was `git pull --ff-only`, which succeeded instantly.

## Why this matters more than a wording nit

1. `reset --hard` is the one remedy that can LOSE work, and it is being
   recommended for the case where it is never needed. The hedge ("check
   `git log origin/main..HEAD` first") puts the burden on a reader who has
   already been told, authoritatively, that histories diverged.
2. A subagent acting on this message today reported to the orchestrator that
   `~/linearb` histories had diverged and that resolving it was a judgment call
   about which side was authoritative. That was wrong, and it was wrong because
   the tool said so. The cost of a misleading diagnosis is that it propagates.
3. This repo goes stale CONSTANTLY now — marketing-vps commits to it too, so
   `~/linearb` falls behind between dispatches as a matter of course. That makes
   this the single most-seen preflight failure, i.e. the worst one to have
   phrased wrong.

Same defect class as dotfiles-rox7 (pulse-stall-reconcile asserting an injection
that never happened): a backstop that fires correctly but describes the cause
wrongly, spending the reader's attention in the wrong direction.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a repo the preflight checks, ensure zero local commits and let origin/main
   advance by one commit (or `git reset --hard HEAD~1`).
2. Run `agents/scheduler/vps-preflight.sh --no-refresh`.
3. Observed: "HISTORIES DIVERGED", remedy is `reset --hard`.
   Expected: "BEHIND by N commits", remedy is `git pull --ff-only`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The check distinguishes the three states and names the one it found:
      BEHIND (`merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main`) — remedy
      `git pull --ff-only`, explicitly noted as non-destructive;
      AHEAD (`--is-ancestor origin/main HEAD`) — remedy `git push`, which is the
      genuine "your work is not published" case this assertion exists for;
      DIVERGED (neither) — only here is `reset --hard` mentioned, with its
      warning intact.
- [ ] The commit counts appear in the message (`N ahead, M behind`), so the
      reader can sanity-check the verdict without re-deriving it.
- [ ] `reset --hard` NEVER appears in the BEHIND or AHEAD messages.
- [ ] Tests for all three states.
- [ ] EVIDENCE: paste the three messages produced by three constructed repos.

## Possible follow-on, do NOT do here

Given `~/linearb` now falls behind as normal fleet behavior, consider whether the
dispatcher should `pull --ff-only` the checked repos itself before asserting
(strictly-behind only, never on ahead/diverged). That is a behavior change with
its own risks — file separately if it looks right.
notes: SUPERSEDED and RESOLVED by dotfiles-w16i (2026-07-31). Root cause found and it was deeper than wording: check_local called 'merge-base --is-ancestor' WITHOUT fetching first, so for exactly the commits this machine was behind by, the published tip was not a local object. Both ancestry arms errored, and the code fell through to the else branch that prints 'HISTORIES DIVERGED' and recommends reset --hard. Reproduced in a throwaway repo 2026-07-31: 'fatal: Not a valid commit name <tip>' before fetch, correct BEHIND classification after. That is why every hand-check contradicted the tool - the hand-checks ran git fetch first. Four false firings (7/30 di-wednesday x2, di-thursday, 7/31 di-friday). Now four-state (BEHIND auto-ff / AHEAD / DIVERGED / UNKNOWN) with reset --hard at exactly one executable site.
