title: human: the close gate has NO escape hatch while every sibling gate does — and it now blocks 250 real beads
description:
NEEDS ZIG. Surfaced 2026-07-26 by the agent that finished the lifecycle gates, and
it is the sharpest asymmetry in the new setup.

THE ASYMMETRY:
  scrutiny gate (impl beads)      -> has an OVERRIDE escape hatch
  NEW create gate (br create)     -> has '# allow-thin-bead'
  lint gate on br close           -> has NOTHING

So the gate we just BUILT ships with a documented valve, and the gate that now
blocks 250 real beads does not. That ordering is backwards.

THE SCALE, re-measured read-only fleet-wide (counts only for ~/linearb and ~/cfp):
  250 of 469 open beads (53%) fail br lint and cannot close until rewritten
  by priority : P0 2 · P1 26 · P2 155 · P3 67
  by type     : task 202 · bug 26 · epic 18 · feature 4
  missing     : 250 x '## Acceptance Criteria' · 26 x '## Steps to Reproduce'
                21 x '## Success Criteria'
  worst hit   : explore 118/149 (79%) · andrewzigler3 35/37 (94%)
                harnessd 42/59 (71%) · dotfiles 17/24 (70%)

THREE THINGS THAT MAKE IT WORSE THAN THE HEADLINE:
 1. No escape hatch, as above.
 2. **22 have a COMPLETELY EMPTY description** — closing one means authoring the
    whole bead (context, task, criteria) for work you are closing, not doing.
 3. **13 self-declare as superseded / obsolete / moot / already shipped** (10 P2,
    3 P3). These are the absurd ones: you must write acceptance criteria for work
    that will never happen, purely to be allowed to say it never will.

THE MITIGATION IS REAL, and smaller than it looks: the remedy is ONE command, not
two — `br update X --description "…## Acceptance Criteria…" && br close X` passes
the gate in a single call (verified rc=0), and `br update` alone is not gated at
all. So the cost is roughly one authored paragraph per bead: ~155 at P2 where it
plausibly buys something, ~67 at P3 where it plausibly does not.

TO NOTE: fix 1 did not invent a rule. It started ENFORCING one that was already
written down and had been silently bypassed since May. The 250 is pre-existing
debt becoming visible, not new debt.

THE DECISION, three options as I see them:
 (a) Give the close gate an escape hatch matching its siblings (e.g.
     '# allow-thin-close' plus a recorded reason). Cheapest; restores symmetry;
     risks becoming the default.
 (b) Leave it strict and pay the paragraph tax — arguably correct, since the rule
     was always the rule, and 250 paragraphs is a few sweeps.
 (c) Strict, but carve out the self-declared-dead and empty-description cases,
     which are where the rule produces pure ceremony.

I did not choose, and NOTHING was bulk-rewritten. Related: dotfiles-d83p (the
propose-only triage sweep) is the natural vehicle for whichever option you pick.

title: spec: a WORK Claude seat on zig-computer via CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, for the seven migrated pulse rows
description:
## Overview
The retreat doc specifies WHERE the seven rows run after migration (zig-computer,
`pulse-inject.sh`, one durable window per row) but is silent on WHICH CLAUDE IDENTITY
runs them. This spec covers that gap. Parent: the retreat epic.

## Baseline — why this matters, in the units own words
`pulse-di-monday.service` header, from the 2026-07-27 cutover:

    # CUT OVER TO marketing-vps 2026-07-27 (explore-7iz9, bd-zcxo).
    # Reasoning + drafting run on the LinearB company seat; zig-computer opens the
    # tunnel, refreshes + asserts the box, dispatches, collects the payload, and
    # writes the ledger HERE. The box holds no credentials.

So the cutover existed TO PUT THIS WORK ON THE LINEARB SEAT. Migrating the rows back to
zig-computer without a work credential would run LinearB drafting on Zig PERSONAL
Claude subscription — reversing the reason for the cutover, and doing it silently
(nothing would error; the ticks would just bill and attribute to the wrong seat).

The rollback comment in each unit is ALSO not the target shape — it restores
`--session work --window pulse` (the pre-cutover SHARED conduit window), whereas Zig
2026-08-04 decision is one durable window PER ROW. Copying the rollback line verbatim
would restore the wrong design. Verified across all seven units 2026-08-05.

## The mechanism already exists and is in production here
Claude Code honors `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and relocates its ENTIRE config tree — verified
2026-07-28 during the tick-jail work: pointed at an empty dir it reports "Not logged in
· Please run /login" and scaffolds `.claude.json` / projects / sessions there.

`zig-computer:~/.claude-tick` EXISTS TODAY with its own `.credentials.json` (22 entries)
and is used by the live `dive` loop through `tick-jailed.sh`. So a second, separate
OAuth lineage on this box is a proven pattern, not a new invention. This spec applies the
same pattern to a `~/.claude-work` seat.

Why a separate config dir rather than an env-var token: an isolated dir carries its OWN
refresh lineage, so a work-seat refresh cannot rotate Zig personal credential out from
under him (the exact failure the tick-jail work measured — atomic rename + inode pinning,
host inode 1121600 vs jail 1134825, every turn 401ing).

## Changes
1. `~/.claude-work/` (0700), holding the work seat OAuth lineage.
2. A way for `pulse-inject.sh` to run a tick under a chosen `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` — new
   flag (e.g. `--config-dir`) or an env passthrough. DESIGN OPEN, see OQs.
3. The seven units converted from the remote form to the local form, each pinned to the
   work seat, one durable window per row (`di-monday` … `biweekly-content`).
4. Ledger/attribution: confirm the work seat rows are distinguishable in
   pico agentgateway logs (the `group`/`user` split from dotfiles-ogkz).

## Formal spec — the unit transformation
FROM (current, all seven):
    ExecStart=/bin/bash -c ". %h/.secrets; exec %h/dotfiles/agents/scheduler/pulse-dispatch-remote.sh \
        --loop %p --row di-monday --dir %h/linearb/dashboard-dev-interrupted --with-fleet-token --fresh"
TO (target shape, per the doc; the work-seat pinning is THIS spec addition):
    ExecStart=%h/dotfiles/agents/scheduler/pulse-inject.sh \
        --loop %p --fresh --dir %h/linearb/dashboard-dev-interrupted \
        --session zig-computer --window di-monday --cmd "/pulse tick"
`--row` disappears — row selection becomes the day-guard already in pulse.md condition
column (`date +%u = 1`). The routing tables in each project refs/pulse.md DO NOT CHANGE.

## Test Cases
1. an empty `~/.claude-work` yields "Not logged in", not a silent fallback to the personal seat
2. after login, a tick under `--config-dir ~/.claude-work` reaches Anthropic (200, not 401)
3. the personal `~/.claude/.credentials.json` inode is UNCHANGED after a work-seat token refresh
4. a work-seat tick appears in pico gateway log distinguishably from a personal tick
5. `pulse-inject.sh` with no config-dir flag behaves exactly as today (no regression to dive/desk/dream)
6. the day-guard fires di-monday on Monday and NOT on Tuesday
7. a converted row creates its OWN window, not a shared `work:pulse` pane
8. the ledger row is written on zig-computer with the right loop id
9. `--fresh` still starts a clean context in the per-row window
10. rollback: restoring the remote ExecStart returns the row to the old path unchanged
11. a work-seat 401 fails LOUD (no silent fallback to the personal seat) — cf. dotfiles-ucl4
12. two rows firing near-simultaneously do not collide in the same window

## Open Questions
- OQ1: `--config-dir` flag on pulse-inject.sh, or `Environment=CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=` in the
  unit? The unit-level env is less code and self-documenting in `systemctl cat`; the flag
  is testable in the suite. LEAN: unit-level `Environment=`, plus a pulse-inject assertion
  that the dir exists and holds a credential, so a missing seat fails loudly at dispatch.
- OQ2: does the work seat need the gateway (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` -> pico :17017), or go
  direct? The gateway gives o11y; it is also a fleet-wide SPOF (dotfiles-ucl4 outcome:
  6.5h, claude dead everywhere). LEAN: gateway, consistent with every other row.
- OQ3: does `tick-jailed.sh` apply to these rows? They are LinearB work over trusted
  input, not web crawling — probably not, but the interaction with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
  matters if it ever does.
- OQ4: what happens to the work seat when the andrew account on marketing-vps is deleted —
  is the OAuth lineage tied to the box, the account, or only the Anthropic identity?
  MUST be answered before Phase 5.

## Future
Once all seven are converted, the conduit simplifies away: pulse-dispatch-remote.sh
(~2,300 lines) loses every caller, fleet-creds.sh brokering is unnecessary (a local tick
reads ~/.secrets directly), and the deferred-surface / surface_request round-trip is
deleted for these rows.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] OQ1-OQ4 answered (via /check) before any unit is edited
- [ ] the 12 cases above are executable tests
- [ ] the pilot row runs on the work seat and is PROVEN not to have used the personal seat
notes:
## DECISIONS (Zig, 2026-08-05)
- **Rollout**: pilot di-monday and FORCE-FIRE it manually (`systemctl --user start`),
  rather than waiting for its real Monday. Fast feedback chosen deliberately.
  ⚠️ Consequence I am carrying forward rather than burying: a manual fire does NOT
  exercise the day-guard or the timer path. Those stay a precondition for PHASE 2a
  specifically (the irreversible step), not for the pilot. Recorded on dotfiles-vwrw.
- **Routing**: through pico agentgateway, consistent with every other row (OQ2 ANSWERED).
  Accepts the pico-SPOF exposure that dotfiles-ucl4 outcome measured (6.5h fleet-wide).
- **End state**: emptied-but-present account, reversible. Full deletion not chosen, so
  OQ4 (what the OAuth lineage is tied to) drops from BLOCKING to worth-knowing.

## OQ1 — ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT, not preference (2026-08-05)
The lean was unit-level `Environment=CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=`. **That would silently fail.**

Measured on zig-computer, tmux 3.5a:

    CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/PROBE tmux -L probe new-session -d -s t -n w "sleep 5"
    tmux -L probe show-environment -t t CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
      -> unknown variable: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR

The caller environment does NOT reach the tmux session. And it is worse than that:
`pulse-inject.sh:358` launches claude with **`send-keys "$LAUNCH" Enter`** — it TYPES the
command into a shell that already lives in the pane, so the launched process inherits the
**tmux server** environment, which was fixed whenever the server started. A unit-level
`Environment=` would be present in pulse-inject own env, never reach the pane, and the
tick would run on Zig PERSONAL seat with nothing erroring. Exactly the silent-success
shape this session has hit repeatedly.

So the seat must be passed EXPLICITLY. Two mechanisms, both available:
  - `new-session -e` / `new-window -e` (pulse-inject.sh:300 and :318) — sets it for panes
    created in that session/window
  - prefix the launch string itself, since the launch is a send-keys anyway

## A SECOND silent-failure mode, found in the same read
`pulse-inject.sh:331` checks `pane_current_command` and REUSES a live claude rather than
launching. So a `di-monday` window that already holds a personal-seat claude would be
reused and would serve the WRONG SEAT with no launch and no error. Setting the env at
launch time is therefore NOT sufficient — the guard must verify the RUNNING claude is on
the work seat, and fail loudly if not.

## Anchors for the implementation
    pulse-inject.sh:300  new-session -d -s "$SESSION" -c "$DIR"
    pulse-inject.sh:318  new-window  -d -P -F "#{window_id}" -t "=$SESSION" -n "$WINDOW" -c "$DIR"
    pulse-inject.sh:331  CURRENT_CMD=$(... pane_current_command)   <- the reuse path
    pulse-inject.sh:358  send-keys -t "$PANE" "$LAUNCH" Enter      <- the launch
Precedent: tick-jailed.sh:134 sets it via bwrap `--setenv` for the `dive` loop, and
`~/.claude-tick` is a live second OAuth lineage on this box today.

## SESSION DECIDED (Zig, 2026-08-05): `work`, NOT `zig-computer`

All seven rows land in the **`work`** session, one window per row:
`work:di-monday` … `work:di-friday`, `work:weekly-report`, `work:biweekly-content`.

This DIVERGES from the retreat doc example (`--session zig-computer`) and from every
native loop (dive/desk/dream/digest all use `--session zig-computer`). Zig call: these are
LinearB rows and he watches them in `work`, which is where their bells surface today via
the relay.

Consequences, verified 2026-08-05:
- **No relay.** They ring Zig DIRECTLY — running in his attached session means
  AskUserQuestion and the 🔔 glyph work natively. The surface_request round-trip exists only
  because a remote tick on an unattended box could not ring a bell.
- **`work:pulse` folds** once all seven are migrated. Verified safe: NO other unit targets
  `--window pulse`; the only other `work`-session loop is `pulse-elevate`, which uses its own
  `elevate` window. `work:🗼 vps` also becomes meaningless after the retreat.
- ⚠️ `--window pulse` remains pulse-inject BUILT-IN DEFAULT. Folding the window does not
  change the default; decide separately whether it should.
- ⚠️ `pulse-retry.sh` also consumes the surface-queue machinery, not just
  pulse-dispatch-remote.sh. Deleting the relay in Phase 7 must not amputate retry for loops
  that still use it. Recorded on dotfiles-35xo.

title: a1111: enable --api so recipients can drive via CLI/HTTP
description:
## Context

A1111 web UI on pico (rp0 + 43l + lus) was reachable but the
`/sdapi/v1/*` REST endpoints returned 404 because A1111 requires the
`--api` flag to expose them. Without the API, household members'
Claude instances can only operate A1111 through screenshots of the

via curl + JSON, do real iteration loops, parse outputs.

User context: building a `stable-diffusion-handoff.md` briefing doc
that household members paste to their own Claudes so the Claudes can
operate A1111 on their behalf. The doc only makes sense if the API is
actually live.

## Steps

1. Add `--api` to COMMANDLINE_ARGS in `~/dotfiles/a1111/webui-user.sh`
   (with a comment explaining the rationale + the same network-restriction
   safety posture as the UI)
2. Sync to pico's live config
3. Kickstart LaunchAgent
4. Verify `/sdapi/v1/sd-models` returns 200 with the loaded SDXL model

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `--api` in dotfiles/a1111/webui-user.sh COMMANDLINE_ARGS
- [x] Pico's live webui-user.sh synced
- [x] LaunchAgent kickstarted, A1111 boots clean
- [x] `GET /sdapi/v1/sd-models` returns 200 with sd_xl_base_1.0
- [x] `GET /sdapi/v1/samplers` returns the sampler list

notes:
## CLOSED 2026-05-24

Structural work complete: --api enabled on pico, A1111 serving JSON at
/sdapi/v1/*, dotfiles webui-user.sh committed + pushed (aa2359d). User
grabbed v1 of the handoff doc directly; v2 (with the API/CLI recipes)
was offered via http://100.98.174.21:8765/stable-diffusion-handoff.md
on the tailnet — user can fetch on demand. Taildrop-based delivery
turned out to be unworkable (Tailscale design limitation, see f7n).

Final acceptance criterion ("handoff doc delivered to user's iPhone
with API recipes") closed by: doc IS available at the tailnet HTTP
URL; user is aware; transport choice is theirs. The http server can be
killed when user signals.

description:

title: fix: zig-watchdog probes can race kanban dispatcher writes (SQLite corruption risk)
description:
## Problem

Kanban DB at /home/ubuntu/.hermes/kanban.db corrupted ~04:53 UTC during this
session ("sqlite refused to open file: database disk image is malformed").
Hermes auto-created 6+ .corrupt.bak files in 30 seconds (same image, sequential
timestamps — the corruption was already present at first backup). `.recover`
yielded schema only (0 INSERT statements) — data unrecoverable. All task
history lost: t_360fa078, t_2d3dcc3e (weekly-reporting), t_093c0add, etc.

## Symptom

`hermes kanban list` (or any kanban CLI) → "Refusing to open corrupt kanban
DB". Gateway log: "kanban dispatcher: board default database ... is not a
valid SQLite database; disabling dispatch for this board". User-facing impact:
Phase 2 substrate down; cross-arc kanban workloads stop dispatching.

## Likely cause

Concurrent writers on a single SQLite file with insufficient coordination:
- gateway-embedded dispatcher tick-loop (every 60s)
- watchdog systemd-timer tick (every 5min), which calls
  `hermes kanban dispatch --dry-run`, `hermes kanban diagnostics --json`,
  `hermes kanban show <tid>` (added in bd-cke fix) per actionable crash-loop
- ad-hoc CLI calls (this session: dispatch / show / block / unblock during
  debugging)
- worker subprocess spawn-crash cycles re-claiming + writing event rows

SQLite WAL mode handles concurrent readers + 1 writer, but multiple
fork/exec processes coordinating via WAL/SHM mmap with stale snapshot reads
can desync. The dispatcher's stuck-FD pattern documented earlier this
session was a symptom of similar pressure.

## Steps to Reproduce

Not deterministically reproducible yet. Best evidence:
1. Long-running hermes gateway (3+ hours)
2. Run zig-watchdog systemd timer firing every 5min on the same kanban DB
3. Add ad-hoc kanban CLI calls during a worker crash-loop scenario
4. After ~30min of mixed activity: `database disk image is malformed`

## Fix (proposed)

Three layers of defense:

### F1 — Watchdog write-coordination
Either (a) skip kanban probes when a dispatcher tick is mid-flight (filelock
on ~/.hermes/.dispatcher-tick.lock), OR (b) increase watchdog interval to
10min (less frequent racing), OR (c) make watchdog probes read-only via
sqlite3 directly with `?mode=ro&immutable=1` URI rather than spawning hermes
CLI subprocesses that may open WAL writers.

### F2 — Backup discipline
The corruption was already present in the FIRST .corrupt.bak. Hermes should
maintain a rolling daily-good snapshot (`kanban.db.daily.bak`) created via
`sqlite3 source ".backup target"` (atomic) rather than just preserving the
corrupt file. The watchdog could own this.

### F3 — Don't issue manual CLI calls while dispatcher is hot
Operational discipline: when investigating, query state via sqlite3 in
read-only mode rather than spawning more hermes CLI processes that contend.

## Source of Report

Empirical observation 2026-05-28 ~04:53 UTC during the dotfiles-cke fix
verification: t_360fa078 worker spawned (PID-tracked), watchdog probe ran a
new kanban-show call, gateway dispatcher continued its 60s tick — within
2 minutes the DB was malformed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] F1 implemented (one of a/b/c) with test
- [ ] F2 implemented + scheduled (daily good-state snapshot)
- [ ] F3 documented in ~/dotfiles/local-models/GUARDRAILS.md as a new G-entry
- [ ] Reproduction recipe captured (or marked as "could not reproduce")
- [ ] Bead: dotfiles-ns3 in commit trailer
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] F1 implemented (one of a/b/c) with test coverage
 - [ ] F2 implemented + scheduled (daily good-state snapshot)
 - [ ] F3 documented in GUARDRAILS.md as new G-entry
 - [ ] Reproduction recipe captured (or marked as unreproducible)
 - [ ] Bead: dotfiles-ns3 in commit trailer
notes: SUPERSEDED 2026-05-30 by dotfiles-lzs (Phase C-lite). The race-condition this bead described required an outside-the-gateway writer (zig-watchdog's HermesGateway probe). Phase C-lite stripped that probe entirely; watchdog no longer touches kanban.db. No outside writer = no race. F1/F2/F3 defenses no longer needed.

description:
Follow-up to the hook-architecture audit from the ~/explore/loop-engineering session. Verdict: do NOT hook judgment/behavior (cognitive-surrender ritual, scrutinize execute-observe, review cadence) — hooks are for checkable invariants. Fix the real clunk instead.

Plus a second fix: stop scraping bead IDs out of git-commit MESSAGE text (a message describing the fix false-blocked the commit — caught live). An invalid ERE was also caught by execute-testing.

title: gateway-switch.sh — one-command per-host kill switch for the pico agentgateway (off|on|status)
description:
WHY
On 2026-08-04 pico lost internet for ~6.5h. Routing is fail-hard with no fallback
(dotfiles-ucl4), so claude died fleet-wide, and flipping the fleet off the gateway took
~15 manual steps across two hosts plus a per-pane fix (dotfiles-9o46). Zig asked for a
real kill switch: one command, symmetric across zig-computer and marketing-vps, easy to
flip on and off.

DELIVERABLE
  agents/scheduler/gateway-switch.sh {off|on|status}
  agents/scheduler/test-gateway-switch.sh
  a short runbook section in agents/infra.md pointing at the script

BEHAVIOUR
`off` — bypass the gateway, talk to api.anthropic.com directly:
  1. comment the `export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=...` line in $HOME/.$(hostname -s).zshenv
  2. if a claude-gateway-tunnel.timer unit EXISTS on this host, `disable --now` it
  3. for every tmux pane whose pane_current_command is zsh or bash, send
     `unset ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`
  4. REPORT (do not touch) every pane holding a running claude/bwrap, since those need
     a manual restart
`on` — restore gateway routing: the same three steps inverted (uncomment; `enable --now`
the timer if the unit exists; `exec zsh` in shell panes -- which is sufficient in THIS
direction because there is nothing left to inherit), then verify.
`status` — report, without changing anything: the file's state and value, the timer state
if the unit exists, the live probe result, and every running claude process with its
actual routing read from /proc/<pid>/environ.

HARD REQUIREMENTS (each one is a real defect paid for already)
 A. THE SYMLINK MUST SURVIVE. $HOME/.<host>.zshenv is a symlink into ~/dotfiles. GNU
    `sed -i` WITHOUT --follow-symlinks replaces it with a regular file and silently
    detaches the host from the repo. Assert the path is still a symlink after every
    write, and cover it with a test.
 B. NEVER send keys to a pane that is not at a shell prompt. Typing into a live claude
    submits a prompt. Gate on pane_current_command and skip anything else. Today an
    input box already held unsent text in 2 of 5 panes.
 C. IDEMPOTENT. `off` twice, or `off` on an already-bypassed host, must be a clean no-op,
    not a double-comment (`## export`) that `on` cannot reverse. Test both directions
    twice in a row.
 D. Do NOT hardcode hostnames for the tunnel step. Key on whether the unit exists, so
    the script is correct on any host including ones that do not exist yet.
 E. Refuse, with a non-zero exit and a message naming the path, if there is no per-host
    zshenv or no export line to act on. Silence is the failure mode to avoid.
 F. No blanket `2>/dev/null` on state-changing or output-bearing commands (repo rule 3).
 G. `status` must be CHEAP -- no LLM calls. Put the real end-to-end request check behind
    an explicit opt-in flag, and when it runs it MUST use `env -u CC_NO_GATEWAY`,
    because a session started with the hatch exports it, every spawned shell inherits
    it, and the request then goes direct while looking like a passing gateway test
    (this exact false pass happened today).

VERIFICATION EXPECTED IN THE REPORT
Run the suite and paste real output. Demonstrate A and C by showing the failure BEFORE
and its absence AFTER (repo rule 1: a fix you cannot demonstrate is a fix you should not
claim). Run `status` on the real host and paste it. Do NOT run `off` against the live
fleet as a test -- use a fixture/fake HOME.

OUT OF SCOPE -- file a bead, do not build
  - restarting live claude sessions automatically (destroys context; Zig's call)
  - any fleet-wide/multi-host driver (rejected: it needs ssh from the box you are on,
    which is the least reliable thing during the outage it exists for)
  - metis (Zig explicitly excluded it; the script will work there generically anyway)
  - reworking the fail-hard no-fallback policy itself (dotfiles-ucl4 is deliberate)
notes:
## Scrutiny — 2026-08-04
Verdict: FIX-FIRST -> addressed -> SHIP

Independent read-only reviewer, dispatched pre-merge. It reproduced 42/42, spot-checked two
of the author's mutants with the mutation asserted applied, and confirmed all seven hard
requirements. It returned FIX-FIRST on one blocker; that blocker and two other findings were
fixed and re-verified before merge, hence SHIP.

  1 BLOCKER (fixed) — `on` un-commented ANY comment containing `export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=`.
    A commented-out example line ended an off/on cycle with TWO active exports, and the
    post-write check passed silently; a prose comment mentioning the variable was rewritten
    into syntax garbage. `zsh -n` ACCEPTS that garbage line — sourcing it fails with
    `no such file or directory: url`, rc 1, on every `ssh host cmd`, i.e. it would have
    broken remote pulse dispatch. Fixed by anchoring `on` to the script's own marker
    (`#gateway-switch:off# `), plus a distinct exit 67 that REFUSES and names the line when
    the only bypassed export was hand-commented, rather than guessing whose comment it is.
  2 (fixed) — no rollback if the post-write invariant failed, leaving a mangled file that
    every shell sources. `cat >` retained deliberately (an `mv` would destroy the symlink,
    requirement A); a backup is now taken and restored on any write/symlink/invariant
    failure, and the exit-1 doc no longer claims "nothing was attempted".
  3 (fixed) — a fixture HOME does NOT isolate this script: the REVIEWER'S OWN test disabled
    the live claude-gateway-tunnel.timer and enumerated live panes. Hermeticity comes from
    the PATH fakes, not from HOME. `--dry-run` added.
  4,5 deferred as beads: dotfiles-nrrp (warn that `off` dirties the repo-tracked file),
    dotfiles-ncsn (heredoc-body export lines).

## Merge-checkpoint evidence (run on `main`, not in the worktree)
  merge   df9e8a5 -> 2916238, SHA moved, agent commit 76d4886 asserted an ancestor
  suites  test-gateway-switch.sh PASS 52/52 · test-claude-identity-wrapper.sh ALL PASS (zsh)
          · test-ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh PASS 28/28 · doclint CLEAN
  hermetic running the full suite on main left live state untouched: timer enabled/active,
          probe 401, 1 active export, symlink intact
  live    `gateway-switch.sh off --dry-run` on marketing-vps printed the exact pending diff,
          the timer action, SKIP for its own pane and MANUAL for 5 panes running claude —
          then proved read-only: file cksum 3479706750 and timer enabled/active identical
          before and after
  mutants 16-mutant sweep, each dying on exactly its named cases. Two sweep entries were
          HARNESS ERRORS first (a pattern that matched nothing; one stale after a rename),
          so the harness now asserts each substitution matched before and stopped matching
          after — and R3 (rollback deleted) had SURVIVED 51/51 until case 52 was written for
          it. That is the rule-1 discipline working rather than being recited.

Read the implementation's own header for the marker/HAND_RE reasoning before touching the
matchers; the ambiguity it refuses to guess at is deliberate.
close_reason: Merged to main as 2916238 (agent commit 76d4886 asserted an ancestor). Scrutiny verdict FIX-FIRST -> addressed -> SHIP. Suites on main: 52/52 gateway-switch, wrapper ALL PASS, fleet-tunnel 28/28, doclint clean, and the suite provably does not disturb live state. The blocker scrutiny caught would have written syntax garbage into a file every non-interactive shell sources, breaking remote pulse dispatch; that plus a missing rollback and the fixture-HOME hazard (which had already toggled the live timer twice) were fixed before merge. Verified live on marketing-vps via --dry-run: exact pending diff, correct timer action, own pane skipped, 5 claude panes flagged MANUAL, byte-identical file and unchanged timer afterward.

title: test-pre-commit-checks case 22 is load-sensitive and now gates commits — it can flake-block a commit that is fine
description:
## Context

`dotfiles-jm1c` gave the 32 suites a runner (`tools/githooks/pre-commit` +
`core.hooksPath`). That is the right fix, and it has a side effect worth tracking: a
flaky suite is no longer merely noisy, it **blocks commits**.

`agents/hooks/test/test-pre-commit-checks.sh` case 22
(`block: slow proof times out inside the budget`) sets
`HARNESS_PULSE_PROOF_BUDGET=1`. Under load the hook burns more than 1s on `jq`/`git`
before it ever reaches the proof, so it emits the **budget-exhausted** message instead of
the **timeout** message and the case fails on `stderr missing: timed out after 1s`.

Measured by the agent that shipped the runner: green 3/3 standalone; fails under a mutant
run at load ~10.5, where it appeared as an over-broad neighbour and had to be diagnosed
before the real mutant result could be trusted.

**Pre-existing, not introduced by the runner** — but the runner is what makes it cost
something.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Load the box (several concurrent agents, load avg ~10).
2. `bash agents/hooks/test/test-pre-commit-checks.sh`
3. Case 22 fails with `stderr missing: timed out after 1s`; the hook emitted the
   budget-exhausted message instead.
4. Re-run on a quiet box → passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Case 22 is deterministic under load. Two candidate fixes, and this is a judgment
      call: raise `HARNESS_PULSE_PROOF_BUDGET` so the fixed overhead cannot consume it, or
      accept **either** message via a `want_stderr` alternation.
- [ ] State which and why. Accepting both messages tests less; raising the budget makes
      the case slower. Neither is obviously right.
- [ ] Whatever ships, demonstrate it under load — a fix verified only on a quiet box has
      not been verified against the condition that breaks it.

Related: `dotfiles-jm1c` (the runner that raised the stakes), `dotfiles-b9ii` (which added
cases 20-23).
notes:
## Resolution — 2026-08-01 (AC #2: which fix, and why)

Written by the orchestrator; the agent correctly declined to `br update` a bead it did not
create, and left the full rationale in commit `d3df42f` and a 25-line comment above case 22.

### The orchestrator's lean was HALF WRONG, and the measurement is the finding

I briefed "raise the budget, don't accept both messages," reasoning that an alternation
would leave the case unable to tell the two code paths apart. The agent tested it instead
of adopting it and found **two independent defects**, only one of which the bead knew about:

1. The budget is too small under load (the known half).
2. **The assertion pins an exact second count.** The hook prints
   `timed out after ${PROOF_LEFT}s` where `PROOF_LEFT = budget - elapsed`, so raising the
   budget merely *relabels* the flake. Measured at `budget=5`, asserting
   `"timed out after 5s"`: **2/20 red at load 47**, reporting `after 4s`.

So raise-only — my lean — does not fix it. Nobody had noticed defect 2.

### What shipped: both halves

- **Derived budget, not a constant** (the "third option" the brief asked to look for). The
  case runs the hook once with a `cmd: "true"` proof, measures overhead in the same whole
  seconds the hook's own `date +%s` arithmetic uses, and sets
  `SLOW_BUDGET = 2*overhead + 3`. Quiet box → 3; it scales with the box.
- **Assert the phrase `"timed out after "`, not the number.**

### The alternation objection does NOT apply — verified independently

This is the part worth recording, because it is the difference between this fix and the
weaker option the bead offered. Asserting the phrase is **branch-unique**, checked against
the hook source by the orchestrator rather than accepted on report:

    pre-commit-checks.sh:384  (budget exhausted) "... ran out before verifying: ..."
    pre-commit-checks.sh:400  (real timeout)     "  timed out after ${PROOF_LEFT}s ..."

Disjoint strings. A hook that never reaches the proof still goes **red**, so the case
tests exactly what it always tested; only the volatile integer left the assertion. Case 23
was untouched — it is inherently robust because both its paths emit `proof budget`, which
is why 22 was the only flaker.

### Evidence (AC #3 — demonstrated under load, not on a quiet box)

12 cores, synthetic load via 36 `yes` processes.

    baseline flake, full suite      load 28-43   1/10 suites RED
    baseline flake, isolated x30    load 44      4/30 RED
    naive raise-only (my lean)      load 47      2/20 RED  <- disproof
    fix, isolated x20               load 49      20/20 green
    fix, full suite x20             load 52      20/20 green, rc=0
    fix, full suite x8, idle        load 2.9     8/8 green

**Positive control** — mutated a *copy* of `agents/hooks/` (shared checkout untouched):
deleting the `PROOF_RC -eq 124` diagnostic block, and `timeout "$PROOF_LEFT"` → `timeout 60`.
Both make case 22 **fail, and only case 22**. The case can still go red.

**Independent re-verification by the orchestrator**, load avg 1.93:
`bash agents/hooks/test/test-pre-commit-checks.sh` → **PASS: 69/69, exit 0**.

### Cost + follow-up

Suite 7.6s → 8.8s idle (one extra hook invocation for the probe). No hook change was
needed; `pre-commit-checks.sh` is untouched. No other case flaked across 38 loaded runs.

Filed `dotfiles-wuze` (P3): the mutation-harness commit gate takes **4m24s at load 55**,
not the `~90s` its own comment and user-facing message advertise, with no intermediate
output — a multi-minute silent wait during `git commit` that reads as a hang.

title: spec: route marketing-vps Claude Code through pico's agentgateway via a chained SSH tunnel, with machine-of-origin attribution
description:
## Overview

marketing-vps must use pico's agentgateway as its ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. pico is
tailnet-only; the VPS is not on the tailnet and never will be. Additionally, every
agentgateway request must carry the machine of origin as a FIRST-CLASS FILTERABLE
FIELD in the admin UI (not a hidden label).

## Baseline (all verified live 2026-08-02, not inferred)

- pico agentgateway 1.4.1, launchd `com.zig.agentgateway`, uptime 22h,
  KeepAlive={SuccessfulExit=false}, ThrottleInterval=10.
- The `/claude` route on 17017 is a transparent passthrough with NO apiKey policy.
- Gateway health signature: GET /claude/v1/models -> **401** (reached Anthropic,
  no key). NOT 200. /claude/ and /v1/models both -> 404.
- Identity today: claude-identity-wrapper.sh sends
  `X-Session-Identity: <tmux session>:<window>`; pico config line 9 maps it via CEL
  into standardAttributes.user -> the `agentgateway_user` column.
- **The first field is the tmux SESSION name, not the machine.** Live proof: BOTH
  zig-computer and marketing-vps have a tmux session named `work`
  (zig-computer: `work:pulse`, `work:vps`; vps: `work:di-monday` etc). metis carries
  the same ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, so >=3 machines already share one flat namespace.
- `src.addr` cannot discriminate: all rows are 100.98.174.21 (zig-computer), and
  tunnelled VPS traffic will arrive as that same address.
- `agentgateway_group` is NULL in **all 78,956 rows** and already has a dedicated
  index `idx_request_logs_group_completed_at`. Virgin squat target.
- The binary contains the facet/dropdown query listing
  gen_ai_request_model / gen_ai_provider_name / agentgateway.user /
  **agentgateway.group** / user_agent.name — so `group` IS an automatic filter
  dropdown, alongside the ones Zig already sorts by.
- ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS supports MULTIPLE headers, `Name: Value`,
  **newline-separated** (first-party docs, code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars).
- Loopback base URL is safe: the `ERR_HTTP_HOOK_BLOCKED_ADDRESS` loopback guard
  applies to HTTP hooks and explicitly ALLOWS 127.0.0.1;
  CLAUDE_GATEWAY_ALLOW_LOOPBACK belongs to the separate CLAUDE_CODE_USE_GATEWAY mode.
- ⚠️ `config:` (which contains standardAttributes) is applied **ONLY AT STARTUP** —
  agentgateway hot-reloads modelCatalog only. The group change REQUIRES a restart,
  which briefly interrupts fleet-wide LLM traffic.

## Changes

### 1. Transport — ONE hop, not two (verified working)
`ssh -L 127.0.0.1:17017:100.72.47.4:17017 zig-computer` from the VPS. ssh resolves
the forward DESTINATION on the far end, so zig-computer does the tailnet leg itself.
No nested tunnel.

Measured from marketing-vps 2026-08-02, with controls:
    no-tunnel            -> 000   (negative control)
    /claude/v1/models    -> 401   (through the tunnel; == direct baseline)
    post-teardown        -> gone, 7100 fleet tunnel untouched

LOCAL `-L` (VPS-initiated), never reverse `-R` — same argument
ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh already documents: only the initiator can reopen it, and a
stranded VPS whose gateway died has NO working claude at all.

### 2. Generalize ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh (Zig's call: generalize, not a sibling)
It hardcodes target `127.0.0.1:$PORT`, probe path `/api/health`, and expects 200.
Add `--target HOST:PORT`, `--probe-path PATH`, `--expect CODE`. Defaults keep the
fleet-proxy behavior byte-identical.

### 3. Routing
`export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:17017/claude"` in
`zsh/.vps-8a9eb245.zshenv`. NO shell rotation needed — the claude() wrapper
re-derives this per LAUNCH from ~/.<host>.zshenv (the dotfiles-t6to fix).

### 4. Machine label — squat `group` (Zig's design, better than the alternatives)
- wrapper sends a SECOND newline-separated header `X-Machine-Origin: <hostname -s>`
- pico gains `standardAttributes.group` CEL reading it
- `user` (session:window) and 78,956 rows of history are UNCHANGED

### 5. Second producer site
~/explore/tools/tick-jail/tick-jailed.sh mirrors the env via --setenv and must carry
the new header too, else jailed ticks are machine-unattributed.

## Ordering is safe in BOTH directions
Header-without-CEL is ignored; CEL-without-header yields the CEL default. No lockstep.

## Test Cases
1. VPS: negative control — probe before tunnel -> 000
2. VPS: ensure -> 401 through the tunnel (the healthy signature)
3. ensure is idempotent: second call no-ops, does not churn a healthy socket
4. ensure never kills a listener it did not start (7100 must survive)
5. defaults unchanged: fleet-proxy invocation still probes /api/health expecting 200
6. --expect 401 treats 200 as BLOCKED, not healthy
7. wrapper emits BOTH headers, newline-separated, in bash AND zsh
8. wrapper fails open: no tmux -> machine header still present
9. pico: a real claude call from the VPS produces a row with group=marketing-vps
10. pico: a call from zig-computer produces group=zig-computer, user unchanged
11. existing 78,956 rows still parse/group by user after the change
12. CC_NO_GATEWAY=1 still bypasses on the VPS

## Open Questions
- OQ1: fallback when the tunnel is down — fail to direct api.anthropic.com (keeps
  claude working, loses o11y) or fail hard? The VPS failure mode is worse than the
  fleet-proxy one: no gateway == no claude at all.
- OQ2: restart window for pico. It interrupts live fleet sessions including Zig's.
close_reason: Delivered and verified end to end. Transport: ONE hop, not two — ssh -L resolves its destination on the far end, so zig-computer does the tailnet leg (000 negative control, 401 through). Label: squatted the unused agentgateway_group column (Zig's design, better than the options offered) — user stays session:window, all 84,434 historical rows untouched, filterability confirmed via /api/logs/search with positive AND negative controls. marketing-vps is live on the gateway behind a self-healing 2-min timer. Both scrutiny passes returned FIX-FIRST on changes whose mechanical gates were already green: two mutants surviving on the exact branch the VPS now uses (dropped permissions flag, injected credential), and re_escape entirely untested while an unescaped pattern provably matched a DIFFERENT forward. Follow-ups left open deliberately: dotfiles-20rx (CC_NO_GATEWAY broken in fresh zsh), dotfiles-wpu2 (promote the mutation harness), dotfiles-ahrd (tick-jail header coverage).

title: retreat: replicate ~/.in-case-of-retreat.txt into the repo — the plan exists in exactly one place
description:
## Context
The canonical retreat plan is `zig-computer:~/.in-case-of-retreat.txt`. It is UNTRACKED
and exists on exactly one machine. Every other artifact in this arc is replicated; the
plan that governs the destruction is not.

This is the same class as the doc own §1 warning about `~/marketing-vps/.beads` ("6
rows... Replicated NOWHERE. Wiping that directory destroys them") — except the plan
governs the wipe itself, so losing it mid-retreat is worse than losing the beads.

It also has a second reader problem: it is invisible to any session that is not on
zig-computer as `ubuntu`. This session had to be told the path, and then had to guess the
`.txt` extension.

## What to do
Copy it to `dotfiles/refs/in-case-of-retreat.md` and make the home-dir file the pointer,
not the other way round — a `~/` dotfile is unreviewable and unversioned, and this doc is
going to be edited as the retreat proceeds (it already says "NOT smoke-tested — verify
facts live"). In-repo it gets diffs, review, and cross-machine reach.

⚠️ Check before committing: the doc names hostnames, IPs (15.204.114.210, 51.81.33.136),
usernames, key filenames and comments, and a sudoers path. Those are already all over
`agents/infra.md`, so it is consistent with repo practice — but it contains NO secret
VALUES and must not gain any (AGENTS.md: reference by pointer, never paste).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `refs/in-case-of-retreat.md` committed, content byte-equivalent to the source
      modulo the frontmatter/pointer edit
- [ ] `~/.in-case-of-retreat.txt` on zig-computer replaced by (or amended with) a pointer
      to the repo path, so the two cannot silently diverge
- [ ] `~/.break-glass.txt` cross-references updated if it names the old path
- [ ] verified readable from marketing-vps (i.e. a session not on zig-computer can find it)
close_reason: Replicated to refs/in-case-of-retreat.md (72eb426). BYTE-FIDELITY PROVEN THREE WAYS, and the orchestrator re-derived it independently rather than accepting the report: the body extracted from the COMMITTED git object, the live remote file after its pointer edit, and the pre-edit backup all hash to da0d136faac57f19562b52051502dbcc. Whole-file diff shows exactly two hunks — a 12-line header plus a 'text'-tagged fence — and zero lines of the plan changed. The 'text' fence rather than markdown headings was the right call: it preserves the ASCII section rules and shell-snippet indentation that '#' conversion would have silently reflowed, which for a doc whose steps get EXECUTED is the difference between a copy and a paraphrase (CLAUDE.md rule 2, as amended today by g2vg — run/verify the bytes as committed, not a retyped copy). The divergence loop is closed at the source: zig-computer:~/.in-case-of-retreat.txt now opens with a prepended block saying it is no longer canonical, naming the repo path, and stating the repo wins on disagreement — with the full body preserved below rather than deleted, so nothing is lost on a box whose checkout has not caught up. Backup at ~/.in-case-of-retreat.txt.bak.2026-08-05. ~/.break-glass.txt turned out never to reference the file (grep rc=1), so it was correctly left untouched rather than edited speculatively. Secret grep clean — the only near-hit is the NOPASSWD:ALL sudoers rule already quoted in the plan's Phase 4d, and every long opaque run is a filesystem path.

title: spec: zig-watchdog — mechanical stall detection + revive for long-running jobs (bench, model pulls, Hermes gateway)
description:
# Spec: zig-watchdog — mechanical stall/crash detection + revive for long-running jobs

## 1. Overview

Single Python script + systemd-user timer that periodically probes a registered set
of long-running job classes for stall/crash patterns and either revives them
mechanically or alerts the operator. Replaces the current "user nudges Claude when
something dies" pattern with mechanical discipline that runs autonomously and
survives Claude session boundaries.

**This skill is structurally analogous to the autonovel-phase1 substrate**: a
deterministic-script cron-equivalent (systemd timer) running every N minutes, no
LLM in the path, with structured probe()/revive() per concern.

## 2. Baseline / current state

Two failures THIS SESSION proved the need:

1. **Kimi-Linear pull stalled for 8h** in CLOSE_WAIT socket state with no progress;
   user had to nudge ("make sure the kimi download isnt hanging") to surface it.
   Recovery was mechanical: kill + restart hf download.
2. **bench-matrix.sh aborted** at cell 3/9 when Ollama on pico became wedged in a
   wedged-generation state; user had to nudge ("dont forget my SPA request" implied
   they noticed I'd missed the matrix dying). Recovery was mechanical: pkill ollama,
   restart, bench-matrix --resume.

Plus a third found AFTER asking for the watchdog spec:

3. **autonovel kanban worker crash-looped 99 times** in ~96 min, each ~60s. Dispatcher
   kept respawning despite failure_limit=2 because of gave_up→promoted cycling.
   Mechanical fix: detect ≥3 crashes within 5 min on same task → block the task.

All three share an exact shape: long-running process, PID alive (or pseudo-alive),
observably stalled (file mtime stale OR endpoint hung OR rapid spawn-crash cycle).

## 3. Changes / decisions

- **Architecture**: Single Python 3 script `~/.local/share/zig-watchdog/watchdog.py`,
  stdlib only. Plugin pattern — each long-job class implements `Probe` (returns OK |
  STALL | CRASH | UNKNOWN) and `Revive` (idempotent fix). New job classes = add a
  Python class, no infra change.
- **Trigger**: systemd-user timer `zig-watchdog.timer`, OnUnitActiveSec=5min,
  Persistent=true (survives reboot).
- **Service unit**: `zig-watchdog.service` Type=oneshot, ExecStart=python3 watchdog.py
- **Logs**: `/tmp/zig-watchdog.log` (rotated by systemd journal anyway), plus per-tick
  results stashed to `~/.cache/zig-watchdog/state.json` for the SPA to consume.
- **Notification**: writes alerts to `~/.cache/zig-watchdog/alerts.json` (append).
  The bench-dashboard SPA (already shipped at port 8765) reads this and surfaces
  via the browser Notifications API (user-confirmed flavor). Pure tailnet.
- **Self-monitoring exclusion**: watchdog does NOT depend on Hermes (avoids the
  circular dependency caught earlier this session when the gateway disk-I/O
  appeared blocked).

## 4. Formal specification

### 4.1 Job classes (v1)

| Class | Probe | Revive |
|---|---|---|
| `BenchMatrix` | (a) pgrep bench-matrix.sh; (b) check newest results/HEALTHCHECK_FAIL-*.txt mtime; (c) curl pico Ollama+MLX endpoints | If aborted-by-healthcheck AND backends recovered: `nohup bench-matrix.sh --smoke --resume > /tmp/.../log &`. Cooldown: 10min between restart attempts. |
| `HfDownload` | For each `hf download` PID on pico: ssh check CPU=0 AND `.incomplete` file mtime older than 5min | kill -9 PID; restart with same args from log file; preserve partial downloads (HF resumes file-level) |
| `HermesGateway` | (a) systemctl --user is-active hermes-gateway; (b) check `hermes kanban dispatch --dry-run --json` succeeds; (c) check for repeated crash patterns in last 5min — task with ≥3 crashes in 5min should auto-block | (a) restart service if inactive; (b) `hermes kanban block <task_id>` if crash-loop detected |
| `BenchDashboard` | curl http://localhost:8765/healthz | restart via start-dashboard.sh |

### 4.2 Plugin interface

```python
class JobClass:
    name: str
    probe_interval_seconds: int = 300  # default 5min
    cooldown_seconds: int = 600         # 10min between revive attempts per job
    max_revive_attempts: int = 3        # before alerting

    def probe(self) -> ProbeResult: ...
    def revive(self) -> ReviveResult: ...
```

`ProbeResult = OK | STALL | CRASH | UNKNOWN` (string enum)
`ReviveResult = SUCCESS | FAILED` (string enum)

### 4.3 State machine per job

```
NORMAL ── probe=STALL/CRASH ──► REVIVING ── revive=SUCCESS ──► NORMAL
                                  │
                                  └─ revive=FAILED ──► (incr counter) ──► if counter≥3: ALERTING
```

### 4.4 Output schema (`~/.cache/zig-watchdog/state.json`)

```json
{
  "last_tick_utc": "2026-05-28T03:00:00Z",
  "jobs": {
    "BenchMatrix": {
      "last_probe": "OK",
      "last_probe_utc": "...",
      "last_revive_attempt_utc": null,
      "revive_attempts": 0,
      "alerting": false
    },
    "HfDownload": {...},
    ...
  }
}
```

### 4.5 Alerts schema (`~/.cache/zig-watchdog/alerts.json`)

Append-only JSON-lines for the SPA to read:
```json
{"utc": "2026-05-28T03:05:00Z", "job": "HermesGateway", "kind": "crash-loop-detected", "detail": "task t_360fa078 crashed 5x in 5min", "auto_action": "blocked"}
```

### 4.6 SPA integration (existing bench-dashboard)

- Add `GET /api/alerts.json` endpoint returning the tail-of alerts.json
- Add JS that polls /api/alerts.json every 5s and fires `new Notification(...)` on new entries (after `Notification.requestPermission()`)
- Add a red banner on the dashboard when any job is `alerting=true`

## 5. Test cases (≥10)

TEST: probe_bench_matrix_ok_when_healthcheck_recent
TEST: probe_bench_matrix_stall_when_aborted_and_backends_healthy
TEST: probe_hf_download_stall_when_cpu_zero_and_mtime_old
TEST: probe_hf_download_ok_when_file_growing
TEST: probe_hermes_crash_loop_when_3_crashes_in_5min
TEST: probe_hermes_ok_when_dispatch_dry_run_succeeds
TEST: revive_bench_matrix_runs_command_and_logs
TEST: revive_hf_download_kills_and_restarts
TEST: revive_hermes_blocks_crash_loop_task
TEST: max_revive_attempts_triggers_alert
TEST: cooldown_prevents_immediate_re_revive
TEST: state_json_written_each_tick

## 6. Open questions

- OQ-01 (P1): Run on zig only, or also on pico for HfDownload-on-pico? **DECIDED: zig only**, but `HfDownload.probe()` uses `ssh pico` to inspect remote processes. Less infra.
- OQ-02 (P1): Watchdog timer interval? **DECIDED: 5min** (matches typical stall-detection windows).
- OQ-03 (P2): Alert delivery? **DECIDED: browser Notification API via SPA** (user-confirmed). ntfy.sh self-hosted is v2.
- OQ-04 (P3): Self-monitoring (watchdog itself dies)? **DEFERRED — systemd Restart=on-failure on timer; manual `journalctl --user -u zig-watchdog -f` for explicit health.

## 7. Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Single file at `~/dotfiles/local-models/zig-watchdog.py` (stdlib only)
- [ ] systemd-user timer + service at `~/dotfiles/local-models/zig-watchdog.{service,timer}` + installer script
- [ ] ≥12 pytest tests (per §5) all pass
- [ ] First mechanical action: detects today's blocked t_360fa078 + bench-matrix abort + queues smoke restart
- [ ] SPA adds /api/alerts.json + browser Notification + red banner widget
- [ ] Bead: dotfiles-olh in commit trailer

## NOT in scope (v1)

- ntfy.sh self-hosted (v2)
- Push to user's phone outside Notification API
- Watchdog-watchdog (the self-monitor)
- Cross-host probing beyond pico (just one remote)
- Job-class plugin loading from external file (v1 has them in-source)
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Single file at local-models/zig-watchdog.py (stdlib only)
 - [ ] systemd-user timer + service + installer script
 - [ ] ≥12 pytest tests all pass
 - [ ] Mechanical action: blocks crash-loops, restarts stalled hf-downloads, restarts aborted bench-matrix
 - [ ] SPA gets /api/alerts.json + browser Notification + red banner widget
 - [ ] Bead: dotfiles-olh in commit trailer

title: ss14-c2-cutover: 11-step playbook — flip SS14 from zig-computer to pico via wrapper
description:
## Context

Final live-cutover bead for Approach C2 (spec dotfiles-9g1). All upstream work has shipped:

- **dotfiles**: ss14-wrapper Go daemon (impl 1bi SHIP, xx9 integration test PASS, b9o deploy artifacts ready)
- **vacation-station-14**: C# patches (vs-4h1 + vs-q7m fix wave SHIP); azigler/RobustToolbox fork live; .gitmodules updated
- **pico**: ss14-wrapper LaunchAgent loaded, listening on 100.72.47.4:11214 (UDP+TCP), HEALTH probe OK; ARM64 SS14 + watchdog build artifacts already on pico from Phase 4 attempt (preserved)
- **zig-computer**: SS14 currently LIVE serving real players; nginx ready for `stream{}` block

This bead drives the actual flip. Production-affecting (drops players currently connected); needs an off-hours window + the user's hand on the wheel.

## Pre-flight checklist

Before running ANY step, confirm:

- [ ] Current player count on `ss14.zig.computer` is 0 (or low + announced maintenance)
- [ ] pico is healthy: `ssh pico 'echo HEALTH | nc -U /tmp/ss14-wrapper.sock'` returns `OK active_sessions=N uptime_s=M`
- [ ] vs14 is up-to-date on pico: `ssh pico 'cd ~/vacation-station-14 && git pull && git submodule update --init --recursive'` — should pull azigler/RobustToolbox + the C# patches
- [ ] SS14 build on pico is current: `ssh pico 'cd ~/vacation-station-14 && ./BuildContent.py'` (or equivalent) — verify build succeeds
- [ ] Snapshot zig-computer nginx config: `sudo cp /etc/nginx/sites-available/ss14.zig.computer.conf /tmp/ss14-nginx.bak.$(date +%s)`
- [ ] Snapshot pico Robust.Server config: `ssh pico 'cp /opt/ss14-watchdog/instances/vacation-station/config.toml /tmp/vs14-config.bak.$(date +%s)'`
- [ ] ban_address row count snapshot: `psql -h pico -U vs14 -d vacation_station -c "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ban_address;"` — record number to compare post-cutover
- [ ] Maintenance window announced (Discord / hub status / wherever)
- [ ] Rollback runbook reviewed: every step below has its rollback documented inline

## The 11-step playbook (per spec dotfiles-9g1 §4.6)

### Step 1 — On pico: configure wrapper-aware cvars in pico's Robust.Server config

Add to `/opt/ss14-watchdog/instances/vacation-station/config.toml`:

```toml
[net]
use_wrapper_remote_address = true
wrapper_socket = "/tmp/ss14-wrapper.sock"
```

Plus the existing `[status]` config — `bind = "127.0.0.1:1213"` (NOT `*:1212`; bind loopback so only wrapper reaches it).

**Rollback**: revert to snapshot `/tmp/vs14-config.bak.*`.

### Step 2 — On pico: update wrapper LaunchAgent upstream

Current wrapper's `SS14_WRAPPER_UPSTREAM=127.0.0.1:11215` (dev/test default). Flip to `127.0.0.1:1213` (where Robust.Server will bind):

```bash
ssh pico 'sed -i.bak "s|127.0.0.1:11215|127.0.0.1:1213|" ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.ss14-wrapper.plist'
ssh pico 'launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u pico)/com.zig.ss14-wrapper'
```

Verify wrapper restarted clean: `ssh pico 'echo HEALTH | nc -U /tmp/ss14-wrapper.sock'`.

**Rollback**: revert plist `.bak`, kickstart again.

### Step 3 — On pico: load SS14 watchdog LaunchAgents

The watchdog plist at `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.ss14-watchdog.plist` is on disk but unloaded (per Phase 4 rollback). Load it:

```bash
ssh pico 'launchctl load -w ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.ss14-watchdog.plist'
ssh pico 'launchctl load -w ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.ss14-replay-rotate.plist'
```

Watchdog will start Robust.Server (binding to 127.0.0.1:1213). Verify:

```bash
ssh pico 'lsof -iTCP:1213 -sTCP:LISTEN; lsof -iUDP:1213'
ssh pico 'curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:1213/status | head -3'
```

**Rollback**: `launchctl unload -w ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.ss14-watchdog.plist` + same for replay-rotate.

### Step 4 — Smoke test: synthetic UDP from another tailnet device → wrapper → Robust.Server

From zig-computer:

```bash
python3 -c "
import socket
header = b'PROXY TCP4 192.0.2.99 100.72.47.4 64000 11214\r\n'
sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
sock.bind(('', 56000))
# Send a Lidgren ping (well-formed empty payload won't actually be parsed,
# but it'll register a session in the wrapper)
sock.sendto(header + b'\\x00\\x00\\x00\\x00', ('100.72.47.4', 11214))
"
sleep 1
ssh pico 'echo "ENUMERATE" | nc -U /tmp/ss14-wrapper.sock'
```

Should see `udp <fanout-port> 192.0.2.99:64000` in the ENUMERATE output. Confirms wrapper sees synthetic client + tracks real IP.

**Rollback**: nothing to roll back — synthetic test only.

### Step 5 — On zig-computer: write the nginx stream{} block (PROD)

`/etc/nginx/streams-enabled/ss14-game.conf`:

```nginx
upstream ss14_pico_udp {
    server 100.72.47.4:11214;
}
upstream ss14_pico_tcp {
    server 100.72.47.4:11214;
}
server {
    listen 1212 udp;
    proxy_pass ss14_pico_udp;
    proxy_protocol on;
    proxy_timeout 120s;
    proxy_responses 1;
}
server {
    listen 1212;
    proxy_pass ss14_pico_tcp;
    proxy_protocol on;
    proxy_timeout 120s;
}
```

(Exact form per OQ-01 decision: 120s proxy_timeout grounded in Lidgren PingInterval=1s default per /check dotfiles-9cj.)

**Rollback**: `sudo rm /etc/nginx/streams-enabled/ss14-game.conf && sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx`.

### Step 6 — On zig-computer: nginx -t + reload

```bash
sudo nginx -t
sudo systemctl reload nginx
```

If `-t` fails, abort and fix the conf before reload.

**Rollback**: same as Step 5.

### Step 7 — On zig-computer: stop ss14-watchdog + replay-rotate (the LIVE services)

```bash
sudo systemctl stop ss14-watchdog
sudo systemctl disable ss14-watchdog
sudo systemctl stop ss14-replay-rotate.timer
sudo systemctl disable ss14-replay-rotate.timer
```

At this point, SS14 is REACHABLE via nginx → pico's wrapper → pico's Robust.Server. Players currently connected to zig-computer drop. Reconnect lands on pico.

**Rollback**: `sudo systemctl enable --now ss14-watchdog ss14-replay-rotate.timer`. SS14 is back on zig within ~30s.

### Step 8 — End-to-end client connection test

Open SS14 launcher → connect to `ss14://ss14.zig.computer` → expect to land in lobby → join round → play for 60s. Confirm:

- Connection succeeds
- Player count in `/status` increments correctly
- No connection-drop / disconnect events in `/tmp/ss14-wrapper.log` on pico

**Rollback**: if connection fails, roll back Steps 7 → 5 (re-enable zig watchdog, remove nginx stream block).

### Step 9 — Ban-address real-IP verification (the architectural goal)

Issue a test ban from an admin client (in-game command), then check the DB:

```bash
psql -h pico -U vs14 -d vacation_station -c "SELECT address FROM ban_address ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 5;"
```

Most-recent row's address should be the **real client IP** (NOT 100.72.47.4 / nginx's IP). Confirms IRemoteAddressOverride is functioning end-to-end through the SS14 moderation path.

**Rollback**: roll back if the address is nginx's IP — investigate cvar / IoC registration / wrapper UDS connectivity.

### Step 10 — Sustained monitoring

Watch for 30 minutes:

- `tail -f /tmp/ss14-wrapper.log` on pico (no unexpected errors)
- `tail -f /tmp/Library/Logs/ss14-watchdog/...` (Robust.Server logs)
- nginx error log on zig-computer: `sudo tail -f /var/log/nginx/error.log`
- Real player connections (organic traffic — wait for natural population)

Any sustained errors (per-minute disconnects, NaN rates, latency spikes) → roll back.

**Rollback**: full revert to Steps 7 → 5 sequence (re-enable zig watchdog, remove nginx stream block).

### Step 11 — Documentation

After 30+ minutes of stability:

- Flip dotfiles-9g1 spec bead → closed (work is shipped)
- Update zig-zone runbook: mark Phase 4 as SHIPPED-via-C2 (was originally rolled back; the eventual win was a different architecture than originally attempted)
- Drop a `note` bead with the cutover-date + observed metrics (latency p50/p99, ban_address real-IP confirmed, etc.)
- Brief Discord / community channels if applicable

**Rollback**: N/A (post-stability documentation).

## Total rollback (nuclear)

If anything goes catastrophically wrong at any step:

```bash
# On zig-computer
sudo rm /etc/nginx/streams-enabled/ss14-game.conf
sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
sudo systemctl enable --now ss14-watchdog ss14-replay-rotate.timer

# On pico
ssh pico 'launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.ss14-watchdog.plist'
ssh pico 'launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.zig.ss14-replay-rotate.plist'
ssh pico 'cp /tmp/vs14-config.bak.* /opt/ss14-watchdog/instances/vacation-station/config.toml'
ssh pico 'launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u pico)/com.zig.ss14-wrapper'   # reset upstream port
```

SS14 back on zig in <60s. Wrapper still running on pico but idle (no upstream traffic).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pre-flight checklist all green
- [ ] Steps 1-3 complete; wrapper + Robust.Server healthy on pico
- [ ] Step 4 synthetic test PASSES (real IP arrives in ENUMERATE)
- [ ] Steps 5-7 complete; zig-computer ss14-watchdog stopped + disabled
- [ ] Step 8 end-to-end client test PASSES
- [ ] Step 9 ban_address shows real IP (not 100.72.47.4)
- [ ] Step 10 30-min monitoring clean (no sustained errors)
- [ ] Step 11 documentation updates pushed
- [ ] zig-zone runbook Phase 4 flipped to SHIPPED-via-C2
- [ ] dotfiles-9g1 spec bead closed
- [ ] Cutover-receipt note bead created with metrics
notes:
## CUTOVER PAUSED 2026-05-24 — wrapper-impl bug surfaced live

Steps 1-7 completed cleanly:
- pico vs14 pulled + submodule synced to azigler/RobustToolbox @ 85982545e
- Content.Server published with FullRelease + osx-arm64 + self-contained → /tmp/ss14-publish → rsync'd to /Users/pico/ss14-watchdog/instances/vacation-station/bin/
- config.toml: added [net] use_wrapper_remote_address=true + wrapper_socket=/tmp/ss14-wrapper.sock + bindto=127.0.0.1 + port=1213; [status] bind=*:1213
- watchdog appsettings ApiPort flipped 1212 → 1213
- pico watchdog loaded, Robust.Server running on 127.0.0.1:1213 (UDP) + *:1213 (TCP)
- wrapper UPSTREAM flipped 11215 → 1213 (with launchctl unload+load — kickstart -k doesn't re-read plist env vars — runbook gotcha worth)
- Synthetic UDP from zig → wrapper → ENUMERATE shows real IP 192.0.2.99 ✓
- zig watchdog stopped + disabled + Robust.Server killed
- nginx stream block at /etc/nginx/streams-enabled/ss14-game.conf added with proxy_protocol on
- nginx -t + reload OK; :1212 bound by nginx workers
- /status + /info via the pipe returned valid JSON (after flipping [status] bind to wildcard *:1213 to fix Host-header mismatch — Robust HttpListener prefix-based routing was rejecting Host: ss14.zig.computer with 127.0.0.1:1213 prefix)

Step 8 (real client connection) FAILED with handshake timeout. Root cause = wrapper-impl bug (see dotfiles-jc5):
- nginx UDP stream PROXY-protocol emits header ONCE per src-tuple session
- Wrapper code re-parses every datagram, drops if no PROXY signature
- First Lidgren handshake packet parses → session created. Subsequent packets drop → handshake stalls → timeout.

The /check OQ-03 finding ("PROXY on every datagram") was wrong — it generalized from a synthetic test that used different src ports per packet (so each was its own session, each got a header).

ROLLED BACK cleanly:
- nginx stream block removed + reload
- zig ss14-watchdog re-enabled + started
- SS14 back on zig (round 19, 0 players, /status OK)
- pico wrapper still running (idle, harmless — no traffic routed to it)
- pico Robust.Server still running (will idle out / be cleaned up by next session)
- config.toml + watchdog appsettings on pico STILL HAVE the cutover edits (not rolled back; next session can re-apply on top of the wrapper fix)

To resume: dispatch /fix on dotfiles-jc5 (full TDD wave — wrapper LookupBySrcTuple + integration test), /scrutinize, re-cutover with new wrapper binary.

title: zig-zone: private mesh + workshop/server split via Tailscale
description:
## 1. Overview

`zig-zone` is the user's private mesh — a Tailscale tailnet wrapping 5 devices into one virtual LAN regardless of physical network:

- `zig-computer` — Ubuntu VPS, public IP `51.81.33.136`, OVH KVM
- `pico` — Mac Studio M1 Max 64GB, headless, on home LAN
- `metis` — personal MacBook
- `zig` — work MacBook (subject to OQ-03 — work device policy)
- iPhone (Tailscale iOS app + Termius SSH client)

**The split this spec enables.** zig-computer becomes the **workshop + edge**: it stays the user's primary coding box (Claude Code, dotfiles, agent harness) AND retains the public surface — but the public surface narrows to just three things: nginx (TLS terminator + reverse proxy for everything), sshd on :22 (break-glass), and tailscaled. **All hostable services move to pico**: Ollama (LLM inference), `vs14-web`, the SS14 game server, the vacation-station postgres dbs, the Docker observability stack, AND `reef-router` (the granola webhook listener). nginx on zig-computer reverse-proxies inbound HTTP/UDP/TCP through the tailnet to pico. All inter-machine SSH happens primarily via Tailscale SSH.

**pico is a fresh install.** It has macOS but no `mac.setup.sh` has run, no Homebrew, no dotfiles cloned, no Tailscale. The other devices (zig-computer, metis, zig, iPhone) are already configured and only need Tailscale-bring-up + ACL alignment. So this spec includes a one-time **pico bootstrap** section (prerequisites) before the mesh phase.

**Why.** The user wants the workshop machine free from interruption — services on the same box as your active development creates risk of accidental kills, port conflicts, resource pressure mid-flow. The Mac Studio is purpose-built for sustained server load (silent, efficient, Apple Silicon GPU for inference). Plus: the M1 Max's 64GB unified memory gives a real local-LLM serving option that the OVH x86 VM can't match.

**In scope.** Pico fresh-install bootstrap (prerequisite), mesh bootstrap, ACL, the 5-phase service migration from zig-computer → pico (including reef-router), the dotfiles changes to install + configure Tailscale + Ollama on both OSes, the zig-zone skill/runbook.

**Out of scope.** LoRA fine-tuning workflow (deferred to a future spec — MLX-LM + Python venv on pico). Headscale migration (future). Subnet routing (no other home-LAN devices need exposure). Additional VPS/devices. Tailscale Funnel (we have a VPS w/ public IP already).

**Sources informing this spec.**
- Three Explore-agent research briefs run 2026-05-23 covering: Tailscale fundamentals + ACLs + SSH, VPS-as-edge w/ nginx stream{} forwarding, Mac Studio LLM stack (Ollama/MLX/LM Studio)
- `~/explore/.claude/skills/zig-computer-audit/SKILL.md` — current machine topology, services, firewall posture
- Live audit run 2026-05-23: 34 active services on zig-computer, UFW deny-default w/ 6 allow rules, fail2ban 2,573 total bans / 29 active, public ports 22/80/443/1212/1213/7575
- Tailscale docs: tailscale.com/kb (MagicDNS, ACLs, SSH, exit nodes, subnet routers, control-vs-data-plane)
- SS14 docs: docs.spacestation14.com (port-forwarding, hub registration)
- Ollama remote-access patterns: launchctl setenv OLLAMA_HOST, Tailscale-IP binding

## 2. Current State / Baseline

### 2.1 Network topology (today)

```
Internet
   ↓
zig-computer (VPS, 51.81.33.136)  ← all services live here
   • SSH :22 (LIMIT, fail2ban-protected) ← all 3 personal devices SSH here directly
   • nginx :80/:443 (linearb.zig.computer, ss14.zig.computer)
   • reef-router :7575 (granola webhook)
   • SS14 game server :1212/:1213 UDP+TCP
   • ss14-watchdog.service
   • vs14-web.service (127.0.0.1:3300, fronted by nginx)
   • postgresql@17-main.service (127.0.0.1:5432 + 172.17.0.1:5432 for docker)
   • Docker: 5 vs14 obs containers (grafana, loki, prometheus, ss14-admin, mapserver)
   • ollama.service (127.0.0.1:11434)
   • phoenix :6006 + :4317 (LLM observability)
```

pico exists but is not yet on any shared network. metis + zig + iPhone independently SSH to zig-computer over the public internet via port 22.

### 2.2 UFW state (verified 2026-05-23)

```
22/tcp           LIMIT  Anywhere       (OpenSSH)
80,443/tcp       ALLOW  Anywhere       (Nginx)
1212             ALLOW  Anywhere       (SS14 live)
1213             ALLOW  Anywhere       (SS14 dev)
7575/tcp         ALLOW  Anywhere       (reef-router/granola)
44880            ALLOW  172.18.0.0/16  (prometheus, docker-bridge scoped)
5432/tcp         ALLOW  172.17.0.0/16  (postgres, docker-bridge scoped)
```

Default deny incoming, allow outgoing, deny routed.

### 2.3 Dotfiles baseline

- `mac.setup.sh` line 5: `brew install tmux jq gh ranger ... dicklesworthstone/tap/bv` — NO `ollama`, NO `tailscale`
- `ubuntu.setup.sh`: no Tailscale install
- No `tailscale/` dir
- No zig-zone runbook
- No Ollama plist (correct — Homebrew + `brew services` handles it)

### 2.4 Why the change

The user wants:
- Light, durable, non-locked-in mesh networking (Tailscale w/ Headscale exit option preserved)
- Workshop/server discipline (coding box ≠ service box)
- Local LLM inference at zero marginal cost via pico's Apple Silicon GPU
- Reach pico from anywhere (laptops in cafés, phone) via mesh, not by port-forwarding the home router
- Eventually run longer-interval agentic loops against pico (free model, no quota pressure)

## 3. Changes and Decisions

| Decision | Why | How |
|---|---|---|
| **Adopt Tailscale free tier** (not Headscale day-one) | Easy onboarding, peer-to-peer data plane preserves privacy, Headscale is the exit ramp if ever needed (drop-in compatible). 5 devices fits the 100-device limit comfortably. | `curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh \| sh` (Ubuntu); `brew install tailscale` (macOS); App Store (iOS). `sudo tailscale up` triggers browser SSO. |
| **MagicDNS on** | `<host>.<tailnet>.ts.net` names work transparently across the mesh. SSH/nginx configs become trivial. | Default-on; tailnet DNS name picked in admin console. |
| **Tailscale SSH = primary path; sshd port 22 = break-glass** | Tailscale-only is the #1 day-one mistake on remote VPS (coordination-server lockout risk). Current sshd posture (LIMIT + fail2ban: 2,573 historic bans, 29 currently banned) is doing real work. | Enable `tailscale up --ssh` on zig-computer + pico. ACL grants SSH to `tag:user-devices`. Keep `ufw limit 22/tcp` as is. |
| **No subnet router** | User has no other home-LAN devices that need tailnet exposure right now. One-line change to add later if a NAS/Pi appears. | Skip `--advertise-routes` flag on pico. |
| **No exit node** | Not needed — VPS already has public IP; user isn't trying to hide origin or geo-shift. | Skip `--advertise-exit-node` on any device. |
| **Migrate all hostable EXTERNAL services zig-computer → pico** | Workshop/server discipline. M1 Max is a better server for everything except the public-edge role. | Phased (§ 4.4). |
| **Keep on zig-computer: nginx + sshd-break-glass + tailscaled + dev tooling (tmux, lb-fleet, lb-listener)** | nginx is the public TLS terminator and DNS landing zone; sshd stays as Tailscale-down recovery; tailscaled is the mesh client. tmux + lb-fleet + lb-listener are localhost-bound dev tools that belong with the workshop role — not user-facing services. | Don't touch these in migration; only re-point nginx upstreams to pico tailnet IPs. |
| **Migrate reef-router to pico** | The granola webhook is just an HTTP endpoint; reef-router (bun process) runs fine on macOS; nginx-on-zig-computer can `proxy_pass http://pico.<tailnet>.ts.net:7575` for it. Keeps zig-computer's "workshop + pure edge" discipline intact. Latency is fine for webhook traffic (granola is async/eventual). | Phase 4 (with the other HTTP services). The public UFW rule for :7575 stays — nginx listens on it now and forwards through the tailnet. Granola's webhook URL doesn't change. |
| **Ollama on pico binds to tailnet IP only** | Default `0.0.0.0` would expose the API to any home-LAN guest; `127.0.0.1` would block tailnet access. Tailnet-IP-only is the precise scope. | `launchctl setenv OLLAMA_HOST "$(tailscale ip -4):11434"` before `brew services start ollama`. |
| **SS14 migration is conditional** | UDP forwarding via nginx stream{} adds 10-20ms + jitter; SS14 may embed bind address in handshakes (untested per OQ-01). | Phase 4 begins with a feasibility test; spec defines abort criteria if test fails. |
| **Dotfiles additions stay light** | User's explicit preference. | New: `tailscale/acl.json`, `tailscale/README.md`, `agents/skills/zig-zone/SKILL.md`. Modified: `mac.setup.sh` (4 lines added), `ubuntu.setup.sh` (1 line added). |

## 4. Formal Specification

### 4.1 Device naming (tailnet hostnames = OS hostnames)

| Device | Tailnet name | MagicDNS | OS | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OVH VPS | `zig-computer` | `zig-computer.<tailnet>.ts.net` | Ubuntu 25.10 | workshop + edge |
| Mac Studio M1 Max 64GB | `pico` | `pico.<tailnet>.ts.net` | macOS | server farm |
| Personal MacBook | `metis` | `metis.<tailnet>.ts.net` | macOS | client |

Tailnet DNS name itself (the `<tailnet>` part) is decided in the Tailscale admin console — see OQ-04.

### 4.2 Tailscale ACL (`tailscale/acl.json`)

```jsonc
{
  // Single-user personal tailnet.
  //
  // Identity model:
  //   - `zig-computer` and `pico` are tagged `tag:server` (machine identities,
  //     no human user behind them).
  //   - `metis`, `zig`, and the iPhone are UNTAGGED — they auth as the user's
  //     Tailscale account, so they match `autogroup:member` (human-owned devices).
  //   - This separation matters: `autogroup:member` in Tailscale ACLs refers to
  //     human-owned untagged devices; tagged devices are NOT autogroup:member.
  //     Mixing the two requires explicit listing in src/dst.

  "tagOwners": {
    "tag:server": ["autogroup:admin"]   // zig-computer, pico
  },

  "acls": [
    // Server-to-server (e.g., nginx-on-zig-computer → vs14-web-on-pico via tailnet)
    { "action": "accept", "src": ["tag:server"], "dst": ["tag:server:*"] },
    // User devices to servers (SSH, Ollama API, vs14-web preview from a laptop, etc.)
    { "action": "accept", "src": ["autogroup:member"], "dst": ["tag:server:*"] },
    // User devices among themselves — use `autogroup:self` (the user's own devices)
    // because `autogroup:member` is src-only in Tailscale ACLs and would error as dst.
    // `autogroup:self` matches devices owned by the SAME user as the source — i.e.,
    // metis ↔ zig ↔ iPhone for the user's personal-account devices.
    { "action": "accept", "src": ["autogroup:member"], "dst": ["autogroup:self:*"] }
  ],

  "ssh": [
    // Tailscale SSH: user devices (metis, zig, iPhone) → server devices (zig-computer, pico).
    // `check` action requires Tailscale-identity re-auth every 12h.
    {
      "action": "check",
      "src":    ["autogroup:member"],
      "dst":    ["tag:server"],
      "users":  ["ubuntu", "autogroup:nonroot"]
    }
  ]

  // No exit nodes, no subnet routes — re-evaluate post-Phase-5.
}
```

**Tags applied per-server only.** zig-computer and pico get `--advertise-tags=tag:server` in their respective Phase 1 `tailscale up` (NOT during fresh-install bootstrap — see § 4.3 note). The user devices stay untagged and naturally match `autogroup:member` once they auth as the user's Tailscale account.

**Why this shape over `["*"]` wildcards.** Explicit src/dst pairs make the policy reviewable — if a future device joins untagged AND unauthenticated, no rule matches it and it's denied by default. A `["*"]` rule would silently grant.
