### 4.4 Migration phases

Each phase has explicit acceptance criteria (§ 5 test cases). A phase isn't done until its tests pass on the live system.

#### Prerequisites — pico fresh-install bootstrap + one-time safety checks (one-time)

pico is a fresh macOS install. Before any mesh work happens, pico needs to BE a functional server with the dotfiles environment, AND a few one-time safety checks need to happen on the other devices.

**0. One-time safety verifications (do these BEFORE pico bootstrap):**

  - **OVH KVM console access on zig-computer**: log into OVH manager, navigate to the VPS, click "KVM console," see the Ubuntu login prompt, log out. Confirms the nuclear-recovery path works AND that you know where the OVH credentials live (NOT in dotfiles — store separately, e.g. password manager). If KVM doesn't launch (Java applet, browser quirks, 2FA on a missing phone) — resolve NOW, before any change to public-SSH posture.
  - **macOS settings on pico (before mac.setup.sh runs):**
    - **FileVault**: in System Settings → Privacy & Security → FileVault, **turn OFF** (or accept that pico is unreachable for any reboot until physically present to enter password). For an in-home server, threat model justifies off.
    - **Auto-restart after power loss**: System Settings → Energy → "Start up automatically after a power failure" → ON. mac.setup.sh later adds `sudo pmset -a autorestart 1` as belt-and-suspenders.
    - **Disable macOS auto-install of updates**: System Settings → General → Software Update → Advanced → uncheck "Install macOS updates" and "Install system data files and security updates." mac.setup.sh adds `sudo softwareupdate --schedule off` as the CLI equivalent.

**1. pico bootstrap proper:**

1. Enable Remote Login (System Settings → General → Sharing → Remote Login → ON) so we can SSH in from the home LAN to drive the rest
2. Install Xcode Command Line Tools: `xcode-select --install` (interactive GUI dialog opens; let it finish before continuing)
3. Install Homebrew (the canonical bootstrap one-liner from brew.sh)
4. Clone `~/dotfiles`: `git clone https://github.com/azigler/dotfiles ~/dotfiles`
5. Run `bash ~/dotfiles/mac.setup.sh` — now includes `ollama` + `tailscale` + `colima` + `docker` + `docker-compose` in the brew line, plus the pmset + softwareupdate + plain-`tailscale up` + launchctl-setenv-OLLAMA_HOST + brew-services-start-ollama lines (see § 4.3). The full `brew install` line runs as-is even though some packages (yabai, skhd, borders, sketchybar) are UI tools that won't be useful on a headless box — acceptable for now; cleanup is a future polish, not a Prerequisites blocker.
6. Run `bash ~/dotfiles/sync.sh` (or equivalent) to symlink configs into `$HOME`
7. Verify Homebrew installed everything: `brew list | grep -E "ollama|tailscale|colima"`
8. Start Colima: `colima start` (creates the Linux VM that Docker runs in). Verify `docker info` works.
9. `mac.setup.sh` already ran `sudo tailscale up` (plain — no tags, no SSH). Browser SSO prompt opens; auth as the user's Tailscale account; pico joins the tailnet.

**Acceptance:** OVH KVM verified working; FileVault off / auto-restart on / auto-update off; pico can SSH-receive (LAN); `mac.setup.sh` ran clean; `brew services list` shows ollama (binding deferred until Phase 2); `colima status` shows running; `tailscale status` shows pico joined (untagged, no SSH yet — both come in Phase 1).

#### Phase 0 — Mesh bootstrap (no service changes)

1. Pre-generate one Tailscale auth key per device in the admin console (or use browser SSO)
2. Install Tailscale on all 5 devices (`zig-computer`, `pico`, `metis`, `zig`, iPhone)
3. `sudo tailscale up` on each (no SSH yet, no tags yet — just join the tailnet)
4. Verify `tailscale status` on each device lists all 5 peers
5. Verify MagicDNS: `ping pico.<tailnet>.ts.net` from `zig-computer` resolves
6. Verify connection type: `tailscale status` shows `direct` between `zig-computer` and `pico` (NOT `relay` — flag for investigation if so)

**Reversible:** `sudo tailscale down` on each, uninstall. No service changes yet.

#### Phase 1 — Hardening (ACL + tags + SSH enablement)

1. Commit `tailscale/acl.json` + `tailscale/README.md` to dotfiles
2. Paste `tailscale/acl.json` into Tailscale admin → Access Controls → Save. Verify policy compiles (Tailscale's editor shows red-underline on errors).
3. Re-run on the servers: `sudo tailscale up --ssh --advertise-tags=tag:server` on `zig-computer`; same on `pico`. (NOW the tag is permitted because `tagOwners` exists in the ACL.)
4. User devices DON'T get tags. On `metis`, `zig`, iPhone: re-run `tailscale up --ssh` (or just `tailscale set --ssh=true`) to enable Tailscale SSH from those devices to the servers. They naturally match `autogroup:member` once authenticated.
5. Test (TC04): `tailscale ssh ubuntu@zig-computer.<tailnet>.ts.net` from `metis` succeeds
6. Test: `tailscale ping zig-computer` from `pico` succeeds (server-to-server reachability)
7. Test (TC05): existing `ssh ubuntu@51.81.33.136` on port 22 still works (break-glass intact)

Per OQ-02 (decided): leave `ufw limit 22/tcp` as-is. No IP allowlist tightening.

#### Phase 2 — Ollama + Phoenix migration

Ollama + Phoenix move as one wave to keep trace data co-located with the model that produces it (no cross-tailnet trace traffic).

1. On `pico`: `brew install ollama` (if not yet), `launchctl setenv OLLAMA_HOST "$(tailscale ip -4):11434"`, `brew services start ollama`
2. `ollama pull llama3.2:3b` (smoke-test model) + `ollama pull qwen2.5:7b` (real model)
3. On `pico`: install Phoenix (`pip install arize-phoenix` or `uv pip install arize-phoenix`), start it bound to tailnet IP, gRPC on the same `:4317` it uses today
4. From `zig-computer`: `curl http://pico.<tailnet>.ts.net:11434/api/tags` returns 200 with model list
5. From `zig-computer`: `curl http://pico.<tailnet>.ts.net:6006` returns the Phoenix UI
6. On `zig-computer`: `sudo systemctl stop ollama lb-phoenix && sudo systemctl disable ollama lb-phoenix`
7. Verify on `zig-computer`: `curl http://localhost:11434/api/tags` returns connection-refused; `curl http://localhost:6006` returns connection-refused
8. Update any client config (Claude Code, agentic loops, OTEL env vars `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`) to point at `http://pico.<tailnet>.ts.net:11434` and `http://pico.<tailnet>.ts.net:4317` respectively

#### Phase 3 — vs14-web + postgres + observability containers + reef-router + project timers

All HTTP/TCP-only services in one wave. They share the migration pattern: stop on zig-computer, run on pico bound to the tailnet IP (per OQ-05 decision), point nginx upstream at `pico.<tailnet>.ts.net:<port>`, **wait for in-flight connections to drain (`sleep 60`)**, then stop the old.

1. **Postgres**: on `pico`, `brew install postgresql@17`, `brew services start postgresql@17`. **Postgres is the explicit exception to OQ-05** — it stays bound to `127.0.0.1` (Homebrew default), NOT to the tailnet IP, because the only consumers (vs14-web, mapserver container via host.docker.internal) are co-located on pico. TC11 verifies this is intentional, not an oversight. From zig-computer, dump both DBs: `pg_dump -h localhost -U <user> vacation_station > /tmp/vs.sql` + same for `vacation_station_mapserver`. Transfer via tailnet: `scp /tmp/*.sql ubuntu@pico.<tailnet>.ts.net:/tmp/`. On pico: `createdb vacation_station vacation_station_mapserver`, `psql vacation_station < /tmp/vs.sql`, same for mapserver. Also recreate any roles/passwords (`pg_dumpall --roles-only`) and adjust `pg_hba.conf` on pico to match access policy. **Step 1 must complete before step 2** — mapserver container in step 2 connects to this postgres.
2. **Docker via Colima**: on `pico`, `colima start` (if not already). Transfer the 5 obs container compose files + data volumes from zig-computer (`scp -r ~/vacation-station-14/docker/* ubuntu@pico.<tailnet>.ts.net:~/vacation-station-14/docker/` — adjust paths to actual layout). Verify volume data integrity.
3. **Critical postgres-bridge fix**: on Linux, the mapserver container connected to host postgres at `172.17.0.1:5432` (docker0 bridge gateway). **Colima on macOS does NOT have `172.17.0.1`.** Update the mapserver container's connection string env (`DATABASE_URL` or equivalent) from `172.17.0.1:5432` → `host.docker.internal:5432`. Verify from inside the container: `docker exec mapserver psql -h host.docker.internal -U <user> -d vacation_station_mapserver -c '\dt'`.
4. **Project timers** (8 known per audit skill § 6 "Periodic timers worth knowing"):

   | Timer | Purpose | Suggested launchd schedule |
   |---|---|---|
   | `ss14-backup.timer` | Daily Postgres backup of vacation_station | daily 04:00 |
   | `ss14-replay-rotate.timer` | Rotate game replays | daily 03:30 |
   | `vs14-postgres-retention.timer` | Postgres retention sweep | daily 04:30 |
   | `vs14-cookbook-build.timer` | Build cookbook content | weekly Sunday |
   | `vs14-guidebook-build.timer` | Build guidebook content | weekly Sunday |
   | `vs14-nurseshark-build.timer` | Build nurseshark content | weekly Sunday |
   | `vs14-writer-build.timer` | Build writer content | weekly Sunday |
   | `vs14-map-render.timer` | Render maps | weekly Sunday |

   Confirm the exact `OnCalendar=` schedules with `systemctl cat <timer>` before porting — the table is a starting point, not authoritative.

   **launchd translation cost**: macOS `launchd` does NOT have a direct `OnCalendar=daily` equivalent. The `StartCalendarInterval` key takes a dictionary per fire-time (or an array of dictionaries for multiple times). Budget extra time per timer for the translation; `cron` is the lighter-weight alternative if scheduling is simple (daily/weekly at a fixed time). Port each timer's underlying script to pico first, then schedule. Disable on zig-computer once the pico equivalents are running: `sudo systemctl disable --now <list-of-timers>`.
5. **reef-router**: on `pico`, `git clone <reef-remote-url> ~/linearb/reef` (it IS a real remote-tracked repo — verify with `git -C ~/linearb/reef remote -v`). Then `cd ~/linearb/reef && bun install`. **Transfer secrets out-of-band**: scp `~/linearb/reef/.env.local` AND `~/linearb/reef/polyps/router/.env.local` from zig-computer to pico (they're gitignored; clone doesn't carry them). Then start `next start -H $(tailscale ip -4) -p 3300`. Verify via tailnet from zig-computer: `curl -I http://pico.<tailnet>.ts.net:3300`.

Add a new server block listening on `:7575` (both ipv4 and ipv6) that `proxy_pass http://pico.<tailnet>.ts.net:7575` for the granola webhook. #### Phase 4 — SS14 game server (conditional on feasibility test)

**Cut-over must happen in a known no-players window** — UDP streams don't drain cleanly via nginx, and any current player gets disconnected instantly. Schedule for low-activity time.

**Performance baseline (recommended before this phase starts):** play-test the current SS14 server on zig-computer for ~10 minutes; note subjective latency / smoothness. After Phase 4 step 5, play-test the pico-hosted version and compare. If pico-via-tailnet feels equivalent or better, the architecture is validated.

1. On `pico`: install SS14 server + watchdog into `/opt/ss14-watchdog/` per upstream docs (will likely need a launchd plist instead of systemd; mirror the watchdog config)
2. Configure SS14 to bind `0.0.0.0:1212` (test the simpler bind first; switch to tailnet-IP if leaked-address test fails)
3. On `zig-computer`: write nginx stream{} config:
   ```nginx
   stream {
       upstream ss14_udp { server pico.<tailnet>.ts.net:1212; }
       server { listen 1212 udp reuseport; proxy_pass ss14_udp; proxy_timeout 30s; }
       upstream ss14_tcp { server pico.<tailnet>.ts.net:1212; }
       server { listen 1212; proxy_pass ss14_tcp; }
   }
   ```
4. `sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx`
5. **Feasibility test:** stop the SS14 game server on `zig-computer`; have a real client connect to `ss14.zig.computer:1212` (or the public IP); play for 5+ minutes; on the CLIENT machine, run `tcpdump -n host pico.<tailnet>.ts.net or 'src net 100.0.0.0/8'` and verify NO packets target tailnet hostnames or IPs (any such packets would indicate SS14 leaked its bind address — see OQ-01)
6. **If test passes:** proceed — disable `ss14-watchdog.service` on `zig-computer`, leave the nginx stream{} forwarding live, port the `ss14-backup.timer` and `ss14-replay-rotate.timer` to launchd on pico
7. **If test fails:** abort SS14 migration. SS14 stays on `zig-computer`. The nginx stream{} block is removed. Update spec with findings (file `ss14-migration-failed` note bead). Other migrations (Ollama, Phoenix, vs14-web, etc.) are independent and stand.

#### Phase 5 — Done state verification

Final state asserted by tests TC14 + TC15 (§ 5). On `zig-computer`:

**System services running**: edge surface (nginx, sshd, fail2ban), system services (systemd-*, dbus, cron, ufw, unattended-upgrades, qemu-guest-agent, etc.), tailscaled.

**User services running (dev tooling — explicit "stays here"):** `tmux.service` (keeps the user's tmux session alive), `lb-fleet.service` (lb-agent-fleet dev server on 127.0.0.1:7100 — internal/localhost), `lb-listener.service` (lb-agent-listener dev server on 127.0.0.1:7102 — internal/localhost). These are NOT external services and stay on zig-computer as part of the workshop environment. **Future consideration**: revisit moving lb-fleet / lb-listener to pico in a later spec once the user's workflow patterns stabilize — both are currently localhost-bound dev tooling, not user-facing servers, so the workshop/server discipline applies less strictly.

**NOT running on zig-computer**: `ss14-*`, `vs14-*`, `postgresql@*`, `ollama`, `reef-router`, `lb-phoenix`, vs14 docker workload containers. Public ports 1212/1213/7575 are now handled by nginx + nginx stream{} proxying to pico.

**Dual-stack edge preserved.** zig-computer's nginx still listens on `[::]:443` and `0.0.0.0:443` (and ditto for 80, 7575); IPv6 inbound traffic terminates at the edge and the tailnet upstream connection to pico is v4-only via `pico.<tailnet>.ts.net` (Tailscale assigns `100.x.y.z` v4 addresses by default). No DNS-record changes needed.

### 4.5 Failure conditions + recovery

| Failure | Symptom | Recovery |
|---|---|---|
| Tailscale coordination server down | New SSH sessions via `tailscale ssh` fail to authenticate | Fall back to `ssh ubuntu@51.81.33.136` (LIMITed sshd is intact); existing sessions stay live |
| pico tailscaled crashes / Mac reboots | nginx upstream `pico.<tailnet>.ts.net` unreachable; vs14-web + SS14 + Ollama all 502/timeout | `brew services restart tailscale` on pico (or full reboot — LaunchDaemon brings it back); nginx upstream auto-recovers on next request |
| Home ISP outage / CGNAT relay fallback | Latency to pico spikes from 5ms → 30ms+; SS14 players notice; Ollama still works but slower | No fast fix; ride out outage. If chronic, investigate Tailscale DERP relay region selection or ISP change |
| OVH VPS rebooted / public IP changes | DNS still points at old IP; all public traffic dead | OVH KVM console; check `ip addr`; update DNS A records if IP changed (rare) |
| Locked out entirely (Tailscale + sshd both unreachable) | Can't reach `zig-computer` at all | OVH KVM web console (documented in zig-zone skill); break-glass user/password reset path |
| Auth key compromise | Unknown device joins tailnet | Tailscale admin console: revoke key, audit log shows affected devices, force re-auth |

```
EXPECTED: keys are local files; documented in zig-zone skill as part of recovery
RATIONALE: confirms not-locked-in property; if Tailscale Inc. ever becomes hostile, keys can move to Headscale
```

## 6. Open Questions

- **OQ-01 (P1): Does SS14 / Robust Toolbox engine embed its bind address in network handshakes or hub-advertise calls?**
  - DECIDED 2026-05-23: test-driven — Phase 4 step 5 is the feasibility test. **Abort criterion**: if any client packets target `*.ts.net` hostnames during the 5-minute play session, SS14 stays on zig-computer permanently (or moves only via a different mechanism — WireGuard direct, FRP, etc. — out of scope for this spec). The other phases (Ollama, Phoenix, vs14, postgres, obs, reef-router) are independent and complete regardless of SS14 outcome.
  - Affects: Phase 4 (decisive, but isolated)

- **OQ-02 (P1): Is your home/office public IP stable enough to allowlist on port 22?**
  - DECIDED 2026-05-23: keep `ufw limit 22/tcp` + fail2ban (current state). No IP allowlist. Existing posture catches enough (2,573 bans / 29 currently banned) and doesn't depend on a stable home IP. Phase 1 step 8 is dropped.
  - Affects: Phase 1 simplified

- **OQ-03 (P2): Does the work laptop (`zig`) allow installing Tailscale per your employer's device-management policy?**
  - DECIDED 2026-05-23: yes, allowed. `zig` joins the tailnet as `tag:client` like `metis`. Tailscale SSH works from both.
  - Affects: ACL roster confirmed at 5 devices

- **OQ-04 (P2): What tailnet DNS name should we pick?**
  - DECIDED 2026-05-23: aspirational target = `zig-zone.ts.net`. If taken when the user is in the admin console, fall back to whatever's available in Tailscale's picker. Spec keeps `<tailnet>.ts.net` placeholder syntax in all URLs until the actual name is locked.
  - Affects: cosmetics only; the spec doesn't change behavior either way

- **OQ-05 (P2): Should the HTTP services on pico (vs14-web, reef-router) bind to `127.0.0.1:<port>` or to pico's tailnet IP?**
  - DECIDED 2026-05-23: Option B — direct tailnet-IP bind. Same pattern as Ollama's `OLLAMA_HOST=$(tailscale ip -4):11434`. No local nginx on pico. Tailnet is the trust boundary.
  - Affects: Phase 3 confirmed

- **OQ-06 (P3): Phoenix observability (`*:4317` gRPC on zig-computer — currently UFW-protected) — does it migrate to pico in Phase 3, or stay on zig-computer?**
  - DECIDED 2026-05-23: migrates to pico **in Phase 2** alongside Ollama (option "with Ollama"). Keeps Ollama traces local to pico — no cross-tailnet trace traffic per request. Phase 2 description updated to include Phoenix bring-up steps.
  - Affects: Phase 2 scope expanded

- **OQ-07 (P3): Should we set up Tailscale's HTTPS cert for `pico.<tailnet>.ts.net` (`tailscale cert`) so internal traffic VPS→pico is TLS-encrypted on top of WireGuard?**
  - DECIDED 2026-05-23: NO. WireGuard already encrypts the underlying link. Belt-and-suspenders with no real threat-model benefit. Revisit only if a future app demands HTTPS upstream.
  - Affects: nothing day-one

## 7. Future Considerations

- **Move lb-fleet + lb-listener to pico (or retire them)** — currently localhost-bound dev tools on zig-computer. If the user's workflow shifts toward agentic loops running entirely on pico (with the workshop just sending prompts), these tools become more useful on pico than on zig-computer. Defer until workflow patterns stabilize. Out of zig-zone Phase 5 scope.
- **Fine-tuning workflow** — separate spec. Add MLX-LM + a Python venv on pico, LaunchDaemon for `mlx_lm.server` if we want a second always-on inference endpoint, dotfiles entry for the venv requirements. Estimated complexity: small spec, ~3 phases.
- **Headscale migration** — if Tailscale Inc. ever changes pricing/policy. The dotfiles work is mostly the same; only the coordination server URL changes. Devices keep their WireGuard keys; you redirect them at `headscale.zig.computer` (a service on zig-computer's edge nginx).
- **Subnet routing** — if a NAS/Pi/Home Assistant box appears on the home LAN, advertise `192.168.x.0/24` via `tailscale up --advertise-routes`. One-line change.
- **Exit node** — if you want to route phone/laptop traffic through home for geo or trust reasons. `tailscale up --advertise-exit-node` on pico (or zig-computer).
- **Additional VPS** — if you want geographic redundancy on the edge, a second VPS with its own public IP joining the tailnet as `corsair` (different cloud, different country). nginx vhosts mirror.
- **Tailscale Funnel** — if you want to expose a single pico service publicly without going through zig-computer (rare — you have zig-computer for that). Per-service decision.
- **Per-service ACL refinement** — current ACL is full mesh among autogroup:member. If you ever add a household member or a contractor to the tailnet, the ACL becomes more granular per `tag:server`/`tag:client` and per-port.
- **Audit logging** — Tailscale paid tier offers audit logs. Free tier doesn't. If audit becomes important, that's the upgrade trigger.

ACL ssh section was extended with a second rule allowing tag:server → tag:server SSH (zig-computer ↔ pico) — discovered during Phase 1 testing as a real workflow gap. The user lives on zig-computer (workshop) and needs to reach pico for ops without a laptop hop. /scrutinize rounds reviewed the spec's documented intent (client→server) and didn't flag the server→server omission because it wasn't in the documented requirements; this came up the first time the user actually tried it.

## Post-spec architectural finding — 2026-05-24 (Phase 1)

**Tag**: this changes a load-bearing assumption in the spec without changing the user-facing intent. Not a supersession; an implementation constraint discovered late.

**Finding**: spec § 4 assumed both pico and zig-computer could run as Tailscale SSH servers AND have MagicDNS for outbound queries. **On macOS, this is fundamentally impossible.** The three Tailscale install variants are mutually exclusive on this feature pair:
- brew formula (CLI/headless tailscaled): SSH server YES, MagicDNS NO (userspace networking)
- Mac App Store: SSH server NO (sandboxed), MagicDNS YES
- "Standalone" .pkg / brew cask: SSH server NO (also sandboxed, despite the naming), MagicDNS YES

**Why /scrutinize missed it**: 3 rounds reviewed the spec's documented intent ("Tailscale SSH is the primary inter-machine SSH path") but didn't actually install the brew formula and try to use MagicDNS outbound from the same host. The constraint is operational, not a spec-stated requirement.

**Resolution** (in scope; doesn't break any spec section, refines § 4):
- pico uses the brew FORMULA → Tailscale SSH server works (clients ssh INTO pico via Tailscale identity, ACL-gated)
- pico's outbound MagicDNS works around with the /etc/hosts shim + the `ssh-zig` / `ssh-pico` aliases that bypass DNS via `tailscale ip -4 <host>` (bead dotfiles-tc1 added the aliases to ~/dotfiles/bash/.bash_aliases)
- For future workstation Macs (metis-style): use cask/App Store variant — opposite trade-off but right for client role

**Documentation trail**:
- Runbook gotcha #12: ~/explore/.claude/skills/zig-zone/SKILL.md (explore commit b1881d6)
- Runbook gotcha #13 (stale /usr/local/bin shims after Standalone uninstall): same commit
- mac.setup.sh comment block: ~/dotfiles/mac.setup.sh (commit 2e2965f)
- SSH aliases: ~/dotfiles/bash/.bash_aliases (commit 15a19b4, bead dotfiles-tc1)

Spec § 4.4 Phase 1 "Tailscale SSH from any device" intent stands; the implementation is per-role variant + workaround for the server side.

title: bug: /daemon's detached best-effort trigger reports success with nobody reading the spawn's outcome
description:
Flagged by the agent that improved /daemon (2026-07-26), as something now WRONG
rather than merely incomplete — and it is right.

THE TENSION: the skill's FULL-STACK-trigger section tells you to `setsid` the
pulse-inject.sh call and return in under a second. That IS correct for the
daemon's hot path. But nothing then reads the detached spawn's outcome: if the
cold boot fails, **the daemon has already reported success.**

That makes the trigger section an instance of the very class the skill's new
"dominant failure class" section documents (dotfiles-cxle) — which is why it
matters more than a doc nit: six new daemons are about to be bootstrapped from
this skill.

THE STATED BACKSTOP IS UNENFORCED. The skill says "a later event or a periodic
drain re-fires." That safety depends on a periodic drain EXISTING — and the skill
never requires you to build one, nor asserts it in the go-live sequence. So the
backstop is a parenthetical, not a guarantee.

FIX (the flagging agent's proposal, which I endorse):
1. The detached spawn writes a verdict line — `spawned` / `deferred-modal` /
   `failed` — somewhere the drain or the ledger reads. That makes the fire-and-
   forget observable without putting it back in the hot path.
2. "A periodic drain exists" becomes an ASSERTED item in the go-live sequence,
   not a parenthetical. If there is no drain, the trigger is not safe to detach.

NOT fixed in the improvement pass deliberately: detaching really is correct, and
rewriting that section risked deleting hard-won structure. This is the follow-up.

Relates: dotfiles-cxle (the class), and the /daemon go-live sequence.

title: vps-repo-refresh: bash 3.2 incompatible — dies on unbound array expansion, so its suite is 54-FAIL on macOS
description:
## Context

`agents/scheduler/vps-repo-refresh.sh:310` dies under macOS's `/bin/bash` (3.2.57) with
`SUBS[@]: unbound variable`. Under `set -u`, bash 3.2 treats an empty array's `${a[@]}` as
unbound; bash 4+ does not. There are roughly **15 `${a[@]}` sites** in the script with the
same exposure.

Consequence: `agents/scheduler/test-vps-repo-refresh.sh` is **54-FAIL on macOS both before
and after** the `dotfiles-ren9` patch — the script under test never gets far enough for the
test's own fix to matter. On Linux the suite is 90 pass / 0 fail either way.

This is why the `dotfiles-ren9` vps half could not land: its `sed -i` fix is correct but
unverifiable from a Mac, and `tools/githooks/pre-commit` rightly refuses a commit to a
red suite.

**Saved hunk:** `/tmp/ren9-vps-hunk.patch` — regenerate rather than trust it if `/tmp` has
been cleared since 2026-08-01.

## Steps to Reproduce

On macOS:

```bash
bash agents/scheduler/test-vps-repo-refresh.sh   # 54 FAIL, from case 1
bash --version                                    # 3.2.57 for /bin/bash
```

Minimal demonstration of the underlying difference:

```bash
/bin/bash -uc 'a=(); echo "${a[@]}"'   # bash 3.2: unbound variable
bash -uc 'a=(); echo "${a[@]}"'        # bash 5.x (brew): fine
```

## Fix direction

Two options, pick deliberately:

1. Make it bash-3.2-safe — `${a[@]+"${a[@]}"}` at each site. Portable but noisy, and easy
   to reintroduce at site 16.
2. Require bash 4+ explicitly — a shebang/guard that fails loudly on 3.2 rather than dying
   mid-run with a confusing message. Legitimate if this script is Linux-only by design.

Note the second is defensible: this script refreshes a VPS checkout and may never be
intended to run from a Mac. But that intent is currently **undocumented**, and the failure
mode is a cryptic unbound-variable death rather than a clear "needs bash 4".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] decide and record: bash-3.2-safe, or bash-4-required-and-says-so
- [ ] `test-vps-repo-refresh.sh` either passes on macOS or skips with a clear stated reason
- [ ] the `dotfiles-ren9` vps hunk lands once the suite is unblocked
- [ ] other `agents/scheduler/` scripts checked for the same bash-4 assumption

title: pulse: a done-proof should be watched FAILING before it is trusted — the skill never says so
description:
## Context

`/pulse`'s SKILL.md mentions `proof` **17 times** and never once says to watch one
fail. It reasons carefully about verifier *distance* (cmd vs scrutinize, why
`artifact`/`commit` are rejected, why a cmd whose clauses only re-read the tick's
own output is `artifact` wearing a permitted label) — all of which is about
whether a proof *could* catch a defect, and none of which is about whether anyone
has *seen* it catch one.

Those are different properties, and the second is cheap to check.

## Evidence this matters

**investd, 2026-08-01 (`rebalance-tradfi`).** The row's first proof token asserted
`count(*) >= 8` over *any* ticker refreshed today. It passed — **for the wrong
reason**: 8 tickers had been fetched, but they were not the 8 held, and one was a
day stale. A proof that can pass while the thing it claims is false is not a
proof. It was caught only because that session happened to run it against a
deliberately-broken state first.

**investd, 2026-08-02 (`rebalance-defi`).** Applied deliberately. The new token was
verified failing on three constructed cases — no credential, an asset not held,
and an injected `LEGACY_ASSET_CODES` mis-normalization — before being trusted. The
third is the one that matters: an independent `/scrutinize` had just demonstrated
that the *original* reconciliation reported a **45.978 BTC** book (vs 0.17027) as
green at 0.0000bps, because its two "independent" legs shared one mapping. A proof
built on that reconciliation would have been re-runnable, well-shaped, correctly
`kind:cmd` — and permanently wrong.

Distance did not catch that. A negative control did.

## Proposal (fleet-wide, hence proposed not edited)

Add to the proof section: **before a proof token is used for the first time,
construct a state where the claim is FALSE and watch the token fail.** Record the
observed failure in the ledger note alongside the pass. If a failing state cannot
be constructed, that is itself the finding — the proof probably asserts something
that cannot be false.

Cheap: it is one extra run at token-authoring time, never per-tick.

Suggested placement: right after the "a cmd proof's CONTENT must have distance
too" paragraph, since it is the same failure family — that paragraph rules out
proofs that *cannot* catch anything; this rules out proofs that merely *happen not
to*.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Rule written into `~/dotfiles/agents/skills/pulse/SKILL.md`.
- [ ] `TOOLKIT.md`'s `/pulse` entry updated (post-write-skill.sh nudges this).
- [ ] Both investd instances cited as the worked examples.

title: hooks: pre-commit-checks Bead-trailer carve-out misses :outbox_tray: (distribute)
description:
## Problem
pre-commit-checks.sh's Bead-trailer block (shipped in dotfiles-5q1)
exempts meta-commits by gitmoji — :card_file_box: / :broom: / :dollar:
— but misses :outbox_tray:, the gitmoji /distribute uses for
harness-sync commits. A `:outbox_tray: distribute: sync from dotfiles`
commit has no owning bead and is wrongly blocked.

## Symptom
Caught immediately: the /distribute sync commit to ~/linearb/skills
this session is blocked by the hook just shipped in dotfiles-5q1.

## Cause
The carve-out gitmoji alternation was incomplete — :outbox_tray: was
overlooked when enumerating meta-commit classes.

## Fix
Add :outbox_tray: to the carve-out alternation; cover it with a test
case. (This is the "carve-out must be maintained" cost the hooks

title: pulse-inject: no verdict marker — exit 0 on paths that inject NOTHING
description:
## Context
`agents/scheduler/pulse-inject.sh` is the fleet's injection primitive. It has NO
verdict marker on any terminal path, and it exits 0 on at least two paths where it
typed nothing at all:

  - line ~326  `BOUNCED: input-ready marker not seen … NOT injecting` -> exit 0
  - line ~350  `deferred: window … blocked on Andrew (🔔) … not injecting` -> exit 0

Both are CORRECT for /pulse, whose contract is "the next timer retries." They are
silently wrong for any ONE-SHOT consumer, which has no next timer. Every consumer
today can only read the exit code, so none can tell "the agent received the
command" from "nothing was typed."

This is the fleet's #1 defect shape (dotfiles-cxle, "the reporter keeps saying
success") living inside the primitive that the /daemon skill tells every daemon to
delegate to.

Live instance, picod (2026-07-26): the ha-portal 🛎️ button dispatches through this
script. A stale --window sent the injection into a newly-created window with a
cold-booted second agent; pulse-inject exited 0; the daemon reported success and
filed no notification. Separately, a 🔔-blocked operator window would have dropped
the homeowner's press entirely — daemon shows "Thinking…" for 8 minutes, then
nothing, no notification, no retry.

picod has since built its OWN verification (bd-u15: parse the bounce ledger + probe
tmux). That is a per-consumer workaround for a primitive-level gap. A verdict
marker fixes it once, for everyone.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. `grep -n 'exit 0' agents/scheduler/pulse-inject.sh` — note the bounce (~328) and
   defer (~357) paths alongside the success path (~400).
2. `grep -c 'RESULT=' agents/scheduler/pulse-inject.sh` -> 0. No marker anywhere.
3. Invoke it against a window whose session is 🔔-blocked: it logs `deferred: …`,
   types nothing, and exits 0 — indistinguishable to the caller from a delivered
   injection.
4. `record_bounce()` (line ~152) DOES record bounce/defer, but returns early unless
   `--loop` was passed (`[ -n "$LOOP" ] || return 0`), so a consumer that does not
   pass --loop gets no trace at all.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every terminal path prints exactly one `PULSE_INJECT_RESULT=<verdict>` line to
  stdout, verdicts drawn from a small documented set that distinguishes AT MINIMUM:
  injected / bounced-not-ready / deferred-blocked-on-human / failed (+ whatever the
  existing early `exit 64/66/69` argument-and-environment paths need)
- The marker is the LAST line of stdout and its format is documented in the script
  header, so a consumer can parse it without guessing
- Exit codes are UNCHANGED — this is purely additive. No existing /pulse unit, and
  no existing consumer, may change behaviour.
- `agents/scheduler/test-pulse-inject.sh` gains coverage asserting the marker on
  every terminal path, including the two silent exit-0 paths
- NEGATIVE CONTROL recorded in the bead: delete the marker from one terminal path,
  run the suite, watch it FAIL. A test that passes with the thing it guards removed
  is not a test.
- The `/daemon` skill's reporting-contract section gains a line pointing consumers
  at the marker (it already prescribes exactly this shape for other scripts)

title: pulse-inject: defer+bounce when target pane is in choose-tree/copy-mode (pane_in_mode), not just 🔔 — send-keys eaten by the tmux modal (2026-07-08 lost-ticks)
description:
pulse-inject.sh §3.5 modal-safety guard only defers when the tmux WINDOW NAME is prefixed 🔔 (blocked on an AskUserQuestion). It does NOT detect a tmux-level PANE MODE — choose-tree (the session/window chooser), copy-mode, view-mode — where send-keys is consumed by the modal UI, not the Claude composer.

INCIDENT (2026-07-08): the 00:00 PT pulse-explore tick, the 07:00 PT daily-digest, and the 07:00 PT pulse-di-wednesday tick all logged "injected into @<pane>" (exit 0) but NEVER RAN — Zig was parked in the tmux session-chooser (choose-tree) view, so the keystrokes went into the chooser, not the composer. No ledger rows, no bounce records. Confirmed fixed the moment he exited the chooser and we re-fired via systemctl.

FIX: before the send-keys inject (after the existing 🔔 check), also query the target pane mode and DEFER+BOUNCE (same path as the 🔔 defer: log, record {"reason":"pane_in_mode"} to pulse-bounces.jsonl when --loop is set, exit 0) if the pane is in a mode that eats keys. tmux exposes this: `tmux display-message -p -t "$PANE" "#{pane_in_mode}"` (1 = in copy/view/choose mode); optionally `#{pane_mode}` for the specific mode name. choose-tree/choose-client/choose-buffer all set pane_in_mode=1.

REGRESSION TEST (test-pulse-inject.sh): put the launch pane into copy-mode (or choose-tree), run the injector, assert (a) NO send-keys of the cmd reached the pane, (b) a "deferred: ... pane in mode" log line, (c) a bounce row when --loop is passed. Mirror the existing 🔔-defer test.

ACCEPTANCE: pane_in_mode=1 -> tick deferred, bounce recorded, exit 0, next timer retries; pane_in_mode=0 -> injects as before. Extends the tested behavior contract (§3.5) so the guard covers tmux pane-modal state, not just the 🔔 window-name state.

title: task: no aggregate hook-test runner — a new hook ships untested and nobody notices
description:
Found 2026-07-26 while fixing explore-yfn4. Left alone as out of scope; filing it
because it is the reason that bug survived.

THE GAP: agents/hooks/test/ has no runner. Tests are discovered only by the
test-*.sh naming convention, and nothing runs them as a set. So a new hook can
ship with ZERO coverage and nothing reports it.

THAT IS EXACTLY WHAT HAPPENED: pre-bash-stderr-guard.sh ran for ~3 weeks as a
live PreToolUse gate on EVERY Bash call in the fleet, with no tests at all. Its
false-positive was found by agents stumbling over it, not by a check.

This is dotfiles-cxle's class one level up: the absence of a test is itself
silent. Nothing said "this hook is untested"; it just looked fine.

FIX: a four-line runner over agents/hooks/test/test-*.sh, called from CI or the
task-completed hook. Cheap, and it converts "untested" from invisible to loud.

Worth pairing with a second check: every file in agents/hooks/*.sh has a
corresponding test-*.sh, failing loudly when one does not. That is the check that
would have caught this specific case on the day the hook landed.

Relates: explore-yfn4 (closed), dotfiles-cxle.

title: decision: Opus-5 refactor thesis + authority grant (2026-07-25)
description:
Context: Zig opened a marathon session on the day the harness moved from Opus 4.8
to Opus 5 (1M ctx). Two things were settled at the top of it.

AUTHORITY GRANTED (Zig, explicit):
"Fix freely, propose live-loop changes" — the orchestrator autonomously fixes
skills, hooks, docs, dead units and bugs, filing a -t decision bead per
non-trivial call; anything that changes a LIVE pulse schedule, a running daemon,
nginx, or pico requires an AskUserQuestion FIRST. This is the propose-and-proceed
rung of the escalation ladder already in AGENTS.md.

THE PAIN, per Zig — he selected ALL FOUR offered options plus a fifth in prose:
  1. output he never reads (comprehension rot)
  2. rate-limit / token cost pressure
  3. nothing compounds (explorations standalone; no synthesis, no retrieval)
  4. too much ceremony per unit of work
  5. "want more synergy between me and my agents now that we have built this
     harness app which likely needs a refactor. many things likely need
     refactors, there are many opportunities to simplify to make our loops more
     harmonious and compounding."

READING: these are not four problems, they are one loop failing to close.
  ceremony -> each tick is expensive -> cost caps throughput
  context-isolated ticks -> no cross-tick memory -> nothing compounds
  no synthesis -> raw output accumulates -> Zig can't read it -> no steering
  no steering -> the loop runs open-loop -> no synergy
The fix has to attack the CYCLE, not any single arc of it.

THE OPUS-5 THESIS (the orchestrator's framing, endorsed by Zig as "good analysis"):
A large fraction of this harness is CONTEXT-SCARCITY ENGINEERING — TOOLKIT.md
exists because full skill bodies measured 75-85k/session; the bead-hygiene rule
bans `br list --json` at ~60k; session-start truncates 137 beads to 12; the 85%
guard, per-window handoffs, offboard-before-compaction. That constraint just got
~8x weaker. But the REAL bottlenecks (rate-limit headroom, Zig's review
bandwidth) did not move.

So the refactor direction is NOT "use more context". It is: spend the freed
context on FEWER, DEEPER sessions instead of many shallow ones. A tick that can
hold 200 beads + 40 FINDINGS at once can SYNTHESIZE across them — the thing the
zettelkasten currently never does — at similar token spend.

NUANCE TO PRESERVE: the bead-hygiene rule has TWO stated reasons — context cost
AND over-anchoring (an agent that ingests 100 bead bodies reflexively ties every
new exploration back to the same handful). Reason 1 is now largely obsolete;
reason 2 is NOT, and may worsen with a bigger window. Keep the rule, rewrite its
WHY. Do not relax a rule just because one of its two justifications expired.

Reversibility: this is a framing/authority record, not a code change. Every
change made under it is individually reverted by git; live-loop changes are
gated behind a separate approval.

title: MIGRATION REGRESSION: dropping --row deleted the time-of-day half of Monday's routing — two units now swap rows
description:
## Context
Introduced 2026-08-05 by the pulse cutover (dotfiles-1n50), lands **Monday 2026-08-10**.
Found by the cutover agent, verified independently by the orchestrator.

Under the remote conduit each unit passed `--row <name>`, so `pulse-biweekly-content`
ran biweekly-content and `pulse-di-monday` ran di-monday, at 08:00 and 10:00 PT. The
local form drops `--row`: `/pulse tick` now "evaluates rows by priority; the first
satisfied row fires" (pulse SKILL.md step 3).

## Steps to Reproduce
    grep -oE "date \+%[uH][^]]*" ~/linearb/dashboard-dev-interrupted/refs/pulse.md | sort -u
      -> only  date +%u)" = 1 .. = 5      # NO check anywhere tests time-of-day

    grep -nE "^\| *2 *\| *(di-monday|biweekly-content)" .../refs/pulse.md
      -> 33: | 2 | di-monday        | time: Mon 10:00 PT | [ ... date +%u = 1 ]
      -> 34: | 2 | biweekly-content | time: Mon 08:00 PT | [ ... date +%u = 1 ] && bun ... check

Both priority 2, both check only the DAY, di-monday first in table order. So on any
Monday BOTH units select di-monday.

## What actually happens Monday
- 08:00 — the `biweekly-content` UNIT fires, evaluates, and runs **di-monday**.
- 10:00 — the `di-monday` UNIT fires, finds di-monday capped, falls through to
  **biweekly-content**.

The rows SWAP UNITS, inverting the biweekly timer own stated reason for existing at
08:00. The trigger column becomes a lie.

## Two ways the cap does not save it
1. It only absorbs the same-row double-fire if the 08:00 tick writes `done` before
   10:00. Measured over 30 `done` rows: median lag 19 min, but **8 exceeded 120 min**
   (di-monday own three samples: 10 / 22 / 27).
2. `pulse-stall-reconcile.py` keys on the manifest per-timer `ledger_row` and skips
   only when `newest_row_ts >= fire`. On a biweekly Monday the single di-monday row
   predates the 17:00Z fire, so at fire+210 min it writes a **spurious `stalled` row for
   work that succeeded** — a false alarm in the mechanism that exists to catch real ones.

Monday is the ONLY day with two rows, so it is the only collision. Tue-Fri are 1:1.

## Recommended fix (Zig decides — this is his routing table)
Restore the time-of-day half in the `check` column, which is where it belongs now that
no argument carries it:
    di-monday        [ u = 1 ] && [ "$(TZ=America/Los_Angeles date +%H)" -ge 9 ]
    biweekly-content [ u = 1 ] && [ "$(TZ=America/Los_Angeles date +%H)" -lt 9 ] && bun ... check
Then 08:00 selects only biweekly-content and 10:00 selects only di-monday, and each unit
runs the row it is named for. Alternatives: distinct priorities (does not fix the swap,
only makes it deterministic), or keep `--row` for these two units (deviates from the
migration, but honestly reflects that row selection needs an argument when two rows share
a day).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] on a Monday, the 08:00 fire runs biweekly-content and the 10:00 fire runs di-monday
- [ ] demonstrated without waiting for Monday — evaluate both checks under a pinned
      TZ/time and show which row each selects
- [ ] `pulse-stall-reconcile.py` writes no spurious `stalled` row for that Monday
- [ ] the trigger column and the check column agree with each other
- [ ] the other four di-* rows are proven unaffected (1 row per day)
close_reason: Fixed in dashboard-dev-interrupted 22a3ab6 (pushed, proven against ls-remote). Restored the time-of-day half that dropping --row deleted, in the check column where it now has to live: di-monday gains [ date +%H -ge 9 ], biweekly-content gains [ date +%H -lt 9 ]. PROVEN BY SIMULATION rather than by waiting for Monday, which was the acceptance criterion: substituting a simulated Monday and each hour into the real check cells extracted from pulse.md, at 08 only biweekly-content passes and at 10 only di-monday passes. So each unit now runs the row it is named for, the trigger column and the check column agree for the first time since the cutover, and pulse-stall-reconcile will not write a spurious stalled row for work that succeeded. The other four di-* rows are untouched — they are 1 row per day and were never ambiguous. Root cause worth keeping: the trigger column ('time: Mon 10:00 PT') was documentation, not enforcement; the timer plus --row carried the time, and the migration silently removed one of those two legs. Monday was the only day with two rows and therefore the only collision.

title: doclint lints the /scrutinize EVAL CORPUS — 5 of its 7 errors are deliberately-planted bad code, which is how a linter trains people to ignore it
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. `python3 agents/doclint/doc-example-lint.py` (full default roots)
2. errors=7. **Five** are in
   `~/explore/.claude/skills/ab/evals/bugfix-harvest/cases/*.md` -- all
   `hook-block: pre-bash-stderr-guard.sh REFUSES this documented command`, e.g.
   `git add "${NOW_TRACKED[@]}" 2>/dev/null`.
3. `head -6` any of those case files:
     "This file is committed and in production use. It is claimed to be correct.
      Review it and return a verdict."

## Why these are FALSE POSITIVES
Those files are an **eval corpus for /scrutinize** (explore-ldfm's bugfix-harvest).
They contain deliberately-planted defects, and the linter is flagging the planted
defects as documentation defects. The suppressed-stderr line IS the bug being
catalogued -- the corpus would be WORTHLESS if it linted clean.

## Why it matters more than 5 lines of noise
/housekeeping 9.10 states the rule this violates: "a gate its users route around has
stopped being a gate" (dotfiles-aj83, dotfiles-vo3t -- three agents worked around a
hook that false-blocked them). Right now 5 of 7 errors are unfixable-by-design, so
the honest response to a FAIL verdict is to ignore it. That is the beginning of the
route-around, and it also poisons the TREND the section exists to make visible: 9.10
asks for the error count so a climbing count is the signal. A permanent floor of 5
false errors makes the trend unreadable.

Same class as the two measurement defects found earlier the same day: USAGE.log
counting log lines instead of umbrellas, and `br orphans` counting filing commits
(dotfiles-ihc0 and the /triage report). The measurement is fine; what it MEANS was
never checked.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] doclint skips eval/fixture corpora -- suggest excluding any path under
      `evals/`, `cases/`, `fixtures/`, or honoring a `<!-- doclint: skip -->` marker
      so a corpus can opt out explicitly (preferred: explicit beats path-guessing)
- [ ] Verify by re-running: the 5 bugfix-harvest errors disappear and
      `files_scanned` does NOT drop to 0 (9.10's own warning -- a zero is the tool
      declining to look, reported in the words of a pass)
- [ ] Plant a REAL error in a non-corpus file and confirm it is still caught, so the
      exclusion cannot silently widen into a blanket skip (repo rule 1: only a dead
      mutant is evidence)
- [ ] Remaining real error: `~/explore/.claude/skills/daily-digest/SKILL.md:87`
      documented JSON does not parse ("Extra data") -- explore's to fix, not dotfiles'

title: vps-8a9eb245: timer runs a 49-line stub, not the tracked 447-line vps-repo-refresh.sh
description:
## Context

`vps-repo-refresh.service` on vps-8a9eb245 runs `%h/bin/vps-repo-refresh.sh` —
a 49-line hand-written stub from VPS migration Phase 1.4, UNTRACKED, so it never
updates. The repo carries `agents/scheduler/vps-repo-refresh.sh` (447 lines) plus
a complete `vps-repo-manifest.txt` that already lists `repo $HOME/dotfiles origin
main`.

What the stub lacks, all of which the tracked version has:
- receipts (deleted first, written only on total success — so a crash leaves NO
  receipt, never a stale one)
- `--assert`, fail-closed, for a tick to gate on
- staleness measured against a LIVE `git ls-remote` rather than the cached
  `origin/<branch>` ref. This is the bug caught live 2026-07-26: `rev-list
  --count HEAD..origin/main` read 0 on a checkout that was 55 commits behind.
- per-failure remedies on stderr tagged `REFRESH-FAIL:`

Not swapped in this session on purpose. The manifest encodes marketing-vps
semantics (`readonly $HOME/dotfiles`), and Zig's stated intent as of 2026-07-27
is the opposite — this box is now HIS machine and authors dotfiles commits.
a39a098 (same night, another session) already relaxed the identity half of that
assertion, so the remaining question is narrower but still real: `readonly` also
asserts no dirty tracked files, which on an interactive dev checkout would fail
LOUDLY every hour while Zig has uncommitted work in flight.

Verified working as-is: the stub ff-only pulls dotfiles fine post-un-sparse
(`dotfiles HEAD 9818b43`, rc=0). This is a hardening upgrade, not an outage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Decide what `readonly $HOME/dotfiles` should mean now that this box is a
      working checkout rather than a read-only consumer
- [ ] Point `vps-repo-refresh.service` at `%h/dotfiles/agents/scheduler/vps-repo-refresh.sh`
      (matching how claude-vault-sync.service already references the repo directly)
- [ ] Delete the untracked `~/bin/vps-repo-refresh.sh` stub once nothing runs it
- [ ] `systemctl --user start vps-repo-refresh` is green and writes a receipt
- [ ] Hourly run does not fail merely because Zig has uncommitted work open
close_reason: DONE 2026-08-01. vps-repo-refresh.service on marketing-vps now runs the TRACKED 610-line script, not the 49-line untracked stub. Verified live: exit 0, receipt at ~/.cache/vps-repo-refresh/receipt.json (ok=true, dotfiles@708bc920, linearb@cb1218db), --assert green ('receipt ok, age 21s') -- the fail-closed gate the stub had no equivalent for. Stub moved to ~/bin/vps-repo-refresh.sh.RETIRED-20260801; zero live units reference it. Also fixed the unit's Documentation= line, which still pointed at the moved file. The bead's recorded blocker was STALE: 'readonly' stopped asserting no-dirty-files at dotfiles-f4ub, so the swap was already safe; per Zig the directive is renamed 'watch' (readonly kept as a silent alias) because the box is a full participant.

title: explore: tick-jailed.sh mirrors the CC_NO_GATEWAY precedence bug, and its VPS comment is now false
description:
Found by the orchestrator while dispatching dotfiles-20rx, 2026-08-03. CROSS-REPO (~/explore) — dispatch ALONE.

## Context
dotfiles-20rx fixes the precedence in agents/lib/claude-identity-wrapper.sh, where an
inherited ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is checked BEFORE CC_NO_GATEWAY, making the hatch
unreachable in any fresh zsh. tick-jailed.sh copied the same structure verbatim:

    GATEWAY_BASE="${ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL:-}"
    if [ -z "$GATEWAY_BASE" ] && [ -z "${CC_NO_GATEWAY:-}" ]; then

Identical defect: when the launching shell exports ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL — which every
zsh on zig-computer and metis now does, and marketing-vps as of today — GATEWAY_BASE is
already non-empty, so the CC_NO_GATEWAY branch is never evaluated and the jailed tick
uses the gateway regardless of the hatch.

This is the same defect propagating by COPY, which is the failure mode CLAUDE.md rule 2
describes: the wrapper was the example, and the example was wrong.

## Steps to Reproduce
Same shape as dotfiles-20rx. With ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL exported in the launching
environment, set CC_NO_GATEWAY=1 and observe the jail still receives
--setenv ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL.

## Second defect in the same block — a now-FALSE comment
Line ~319 states: "a host with no per-host file (the VPS) gets nothing."
That stopped being true on 2026-08-03: marketing-vps now HAS
zsh/.marketing-vps.zshenv and it exports ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. The comment also still
calls the box by its pre-rename identity implicitly.

## Do this AFTER dotfiles-20rx lands
Mirror whatever fix shape it proves, rather than inventing a second dialect — that
divergence is how the two copies drift in the first place.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CC_NO_GATEWAY=1 genuinely opts a jailed tick out, even with an inherited value
- [ ] a deliberate inherited value still wins when the hatch is NOT armed
- [ ] the stale VPS comment corrected
- [ ] covered in test-tick-jailed.sh (which gains header coverage in dotfiles-ahrd)
- [ ] a mutant reverting the fix is OBSERVED to fail, with the mutation asserted applied
notes:
## Refinement from dotfiles-20rx (2026-08-03)

The dotfiles fix had TWO halves, but tick-jailed.sh needs only ONE.

- ORDERING half: required here. Identical defect at tick-jailed.sh:321
  (`[ -z "$GATEWAY_BASE" ] && [ -z "${CC_NO_GATEWAY:-}" ]`).
- STRIPPING half (`env -u ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL claude`): NOT required here. bwrap runs
  `--clearenv` (tick-jailed.sh:676) and only explicit `--setenv` values enter the jail,
  so clearing GATEWAY_BASE genuinely suffices — the child cannot inherit the exported
  value the way the wrapper's child could.

So this is a one-line fix, not a mirror of the two-part dotfiles change. Do NOT copy the
`env -u` treatment across; it would be cargo-culted and misleading about why the wrapper
needed it.

Verified fix shape to mirror: agents/lib/claude-identity-wrapper.sh on main (29e5bb9).
close_reason: Fixed in ~/explore 23faff5: hatch-first precedence, mirroring claude-identity-wrapper.sh 29e5bb9. Only the ORDERING half was copied — and the reason was VERIFIED, not assumed: the agent ran real bwrap 0.11.0 with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL exported and the child saw @@ABSENT@@ (env printed PATH + PWD only), confirming --clearenv at tick-jailed.sh:676 is a real flag inside BWRAP_ARGS and not just the comment it appears as three other places. So clearing GATEWAY_BASE suffices and the wrapper's 'env -u' half was correctly NOT cargo-culted. Stale comment corrected (marketing-vps now resolves via step 3 like every other box). Orchestrator independently re-ran the reverting mutant with the mutation asserted applied and bash -n clean: 20 passed / 1 failed, dying on exactly 'CC_NO_GATEWAY=1 opts a jailed tick out even with an inherited value'. Suite 17/17 -> 21/21.

title: tailscale/acl.jsonc: add tag:server → tag:server SSH rule (server-to-server gap)
description:
## Problem
Our `ssh` ACL allows only `autogroup:member` (clients: metis, iPhone) → `tag:server` (zig-computer, pico). It does NOT allow `tag:server` → `tag:server` SSH, so server-to-server Tailscale SSH is denied.

Real workflow gap: the user spends much of their time SSH'd into zig-computer (the workshop). From there, they want to `tailscale ssh <user>@pico` for ops/debug without bouncing back to a laptop. Today: `tailnet policy does not permit you to SSH to this node`.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. From a `tag:server` device (e.g., zig-computer), run `tailscale ssh <valid-user>@pico.tailfb4637.ts.net`
2. Observe: `tailscale: tailnet policy does not permit you to SSH to this node`

Expected: connection succeeds (with `check` re-auth) and drops you in pico's shell.

## Root cause
Spec said "all inter-machine SSH happens primarily via Tailscale SSH" but ACL was tighter — only documented the client-side path. /scrutinize rounds reviewed the spec's intent (client→server) and didn't flag the server→server gap because it wasn't in the documented requirements.

## Fix
Append one rule to the `ssh` ACL: `tag:server` → `tag:server`, `check` action (12h re-auth), users = `autogroup:nonroot` (no root, no exotic system users). Update comment block accordingly.

## Regression guard
- Update the `/zig-zone` runbook (in explore) to document the server→server SSH rule and the workflow it enables
- Append a `## Decision` block to the closed spec bead `dotfiles-phe` --notes — promotes the rule from gap-discovered to documented-design

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `tailscale/acl.jsonc` has a second ssh rule: tag:server → tag:server, check action, users=autogroup:nonroot
- [x] User re-pastes ACL into Tailscale admin
- [x] `tailscale ssh pico@picos-mac-studio` from zig-computer succeeds after the check re-auth
- [x] `/zig-zone` runbook in explore notes the rule
- [x] dotfiles-phe --notes appended with the decision pointer

title: fix: beads JSONL silent duplicate-id merge artifacts — PostToolUse guard hook + skill staging reconciliation
description:
## Problem
git auto-merges .beads/issues.jsonl across branches "cleanly" (ort strategy, no conflict) while silently DUPLICATING bead lines when both sides touched the same bead. Caught live 2026-06-09 in dashboard-dev-interrupted PR #9: bd-dtz appeared twice (in_progress from the branch + closed from main). Empirical test: a duplicate id makes the JSONL INVALID to br (ERROR jsonl.parse: Duplicate issue id), bricking bead operations until repaired. br doctor has a purpose-built detector (jsonl.duplicate_ids: "usually an unresolved merge artifact").

## Root cause
The global /commit and /handoff skills instruct `git add .beads/issues.jsonl` with EVERY commit. Correct on main; on a feature branch it forks bead state, and the eventual merge-back produces the silent duplicate. The harness teaches the failure path.

## Research finding
br 0.2.15 ships `br sync --merge`: three-way merge of .beads/beads.base.jsonl (anchor) + DB + JSONL, with semantic conflict guards (--force-db / --force-jsonl / --force = newer timestamp). The anchor file is written by sync flush on current versions (older repos may lack it until next flush — doctor warns base_jsonl.missing_post_flush). So upstream owns semantic resolution; we need detection at the merge moment + skill reconciliation.

## Fix (3 parts, all in dotfiles)
1. **post-bash-beads-merge-check.sh** — PostToolUse:Bash hook. Fires after successful merge-ish git commands (git merge / pull / rebase / cherry-pick, gh pr merge); if repo has .beads/issues.jsonl, checks for duplicate top-level ids; exit 2 with remediation guidance (resolve toward authoritative branch, or br sync --merge when the anchor exists, verify with br doctor). Registered in claude/settings.json PostToolUse Bash group.
2. **Test** at agents/hooks/test/test-beads-merge-check.sh per the bd-n47 convention (run_case helper, PASS N/N).
3. **Skill reconciliation**: /commit + /handoff amended — stage .beads/issues.jsonl ONLY when committing on the default branch; never on feature branches; never from worktrees (already symlinked). /beads gains a merge-trap note in repo hygiene pointing at br sync --merge.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Hook detects injected duplicate after a merge command, exit 2 with id named
- [ ] Hook silent (exit 0) on: non-merge commands, failed merges, repos without beads, clean JSONL
- [ ] Test script passes all cases
- [ ] settings.json registers the hook under PostToolUse matcher Bash
- [ ] /commit + /handoff staging guidance scoped to default branch
- [ ] /beads notes the trap + br sync --merge
- [ ] /distribute run so ~/linearb/skills picks up the skill changes
notes:
---
## Closed 2026-06-10

All three parts shipped:
1. post-bash-beads-merge-check.sh + settings.json registration (PostToolUse:Bash group)
2. test-beads-merge-check.sh — 12/12 cases passing (incl. merge-base exclusion, gh pr merge, git -C form, anchor-conditional br sync --merge hint, failed-merge silence)
3. /commit Bead-state exception + /handoff no-beads-from-worktree + /beads 'JSONL merge artifacts' defense-in-depth section

Research confirmed: br 0.2.15 ships br sync --merge (3-way via .beads/beads.base.jsonl anchor). Anchor missing in older repos until next flush; hook's remediation message offers it conditionally on anchor presence.

title: decision: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL moved to a per-host file rather than dropped fleet-wide
description:
Context: Zig removed ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL from claude/settings.json because
vps-8a9eb245 cannot reach pico's tailnet address and every session here was
pinging a gateway that would never answer. He asked for a "surgical edit". But
settings.json is FLEET-WIDE and symlinked to ~/.claude/settings.json on every
machine, so committing the removal also strips the gateway from zig-computer,
which legitimately uses it. The instruction and its blast radius diverged.

Alternatives weighed:
  (a) commit the removal as-is — honours the instruction literally, silently
      breaks another machine's routing
  (b) leave it in and special-case this box — impossible, JSON has no conditionals
  (c) move it to a per-host file — the mechanism this session had just built

Decision: (c). Added zsh/.zig-computer.zshenv exporting it. Chose the .zshenv
tier over the interactive .zig-computer.zsh deliberately: scheduled pulse
dispatch runs non-interactively, and .zshrc never loads there.

Why not escalate: reversible, and it PRESERVES the status quo on the other
machine rather than changing it. Escalating would have meant blocking Zig's
explicit request on a question whose answer ("don't break the other box") was
not in doubt. Flagged in the reply and in commit 2b8d22a.

Reversibility: delete one line from zsh/.zig-computer.zshenv, or restore the key
to settings.json. No data, no migration.

Known gap, stated at the time: zig-computer loses the gateway between pulling the
settings change and running `sync.sh zsh` + opening a new shell. A later session
on another machine extended the same file with a body-size/503 escape hatch
(commit 5c9ff80), so the placement has since been accepted downstream.

title: bug(/lint): the skill never documented linter version-drift — a pinned $schema against a caret range reds the whole check gate
description:
## Context
`/lint` documented which linters run where, but never the failure mode that a versioned
config schema and a ranged dependency will always eventually diverge.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. A `biome.json` hardcodes `https://biomejs.dev/schemas/<X>/schema.json`.
2. `package.json` declares `"@biomejs/biome": "^<Y>"` — a range, so the lockfile decides.
3. Any install resolves the CLI to a version != X.
4. `biome check` emits a `deserialize` error and **counts it as an error**, so the whole
   gate goes red for a config reason and a real lint regression is indistinguishable from
   the standing noise. Nobody upgraded anything; a lockfile simply resolved elsewhere.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `/lint` documents the drift mode, the exact error text, and why it degrades silently
- [x] States the rule: pin formatters/linters EXACTLY (no caret/tilde), keep `$schema` on
      that version — byte-identical formatting across machines is the point, a range buys
      nothing
- [x] Gives the measure-before-you-bump recipe (`bunx --bun @biomejs/biome@<v> check .`)
      with real measured numbers showing a patch bump free and the next minor +4 findings
- [x] Ships a drift-detection loop (declared schema vs installed CLI for every biome.json)
- [x] No client identifiers: `~/dotfiles` is a PUBLIC repo, so the worked example is
      described generically ("a twelve-package TypeScript monorepo"), never by repo, bead,
      or file name

title: cadence drift: hermes lb-weekly-report-worker + the fleet-proxy ref still encode the Thursday report day
description:
Found 2026-07-26 while fixing dotfiles-gify (the weekly-report AirTable filter).

THE ROOT FACT: the weekly report day MOVED from Thursday to Tuesday on 2026-06-24. Proven from the AirTable column's stored values — 05-21 / 05-28 / 06-04 / 06-11 / 06-18 are all Thursdays; 06-30 / 07-07 / 07-14 / 07-21 are all Tuesdays. The column was renamed to match. Two other places still encode the old cadence:

1. **hermes-skills/lb-weekly-report-worker/SKILL.md:3,22,65,144** — still says "Thursday weekly marketing report", treats T as the report Thursday, and emits a `report_thursday` JSON key. It is a DIFFERENT runtime that stops at the draft and never touches AirTable, so it does not 422 — it just reasons about the wrong day. Retargeting its Asana windows needs its own verification; doing it blind is exactly the failure the gify fix was about.

2. **agent-factory/agents/lb-agent-fleet/refs/gdoc-airtable-proxy.md:115-119** — documents the rename but calls it a "one-line correction" and MISSES the boundary move. That is the careless fix written down as guidance, which is the dotfiles-mlti class: a wrong documented example that will propagate to whoever reads it next. **Fix before the explore-7iz9 VPS migration**, since that doc is the proxy's own reference.

WHY THE NAIVE FIX IS WORSE THAN THE BUG: renaming the column alone produces a filter that returns HTTP 200 with ZERO records — valid, silent, wrong week. The date passed had to move too (from the Wednesday read-day to the report Tuesday, tab date minus one). Verified live: naive fix = 200 / 0 records; correct fix = 200 / 4 team records.

## Acceptance Criteria

- the hermes worker's cadence is corrected AND its Asana windows re-verified, not blind-renamed
- the fleet-proxy ref describes the boundary move, not just the rename
- a sweep for any other place the Thursday cadence is encoded
notes:
## Fixed — 2026-07-26 (Opus-5 audit Wave 2)

weekly-reporting f1b4f89 (10 files, PUSHED). lb-agent-fleet 7f97dbf (1 file,
COMMITTED NOT PUSHED — that repo deploys to Vercel on push to main; doc-only
change, held per the no-deploy rule. Needs Zig's call.)

SCOPE WAS ~2.3x THE BEAD. The 6 cited lines plus 8 more encodings, including
LIVE-WRONG CODE the bead never mentioned: packages/job-runner/src/jobs/
weekly-report.ts anchored the whole report on thisWeeksThursday. Not the
scheduled path (pulse-weekly-report.timer drives the skill directly; there is no
job-runner unit), so nothing was misfiring — but it was a loaded gun.

RE-DERIVED ARITHMETIC (T = report Tuesday), mirrored from the canonical skill,
which had ALREADY migrated correctly — the worker SKILL.md had drifted from the
contract it explicitly defers to:
  LWP [T-6, T] not [T-7, T], keyed on completed_at
  TWP [T, T+8] not [T, T+7], inclusive of T
  tab = T+1 (Wed); AirTable week key = T (tab date minus one)

VERIFIED AGAINST LIVE DATA, not asserted:
- The cadence move is real in Asana: 06-04/06-11/06-18 Thursdays, then
  06-30/07-07/07-14/07-21/07-28 all Tuesdays.
- The boundary is MATERIAL: 500 live tasks bucketed for T=2026-07-21 gives
  [T-7,T]=28 vs [T-6,T]=23 — the 5-task delta is exactly the tasks completed on
  the PRIOR report Tuesday, which the stale window double-reports. On the other
  side [T,T+8]=12 vs [T,T+7]=11, plus 1 open task due exactly on T that any
  T+1-start filter drops.
- completed_on is NEVER populated: 0 of 500 task objects carried it even when
  requested, while 386 had a non-null completed_at. The worker skill said
  completed_on; corrected, with a warning added.
- AirTable: week key 2026-07-22 (Wed) -> 200 with ZERO records; 2026-07-21 (Tue)
  -> 4 team rows. The silent-empty failure mode reproduced.

UNANTICIPATED: both AirTable regime tables told you to query pre-move weeks via
{Thursday of Report Week}. That column DOES NOT EXIST — the rename was applied
IN PLACE, so one column holds Thursday values for old rows and Tuesday for new.
The CODE was already right (WEEK_COLUMN is one constant); only the docs disagreed.

COULD NOT VERIFY: the windows end-to-end through the skill's actual tasks/search
call — the fleet proxy forwards only text and projects.any, not completed_on.*/
due_on.* date params. Arithmetic was verified by pulling the board with full date
opt_fields and bucketing client-side, which tests the same boundaries but NOT the
server-side date-filter off-by-one the skill compensates for with a one-day-wider
fetch. That compensation remains asserted-not-retested.
close_reason: Fixed across 2 repos, 14 encodings total, verified against live Asana + AirTable data. One doc commit held unpushed (Vercel deploy on push).

title: ss14-tproxy: test TPROXY (nginx transparent UDP proxy on zig-computer) for SS14-on-pico
description:
## Context

Sub-bead of `dotfiles-52c` (explore: SS14-on-pico via TPROXY or GRE —
preserve source IPs + VPS-IP public face). This bead is the **TPROXY**
test track. See parent for full rationale (DNAT rejected because exposes
home WAN IP; need source IPs + VPS public face simultaneously).

## Goal

Validate (or rigorously disprove) that nginx `stream{}` with TPROXY
transparent UDP proxy on zig-computer can deliver SS14 packets to pico
with real client source IPs intact in `RemoteEndPoint.Address`, while
zig-computer remains the only publicly-known address.

## Approach summary (from 52c)

- Linux kernel `IP_TRANSPARENT` socket option
- nginx stream module: `proxy_bind \$remote_addr transparent;`
- Requirements: nginx workers with `CAP_NET_RAW` (auto since nginx
  1.13.8), `iptables -j MARK` is NOT needed for the egress half of
  TPROXY (only the return-path mark interception is), policy routing
  for the marked return packets, asymmetric-routing fix on pico
- Wrinkle: Tailscale already does its own src-IP-rewriting; TPROXY on
  top requires careful coordination

## Why this approach is HARDER than GRE (from Phase 1 research, 2026-05-24)

nginx's `proxy_bind \$remote_addr transparent` on Linux is the OUTBOUND
half of TPROXY: nginx opens its forwarding socket to pico with src=client
IP via `IP_TRANSPARENT`. Packet egresses zig-computer with spoofed src
(client's public IP). Pico receives it, but now its return packet has
src=pico's home WAN IP (or its tailnet IP if routed via Tailscale) and
dst=client. The client expected the reply to come from
51.81.33.136 (zig-computer's public IP), so the reply gets dropped at
the client.

The canonical TPROXY-with-remote-backend fix per the NGINX/F5 blog
"IP Transparency and Direct Server Return" requires:
1. The backend's default route to point AT the proxy box (so all egress
   goes through nginx) — destructive on pico (would break Ollama outbound,
   docker pulls, brew updates, etc.)
2. **Stateless NAT rewriting on the backend** via `tc nat egress` to
   rewrite the source on outbound replies back to nginx's IP — **`tc`
   does not exist on macOS**. The macOS equivalent would be `pfctl`
   rdr/nat rules, which is uncharted territory for this UDP-game use
   case
3. OR: source-NAT on egress so pico sees nginx as the client (defeats
   the entire point — we WANT pico to learn the real client IP)

None of these cleanly fit pico-as-macOS-server. **GRE/IP-in-IP solves
the asymmetric routing automatically via the tunnel interface**: pico's
reply routes back through gif0 because the route table directs the
specific client /32 (or specific src-IP /32 via reverse policy) through
the tunnel. The reply emerges from zig-computer's public IP (post
decapsulation + masquerade), so the client sees a coherent flow.

**Recommendation: Test GRE (Approach B) FIRST. Defer TPROXY testing
unless GRE fails with a fundamental blocker.**

## Test plan (high-level, deferred to post-GRE-result)

If GRE-track (dotfiles-jjd) fails AND TPROXY is still worth trying:

### Test bench: synthetic UDP-echo at :11212 (NEVER touch :1212 live)

Synthetic test will use port :11212 throughout. Real SS14 `:1212`
listeners stay untouched.

### Step 0 — Snapshot pre-test state

```bash
# zig-computer
sudo iptables-save > /tmp/iptables.pretest.\$(date +%s)
ip rule list > /tmp/iprule.pretest.\$(date +%s)
ip route show table all > /tmp/iproute.pretest.\$(date +%s)
sudo nginx -T > /tmp/nginx.pretest.\$(date +%s) 2>&1

# pico
ssh pico 'sudo pfctl -sr > /tmp/pfctl.pretest 2>&1; netstat -rn > /tmp/route.pretest'
```

Rollback verification later compares against these snapshots.

### Step 1 — Create test stream config (NEW file, never touches live ss14)

```bash
sudo tee /etc/nginx/streams-enabled/ss14-tproxy-test.conf <<'CONF'
# TEST ONLY — port 11212; live SS14 stays on :1212 untouched
upstream tproxy_test_pico {
    server 100.72.47.4:11212;
}
server {
    listen 11212 udp;
    proxy_pass tproxy_test_pico;
    proxy_bind \$remote_addr transparent;
    proxy_responses 1;
    proxy_timeout 10s;
}
CONF
sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
```

Rollback:
```bash
sudo rm /etc/nginx/streams-enabled/ss14-tproxy-test.conf
sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
```

### Step 2 — UFW allow inbound :11212

```bash
sudo ufw allow 11212/udp comment 'TPROXY test'
```

Rollback:
```bash
sudo ufw delete allow 11212/udp
```

### Step 3 — Mark + route the RETURN traffic so it reaches nginx

The OUTBOUND-to-pico half needs no mangle (nginx sets IP_TRANSPARENT on
its own socket). The RETURN-from-pico half needs to land on nginx, not
the kernel:

```bash
# Use mark 0x1 (avoid Tailscale's 0x80000/0xff0000 range)
sudo iptables -t mangle -A PREROUTING -p udp --sport 11212 -s 100.72.47.4 -j MARK --set-mark 0x1
sudo ip rule add fwmark 0x1 lookup 100 priority 100
sudo ip route add local 0.0.0.0/0 dev lo table 100
```

Rollback (in reverse order):
```bash
sudo ip route del local 0.0.0.0/0 dev lo table 100
sudo ip rule del fwmark 0x1 lookup 100 priority 100
sudo iptables -t mangle -D PREROUTING -p udp --sport 11212 -s 100.72.47.4 -j MARK --set-mark 0x1
```

### Step 4 — Asymmetric routing fix on pico

Pico must send the reply back to zig-computer (so nginx sees it as the
return and forwards to client) rather than out its default route. Per
the F5 doc, this needs either:

**Option 4a — Per-source route via pfctl** (untested for this scenario):
```bash
ssh pico 'sudo route add -host 100.98.174.21 -interface utun5'
# (already direct via tailscale; this is informational. The TRICKY part
# is: pico's reply to the public client IP must NOT go via en0 default
# route; it MUST go via utun5 (tailscale) back to zig-computer.)
```

For this, on pico:
```bash
# Route ALL traffic originating from listener back through tailnet to zig
ssh pico 'sudo route -n add -net <client-public-IP-or-test-src>/32 \
  -interface utun5'
```

But the test client is the synthetic UDP src, not a real public IP.
**This is the un-solved part** — without `tc nat egress` on Linux or
equivalent on macOS, every public client would need its own per-host
route on pico, which scales O(connected players). Not viable in
production. **The TPROXY-to-remote-backend pattern collapses here.**

### Step 5 — Synthetic test (if Steps 0-4 cleanly applied)

On zig-computer (acting as proxy):
```bash
# Confirm proxy listener up
ss -unap | grep :11212
```

On pico:
```bash
# Set up tcpdump + listener
ssh pico 'sudo tcpdump -ni any port 11212 -c 5' &
ssh pico 'nc -ul 11212' &
```

From a tailnet client (or a different source — emulated by sending from
zig-computer's docker IP):
```bash
# Send a packet bound to a synthetic src — needs IP_TRANSPARENT to actually
# spoof, otherwise sends from zig-computer's tailnet IP.
echo "tproxy-test-\$(date +%s)" | nc -u -q1 \
  -s 172.17.0.1 zig-computer-public-IP 11212
```

Expected pico tcpdump: `IP 172.17.0.1.<srcport> > 100.72.47.4.11212`
(showing the spoofed source). If instead it shows
`IP 100.98.174.21.<srcport> > 100.72.47.4.11212` (zig-computer's tailnet
IP), the TPROXY proxy_bind didn't fire.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Step-by-step test plan documented (this section)
- [ ] Each step has explicit rollback documented (above)
- [ ] Synthetic-test result: pico tcpdump shows real client IP (PASS) or
      doesn't (FAIL with diagnosis)
- [ ] Real-SS14-client test result (if synthetic passes AND
      asymmetric-routing fix proven not to scale-block)
- [ ] Outcome reflected back to parent 52c bead's --notes

## Open questions

- Can `pfctl` rdr/nat rules on macOS replace `tc nat egress` for
  per-connection stateless rewriting? (Needs deep dive — out of
  scope for first-test attempt.)
- If the asymmetric-routing fix requires touching pico's default route,
  is there a tailscale subnet route trick that avoids breaking pico's
  outbound? (Possibly: advertise the public-IP-space /32 via Tailscale
  subnet routing from zig-computer, so pico learns "go back via
  tailnet to reach 51.81.33.136" — needs experimentation.)
notes:
## CLOSED 2026-05-24 — research complete, approach RULED OUT

TPROXY-to-macOS-backend has no clean asymmetric-routing fix. F5/NGINX
docs propose three remedies, all unworkable in this topology:
(a) flip pico's default route to zig-computer (catastrophic for outbound),
(b) tc nat egress on backend (Linux-only, doesn't exist on macOS),
(c) per-client routes that scale O(connected players).

A multi-day pfctl research project COULD surface a macOS-specific
recipe, but the risk-reward is poor when Approach C2 (Robust.Server
wrapper-pair, see superseder bead) delivers the same goal with clearly-
scoped code work and no per-client routing-table thrash.

**Superseded by**: dotfiles-52c continues; the C2 spec bead (opening
next) becomes the live work track. r8k stays closed as honest research
exhaustion.

Dependencies:
  -> dotfiles-52c (parent-child) - explore: SS14-on-pico via TPROXY or GRE — preserve source IPs + VPS-IP public face

## Closed 2026-05-25 — not viable
TPROXY-to-macOS-backend: no clean asymmetric routing path; macOS doesn't honor Linux's TPROXY mark semantics on the return leg. Documented in dotfiles-52c --notes. The C2 wrapper architecture (dotfiles-9g1) was the eventual answer, technically shipped + rolled back per dotfiles-v1i.

title: tests: two sed -i calls are BSD no-ops — test-always-loaded-staleness and test-vps-repo-refresh never ran their real case on macOS
description:
## Context

Sibling of `dotfiles-1rj5` (fixed in `ce5f531`), same root cause, different files. The
`grep -rn 'sed -i' agents/` audit that bead mandated turned up two more live instances:

- `agents/hooks/test/test-always-loaded-staleness.sh:169`
- `agents/scheduler/test-vps-repo-refresh.sh:240`

BSD sed takes the script as `-i`'s backup-suffix argument and then dies on the filename
("invalid command code"), so on macOS the mutation these tests depend on **never happens**
and the assertion that follows tests nothing.

A patch was written and verified but could NOT be committed from `zig`: both suites are
