title: promote the ad-hoc tunnel-ownership mutation harness into agents/scheduler/ and wire it into pre-commit
description:
Raised by the dotfiles-47nf agent as out-of-scope; filed rather than done.

## Context
dotfiles-47nf built a throwaway mutation harness in scratchpad to prove that
ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh ownership logic actually bites. It killed 3 real mutants,
including a LIVE cross-kill (bringing up tunnel B printed "closed our local forward"
against tunnel A pid 3101373).

That harness is currently disposable, so the next edit to the ownership logic has a
green suite and no mutant check — which CLAUDE.md rule 1 says is not evidence:
"A green suite is not evidence that a guard bites; only a mutant that dies is."

`agents/hooks/test/mutate-scrutiny-guards.sh` is the existing precedent and is already
wired into tools/githooks/pre-commit. Mirror it as
agents/scheduler/mutate-tunnel-ownership.sh.

## Also worth encoding: a mutant must die of the bug it NAMES
The 47nf agent's first attempt over-escaped a sed pattern so the mutant matched
NOTHING — the suite failed, but for the wrong reason, which would have been recorded
as "mutant died" by anyone reading only the exit code. A mutation harness should
assert that the mutation actually applied (diff non-empty AND the mutated pattern
still matches the intended shape) before trusting the failure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] agents/scheduler/mutate-tunnel-ownership.sh exists, modeled on mutate-scrutiny-guards.sh
- [ ] it asserts each mutation APPLIED before interpreting the suite result
- [ ] wired into tools/githooks/pre-commit keyed on ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh AND its test
- [ ] observed: harness passes on clean tree, fails on a reintroduced ownership bug
- [ ] case 25 weakness from dotfiles-47nf re-examined (it may be a test that cannot fail)
close_reason: agents/scheduler/mutate-tunnel-ownership.sh shipped and gated in tools/githooks/pre-commit, keyed on BOTH ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh and its suite. Five mutants (M1 target-blind cross-kill, M2 pre-generalization hardwired, M3 shared pidfile, M4 re_escape neutered, M5 tunnel_down kill-target blind); each mutation is asserted applied FIVE ways before its result counts (target present exactly once pristine, replacement absent before, bytes changed, replacement present once after, bash -n still clean) — any failure is a HARNESS ERROR at rc 2 with the mutant printed NOT RUN, demonstrated by injecting a stale target. Killed mutants must also die on the cases they NAME, so the suite header's map is executable rather than a comment. It also CORRECTED the reviewer's construction: blind our_pid discovery also reddens case 23 (B finds A by discovery and recycle-kills it during setup), so M5 blinds tunnel_down instead, isolating it with both pidfiles correct and both pids non-empty — proving 24/25/27/28 detect ownership rather than empty strings. Orchestrator re-verified independently: harness green on the clean tree with all five killed on their named cases; then deleted case 28 from the TEST ONLY (script untouched) — suite stayed green at 27/27 while the harness caught it FOUR ways (M4 SURVIVED plus M2/M3/M5 MIS-KILLED for no longer dying on the case they name) and exited rc 1, so the gate can actually block. Measured cost: suite 9s, harness 63s, commit 71s — comparable to the existing 88s scrutiny gate.

title: pico: three launchd jobs have been crash-looping ~240k times each, unnoticed
description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-26 while auditing pico for boot persistence. Three separate
launchd jobs were in permanent restart loops, each with a restart count around a
quarter of a million:

| Job | runs | last exit | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `com.zig.vs14-web` | 237,737 | 1 (EADDRINUSE) | **fixed today** — an orphan was squatting :3300 |
| `homebrew.mxcl.tailscale` (user agent) | 242,422 | 78 EX_CONFIG | **fixed today** — duplicate of the system daemon; tailscaled needs root |
| `com.zig.tmux` | ~241,920 | 1 | **open** |

None of them alarmed. `vs14-web`'s loop grew `/tmp/vs14-web.log` to **51 MB**
and the only visible symptom was a log file nobody looks at.

## Why this is a pattern and not three coincidences

All three share the shape in `dotfiles-cxle`: a scheduled/supervised step stops
working while nothing reports it. launchd faithfully does its job — restart on
failure — and a job that can NEVER succeed turns that into an infinite loop that
looks, from every casual angle, like a running service. `launchctl list` shows
the label. `ps` shows a process for the two that had squatters. Only the `runs`
counter tells the truth, and nothing reads it.

**The counter is the tell, and it is free.** A job with `runs` in the hundreds of
thousands is definitionally broken; a healthy long-lived daemon has `runs = 1`
(tailscaled: pid 367, runs = 1, up since May 28).

## Steps to Reproduce

    ssh pico 'launchctl list | awk "\$2 != 0 && \$1 == \"-\""'   # failed, not running
    ssh pico 'sudo launchctl print system/<label> | grep runs'   # the counter

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Root-cause `com.zig.tmux` exit 1 and fix or retire it
- [ ] A cheap standing check — any launchd/systemd job whose restart count
      exceeds a threshold is reported. This is the generalisable half and it is
      worth more than the three individual fixes.
- [ ] Consider the systemd equivalent on zig-computer (`NRestarts`) — the same
      blindness applies; nginx there showed `NRestarts=0`, but nothing looks
- [ ] Truncate `/tmp/vs14-web.log` (51 MB, inert now)
notes:
FIXED 2026-07-26. All three loops dead, and the generalisable half shipped.

| Job | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| `com.zig.vs14-web` | 237,737, exit 1 | running, counter frozen at 237,744 — an orphan was squatting :3300; killed, launchd took over |
| `homebrew.mxcl.tailscale` (user agent) | 242,422, exit 78 EX_CONFIG | booted out, disabled, plist retired — a duplicate of the SYSTEM daemon, and tailscaled needs root so the agent copy could never start. The real daemon (pid 367, runs=1, up since May 28) untouched. |
| `com.zig.tmux` | 242,224, exit 1 | runs=1, exit 0, not running |

THE TMUX BUG, which Zig diagnosed from the symptom before seeing it: the plist
ran `tmux new-session -d -s pico`, which is NOT idempotent. First run creates the
session and exits 0. Every run after fails `duplicate session: pico` and exits 1
— and `KeepAlive {SuccessfulExit=false}` restarts precisely on nonzero exit.
**The job's own success is what made it fail forever.** 5.5 MB of "duplicate
session" in /tmp/com.zig.tmux.log.

Fixed by making it idempotent: `tmux has-session -t pico || exec tmux
new-session -d -s pico`. KeepAlive was KEPT deliberately — it now means what it
was always meant to (retry if the job genuinely cannot do its work) instead of
retrying because the work was already done. Zig's requirement — one long-lived
system-owned tmux server that survives logout — is satisfied by the server
daemonising and reparenting to launchd (pid 21174, PPID 1, since Jun 5); tmux
has no foreground-server mode, so that is the only shape available.

Verified his live sessions (`work`, 2 windows, attached) survived the change,
after first confirming launchd tracked NO pid for the job so bootout could not
kill the server.

54.5 MB of log reclaimed (5.5 MB tmux + 49 MB vs14-web).

THE STANDING CHECK — `~/dotfiles/agents/bin/restart-loop-check.sh`, and it is
worth more than the three fixes. Covers both hosts (systemd `NRestarts` +
launchd `runs`).

The design decision that makes it trustworthy: **a high count is NOT a loop.**
vs14-web sits at 237,744 and is healthy — launchd does not reset the counter
until re-bootstrap. Flagging that would train the reader to ignore the check,
which is the precise failure this exists to prevent. So it samples TWICE, 15 s
apart, and flags only counts that CLIMBED; high-but-static is reported as `scar`
— history, not fault.

PROVEN BY NEGATIVE CONTROL, not by a green run: a throwaway `com.zig.looptest`
(/usr/bin/false + KeepAlive) was installed on pico, and the checker caught it —
`runs 7 -> 22 in 15s ACTIVELY LOOPING`, `RESULT=found` — while still classifying
vs14-web as a scar. Then removed.

An earlier version of this script reported `clean` because its own awk quoting
broke and every comparison silently skipped. Caught only because the result
contradicted a known-bad job. That bug WAS the bug class it hunts, committed
inside the hunter, which is why the negative control is not optional here.

Still open: nothing on the three jobs. The check is not yet on a timer — worth a
pulse row or a weekly unit, deliberately left for a session that owns the
scheduler.

title: githooks: the mutation-harness gate costs 4m24s under load, not the ~90s the runner advertises
description:
## Context

Found while fixing `dotfiles-oe80` (case 22 load-flake), on the same box and under
the same synthetic load used to verify that fix.

`tools/githooks/pre-commit` fires `agents/hooks/test/mutate-scrutiny-guards.sh` when a
commit stages any of six scrutiny-guard files, and both its inline comment and the
message it prints to the committer say **~90s** (measured at load 8.4 on 12 cores).

Measured 2026-08-01 at **load 55 on the same 12 cores: 4m24s** — ~3x the advertised
number, with no output between the "running mutation harness (~90s)" line and the
result. On a box running several agents that is a multi-minute silent wait during
`git commit`, which reads as a hang. It is a cost/UX problem, not a correctness one:
the harness passed (all mutants killed) at that load, and the git pre-commit hook has
no time ceiling to blow.

Not fixed under `dotfiles-oe80` — that bead was scoped to case 22 only.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Load a 12-core box to ~55 (`for i in $(seq 1 36); do yes >/dev/null & done`).
2. `time bash agents/hooks/test/mutate-scrutiny-guards.sh`
3. Observe 4m24s wall clock, exit 0, "all mutants killed", and no intermediate
   output for minutes at a time.
4. Kill the load, re-run: back to the advertised order of magnitude.

## Task

Decide whether to (a) reword the advertised figure to something load-honest
("~90s on an idle box; several minutes under load"), (b) emit per-mutant progress so
the wait is legible, or (c) both. Do not simply narrow the trigger — the six-file
trigger is deliberate and load-bearing (see the comment above it in the runner).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The committer can tell the difference between "still working" and "hung".
- [ ] Any stated runtime figure names the load it was measured at.

title: pulse-dispatch-remote: adopt a healthy box-side forward instead of hard-failing on the -R bind
description:
## Context

INCIDENT (2026-07-29 14:00 UTC): pulse-di-wednesday.service exited 71
failed-tunnel at step 1. The tick never dispatched; no ad-reads drafted;
NOTHING rang a bell — Zig discovered it by asking hours later.

ROOT CAUSE — two features shipped the same day bind the same port:
  * pulse-dispatch-remote.sh step 1 opens `ssh -R 127.0.0.1:7100:...` to the
    box, ExitOnForwardFailure=yes.
  * ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh (shipped 2026-07-28, the box self-heal) opens
    `ssh -L 127.0.0.1:7100:127.0.0.1:7100 zig-computer` FROM the box.
Both bind 127.0.0.1:7100 ON THE BOX. Whichever is up first wins; the other
gets "remote port forwarding failed for listen port 7100".

A local forward from the box has been up since Jul 28 (pid 1220000, user
andrew) — left behind by last session's self-heal verification. It is
HEALTHY: `curl 127.0.0.1:7100/api/health` from the box returns 200 right now.
So the box had a working path to the fleet proxy, and the dispatch killed
itself rather than use it.

ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh is already the tolerant half ("never fights a healthy
tunnel — if the port answers, do nothing"). pulse-dispatch-remote.sh is the
intolerant half. The asymmetry IS the bug. Step 3's A3 already treats the
box-owned forward as a legitimate state (it calls the self-heal and accepts
the result) — step 1 just dies ~370 lines before A3 can say so.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On marketing-vps, open the box-side forward:
   `~/dotfiles/agents/scheduler/ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh ensure`
   (or simply observe the one live now: `ss -tlnp | grep 7100`).
2. Confirm it is HEALTHY from the box:
   `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:7100/api/health`
   -> 200.
3. From zig-computer run any remote dispatch, e.g.
   `pulse-dispatch-remote.sh --row di-wednesday --dir ~/linearb/dashboard-dev-interrupted --dry-run`
4. Observed: exits 71, `PULSE_DISPATCH_RESULT=failed-tunnel`,
   tunnel.err = "Error: remote port forwarding failed for listen port 7100".
   Nothing is surfaced to work:di. Expected: the dispatch adopts the healthy
   path and proceeds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Step 1 is ADOPT-OR-OPEN, tracking TUNNEL_MODE (owned|adopted):
      (a) try `-R` as today -> owned;
      (b) on bind failure open the control master WITHOUT the forward; if that
          fails the box is genuinely unreachable -> fail failed-tunnel;
      (c) with the master up, probe health FROM THE BOX (rsh, login shell,
          three-valued 200/000/other, same contract as /vps). 200 -> adopted,
          proceed, say so loudly. Anything else -> ask the box to drop only ITS
          OWN forward (`ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh down`, already pidfile-scoped —
          never pkill on a shared box), close the master, retry `-R` ONCE;
          still failing -> fail failed-tunnel with the real reason.
- [ ] TUNNEL_MODE is recorded in the run state dir and in the say/receipt trail.
- [ ] Teardown never kills a forward this run did not create (assert in a test).
- [ ] Cleanup DOES tear down a forward this run caused: when A3's self-heal
      opens a box-side forward mid-run, track it (A3_HEALED=1) and call
      `ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh down` on the box at cleanup in that case only.
      Restores the lifetime-bounded property CLAUDE.md promises. Adopted-mode
      forwards are never torn down.
- [ ] fail() surfacing inverted to cover the class: surface EVERY verdict
      EXCEPT failed-usage / failed-row (operator typos on hand-runs) and except
      --dry-run. Recursion guard and "surface_locally warns, never calls fail"
      must hold.
- [ ] test-pulse-dispatch-remote.sh passes with NEW cases: adopt on a healthy
      pre-bound port; reclaim-and-retry on a dead-but-bound port; genuinely
      unreachable box still fails 71; failed-tunnel now surfaces.
- [ ] `bash -n` clean.
- [ ] EVIDENCE: paste a real `--dry-run` against marketing-vps showing
      TUNNEL_MODE=adopted and A3 green. The box's forward is up right now, so
      this is a live reproduction of the exact failing condition.

## Out of scope — file a bead, do not do it

ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh's own logic; the pulse ledger schema; the DI skills;
and the policy question of whether the box should hold a STANDING forward at
all (that is Zig's call, asked separately).

title: tailnet acl: untag pico, add server→user rules for native Taildrop
description:
## Context

Tailscale Taildrop is hard-locked to same-user transfers (see f7n
WON'T FIX + runbook gotcha #23). User confirmed they want native
Taildrop between pico ↔ iPhone ↔ metis, accepting the trade-off that
pico loses tag:server identity. Hybrid model: zig-computer keeps tag
(public-internet edge, isolation matters); pico moves to user-owned
(internal home-LAN compute).

## ACL changes (this commit)

- Comment block rewritten to document the new identity model
- New L3 rule: `tag:server → autogroup:owner:*` (zig → pico-as-user)
- New SSH rule: `autogroup:member → autogroup:self` with action `check`
  (metis → pico SSH, with 12h re-auth)
- New SSH rule: `tag:server → autogroup:owner` with action `accept`
  (zig → pico SSH; `check` not possible since src is a tag)

## User action (NOT done by me)

1. Open https://login.tailscale.com/admin/acls/file → paste updated
   `tailscale/acl.jsonc` → Preview to confirm intent → don't save yet
2. Open https://login.tailscale.com/admin/machines → click `pico` →
   Edit tags → remove `tag:server` → save. (Or via `tailscale set
   --advertise-tags=` on pico, but admin console is simpler.)
3. Save the ACL from step 1 (now that pico's tag matches the new rules)
4. Verify: `ssh pico` still works from zig-computer (rule 4 covers it)
5. Verify: `tailscale file cp /tmp/foo iphone-15-pro:` works FROM PICO

title: the guarded merge sequence has NO owner — AGENTS.md and /orchestrator each name the other, and the commands exist in neither
description:
Hit live while merging a dotfiles-ogkz subagent wave, 2026-08-02.

## Context
The 2026-08-01 single-owner consolidation (dotfiles-oec6) pointed these two at each
other and the content fell out between them.

agents/AGENTS.md, "Delegation":
    "The merge / bead-close / worktree-cleanup sequence after a subagent finishes,
     with all of its guards, lives in **`/orchestrator`** — run it, don't retype it."

~/.claude/skills/orchestrator/SKILL.md, "After Subagent Completes":
    "Then run the merge sequence — **single owner: `~/dotfiles/agents/AGENTS.md`,
     "Delegation"** (assert $TARGET -> BEFORE=$(git rev-parse HEAD) -> guarded merge
     -> SHA-moved + --is-ancestor checks -> br close -> commit .beads/issues.jsonl
     -> git worktree remove --force --force + git branch -D -> conditional remote
     delete). That block is loaded in every session; copying it here is how the two
     drift."

Each declares the OTHER the single owner. The runnable commands are in neither.

## Steps to Reproduce
    cd ~/dotfiles
    grep -n "is-ancestor\|BEFORE=\$(git rev-parse\|worktree remove" agents/AGENTS.md
    # -> no output. AGENTS.md has none of the guards it is credited with owning.

    sed -n "/^## Delegation/,/^## Beads lifecycle/p" agents/AGENTS.md
    # -> ends by pointing at /orchestrator. No commands.

Then follow the chain as an orchestrator would: AGENTS.md -> /orchestrator ->
AGENTS.md. It terminates in a loop with nothing executable.

## Why this is P1
The ONLY surviving description is /orchestrator's parenthetical step LIST, which is a
summary, not a runnable block. An orchestrator that follows the pointer chain in good
faith finds nothing to run and improvises — landing on exactly the bare
`git merge worktree-agent-XXX` that both documents warn "no-ops SILENTLY on cwd drift
or an agent that committed nothing."

So the guard rule survived the refactor while the guard itself did not, and the
failure is silent by construction. Same shape as dotfiles-cxle (the consumer reports
success while the step stopped working).

This is also CLAUDE.md rule 2 (a documented EXAMPLE is executable): the missing block
is worse than a wrong one, because a wrong example fails loudly.

## Candidate fix
Put the runnable block in exactly ONE place and make the other a pointer that names
the file AND section. Given AGENTS.md is loaded in every session and /orchestrator is
loaded on demand, AGENTS.md is the better host — but either works as long as the
pointer is one-directional. Then add a guard that fails when a "single owner: X"
pointer resolves to a section that does not contain the artifact it claims to own.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] the guarded sequence exists, verbatim and runnable, in exactly one document
- [ ] the other document points to it one-directionally (no mutual "single owner")
- [ ] the block is RUN once end-to-end before being committed (CLAUDE.md rule 2)
- [ ] a check catches a "single owner" pointer whose target lacks the content
- [ ] the check is OBSERVED to fail against the current circular state before the fix
close_reason: Fixed in parallel by Zig's dc99ec8 while this session ran. Verified: agents/AGENTS.md now carries the runnable guards (--is-ancestor :236, worktree remove --force --force :248) and /orchestrator points at it one-directionally. NOT implemented: a check that fails when a 'single owner' pointer resolves to a section lacking the content it claims to own.

title: reef on pico: REEF_ROOT was unset, so the entire .env.local hierarchy was inert
description:
Found 2026-07-25 while wiring granola webhook auth (dotfiles-ks1u).

The launchd plist com.zig.reef-router set REEF_DIR but NOT REEF_ROOT, so loadReefEnv() resolved \$HOME/reef = /Users/pico/reef — a path that does not exist on pico. Every .env.local in the reef hierarchy was therefore being silently ignored on the box that actually runs the router.

title: /commit: a push fallback behind a pipe can never fire — the pipe masks git push's exit code
description:
Standing-practice proposal promoted out of the 2026-08-03 handoff note (offboard Step 2.6).

## Context
The orchestrator used this idiom for every push in a long session:

    if ! git push origin main 2>&1 | tail -1; then
      git fetch origin && git merge --no-edit origin/main && git push origin main
    fi

`if !` tests the exit status of the PIPELINE, which is `tail` — always 0. So the
fetch+merge absorb path CANNOT run, ever. It was written specifically to satisfy the
AGENTS.md "two writers" rule and it satisfied nothing.

This is invisible while pushes succeed. It surfaced only when a real rejection landed
(marketing-vps / another session had pushed four commits): the push failed, the
fallback silently did not fire, and the divergence was caught ONLY by the separate
`git ls-remote` comparison that /commit already mandates as push proof.

## Steps to Reproduce
    cd <repo behind its remote>
    if ! git push origin main 2>&1 | tail -1; then echo "FALLBACK RAN"; fi
    # push fails; "FALLBACK RAN" never prints; exit status of the `if` is tail's 0

## Why it belongs in /commit
/commit already carries the push-proof anti-pattern ("`git rev-parse HEAD` as push proof
— it prints your local head, not what the remote got"). This is the same family one
level down: a guard whose exit code is swallowed before anything reads it. The existing
ls-remote proof is what caught it, which is a good argument for that rule and a good
place to note this.

## Fix
Capture the status without a pipe (`git push origin main; rc=$?`), or use PIPESTATUS.
Then keep the ls-remote comparison regardless — it is the check that actually bit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] /commit names this idiom explicitly as an anti-pattern, with the reason
- [ ] the corrected form is shown and has been RUN (CLAUDE.md rule 2)
- [ ] the ls-remote proof stays mandatory — it is what caught this one
close_reason: Landed in agents/skills/commit/SKILL.md (781aef5), immediately after the rev-parse push-proof block, plus one appended sentence on /commit's TOOLKIT anti-pattern line. Named as 'the rev-parse trap one level down — a guard whose signal is swallowed before anything reads it', with the durable tell pinned: the failure mode is SILENCE, which is why it survived a whole session. It states explicitly that the ls-remote proof is NOT redundant with the fallback — it is what catches the fallback itself being broken. MY BRIEF WAS WRONG and the agent caught it: I sanctioned ${PIPESTATUS[0]} as an alternative. It is bash-only and expands EMPTY in this fleet's zsh 5.9, failing open exactly as the bug it would replace — I hit that live, printing 'push succeeded' on a rejected push. It is now documented as a 🚫, not an alternative, with zsh's lowercase 1-indexed $pipestatus shown alongside. The agent also sharpened my own measurement: my pipestatus[1]=0 reading was contaminated, because ANY intervening command clobbers the array; captured immediately it is 1. Orchestrator verified independently: no $N skill-arg substitution hazards (rule 7), TOOLKIT still a digest at 40,169 bytes, and the documented fix EXTRACTED VERBATIM by regex from the committed SKILL.md and executed under zsh against a throwaway repo whose remote had moved — push rejected, fallback fired, fetch+merge, push landed, ls-remote proof MATCH.

title: hooks: require-isolation guards the WRONG repo on a cross-repo subagent dispatch
description:
## Context
Hit live on 2026-07-27 from a `~/hevyd` session dispatching work into `~/harnessd`
(bead harnessd-zvum).

`~/.claude/hooks/pre-tool-use-require-isolation.sh` blocks any
`subagent_type: "subagent"` dispatch that lacks `isolation: "worktree"`. Its stated
rationale is git-index racing: two subagents in the orchestrator's own working
directory corrupt each other's commits.

But the worktree is created from the ORCHESTRATOR'S repo. When the work lives in a
different repo, satisfying the hook produces a worktree the agent never uses, while
it writes directly to the other repo's shared checkout — exactly the hazard the hook
exists to prevent, now invisible to it. The dispatch reads as guarded and is not.

Single cross-repo agents are fine (no concurrent writer). TWO of them targeting the
same foreign repo would race silently, and the hook would pass both.

Precedent: this project's own history records "ten worktree subagents, two repos"
(hevyd handoff 2026-07-27), so cross-repo dispatch is established practice here, not
a one-off.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Decide the intended posture for cross-repo dispatch: teach the hook to detect
      it, or document that isolation is orchestrator-repo-scoped and cross-repo
      dispatch must be serialized by the orchestrator
- [ ] Whichever is chosen, the hook's message no longer implies a guarantee it does
      not provide for this case
- [ ] If detection is chosen, a cross-repo dispatch either targets a worktree of the
      RIGHT repo or is refused with a reason

title: br 0.1.7 -> 0.2.19 left a stale DB schema: br lint dies, doctor says schema OK, and the close gate blames the bead
description:
## Context

After upgrading `br` 0.1.7 -> 0.2.19 on `zig` (2026-08-01), `br lint` failed outright:

```
Error: Database error: internal error: column 'last_child' not found in table 'child_counters'
```

The 0.1.7 schema was `child_counters(parent_id, next_child_number)`; 0.2.19 expects
`child_counters(parent_id, last_child, …)`. **The migration never ran**, and nothing said so
until a command happened to need the column.

Three separate failures stacked on top of that, and the stacking is the real finding:

**1. `br lint` is dead, not degraded.** Every invocation errors. Any gate built on it is
therefore inoperative rather than lenient.

**2. `br doctor` reports `OK schema.tables` and `OK schema.columns`.** The one diagnostic
whose job is to catch this **passes** on it. Health read `degraded` for unrelated sync
reasons, so even the summary line pointed elsewhere.

**3. `pre-bead-close.sh` blamed the bead.** Closing `dotfiles-22xi` produced:

> Blocked: bead dotfiles-22xi has incomplete template sections.
> Error: Database error: internal error: column 'last_child' not found …

followed by advice to add `## Context` / `## Acceptance Criteria`. The bead **already had
`## Context`, `## Steps to Reproduce`, `## Acceptance Criteria`, `## Fix` and one more**. The
gate ran `br lint`, got a non-zero exit for a reason it never inspected, and asserted a cause
it had not checked — verbatim the `dotfiles-kel5` shape, in a different gate. It does print
the DB error, but buried under a confident wrong headline, which is worse than silence
because it sends you to edit a bead that is fine.

## Steps to Reproduce

With a `.beads/beads.db` created by br 0.1.x, then br >= 0.2.x installed:

```bash
br lint <any-id>          # Database error: column 'last_child' not found
br doctor | grep schema   # OK schema.tables / OK schema.columns
br close <any-id>         # "incomplete template sections" — false
sqlite3 .beads/beads.db '.schema child_counters'
```

## Resolution applied on zig

JSONL is the source of truth and was committed (329 beads), so: backed the DB up to
`.beads/beads-backup-20260802.db`, moved a 143537s-orphaned `.write.lock` aside, deleted
`beads.db` + its `-fsqlite-ns-*` sidecars, and let 0.2.19 rebuild. Result: correct schema,
DB count 329 == JSONL 329 (was 305, i.e. **24 beads behind**), `br lint` clean, doctor
`degraded` -> `healthy`.

**Other machines are exposed.** `marketing-vps` reports br 0.2.16 and `pico` 0.2.11 per the
`dotfiles-1r6k` audit; any box that crossed 0.1.x -> 0.2.x has the same latent mismatch.

Separately, `br delete --hard` did NOT prune the tombstone from the JSONL as its `--help`
claims (`bd-2lcr` persists as `status: tombstone`).

Also a doctor false positive worth a line: it warns `.beads/.gitignore` is "missing expected
pattern(s): .write.lock" while `*.lock` on line 8 already ignores it. It greps for a literal
pattern instead of asking git whether the path is ignored.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pre-bead-close.sh` distinguishes "lint found template problems" from "lint could not
      run" — a non-zero exit it did not inspect must not be reported as a bead defect
- [ ] `br doctor`'s schema check actually detects a missing expected column (it is the
      designated detector and it passed)
- [ ] `br` / `pico` / `marketing-vps` checked for the same stale schema and rebuilt if present
- [ ] the migration gap reported upstream to beads_rust, or a documented rebuild-on-upgrade step added
- [ ] doctor's gitignore check consults `git check-ignore` rather than grepping for a literal

title: pulse-inject: skip injection when target window is 🔔 (blocked on Andrew)
description: State-blind injector bug (diagnosed from Zig's question 2026-06-30). pulse-inject.sh step 4 send-keys the command + Enter UNCONDITIONALLY — it only checks pane_current_command==claude, never the session's interaction state. If a timer fires while the target window is blocked on an AskUserQuestion / ExitPlanMode / permission prompt, the keystrokes feed the MODAL DIALOG (not the message composer): the command text is eaten and the trailing Enter resolves the dialog with the wrong/default answer — losing the tick AND mis-answering Zig's open question. (Not queued — queuing only happens at the composer.) Affects ALL pulse-style timers (explore pulse, daily-digest, elevate, local-coding-models, autonovel) since they all route through this one script. Fix: before the inject, read #{window_name}; the tmux-status.sh hook prefixes '🔔 ' on PreToolUse(AskUserQuestion|ExitPlanMode) + permission Notifications and only clears it on resume (PostToolUse->🧠 / Stop->✅), so '🔔 ' is present exactly for the blocked-modal duration. If the name starts with 🔔, DEFER (log + exit 0); the next timer retries once answered. Guard is 🔔-specific — 🧠 (mid-turn, cleanly queues) / ✅ / 🌀 still inject. Regression test in test-pulse-inject.sh: a 🔔-prefixed window must NOT receive the command; the existing 🌀 case must still inject (proves 🔔-specificity).

title: pulse-inject: re-source the claude() wrapper before a cold launch (durable panes hold stale function bodies)
description:
## Context
Follow-on to dotfiles-t6to, and the same class of bug one level up. The wrapper fix
lands in claude-identity-wrapper.sh, which a shell reads ONCE at start. The harness's

prints a line and the launch proceeds.

title: always-loaded: _al_mtime uses GNU-only stat -Lc and swallows the error — every mtime is 0 on every Mac
description:
## Context

`agents/hooks/lib/always-loaded.sh:78`:

```bash
_al_mtime() { stat -Lc %Y "$1" 2>/dev/null || echo 0; }
```

`stat -Lc %Y` is **GNU-only**. BSD/macOS `stat` has no `-c`. So on every Mac this function
fails on every call, the `2>/dev/null` hides the error, and `|| echo 0` returns **0 as the
mtime of every file**. Staleness detection is silently degraded fleet-wide on macOS.

This is the repo's own rule #3 doing exactly what the rule warns about: the blanket stderr
suppression is what converts a hard portability failure into a plausible-looking `0`. Rule
#3 already says "the hooks themselves have violated it" — this is another instance.

## Steps to Reproduce

On macOS, in the repo root:

```bash
stat -Lc %Y agents/hooks/lib/always-loaded.sh
# stat: illegal option -- c   ; exit 1

stat -Lf %m agents/hooks/lib/always-loaded.sh
# 1785628117                  ; the BSD form works

bash agents/hooks/test/test-always-loaded-staleness.sh
# FAIL: 9/25 test cases failed
```

All three verified on `zig` 2026-08-01. The 9 failures include "names HOW LONG ago",
"MEMORY.md change is detected", and "project CLAUDE.md change is detected" — i.e. the
staleness feature's core behavior, not edge cases.

## Fix direction

Detect once, define the function accordingly — do not stack two suppressed `stat` calls:

```bash
if stat -Lc %Y . >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  _al_mtime() { stat -Lc %Y "$1" || echo 0; }   # GNU
else
  _al_mtime() { stat -Lf %m "$1" || echo 0; }   # BSD/macOS
fi
```

Keep a fallback, but the fallback must not be reachable merely because the platform is
macOS. While in here, audit `agents/` for other GNU-only `stat`, `date -d`, `readlink -f`,
and `grep -oP` uses — same class as `dotfiles-1rj5`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_al_mtime` returns a real mtime on macOS AND Linux, both demonstrated with output
- [ ] `test-always-loaded-staleness.sh` passes 25/25 on macOS; show the before (9 failing)
      and after
- [ ] the blanket `2>/dev/null` is gone or narrowed to a genuine existence probe
- [ ] `agents/` audited for other GNU-only coreutils idioms; each hit fixed or annotated
close_reason: Fixed in d063a13 — stat flavour probed once; also found declare -A (bash 4) in stop-always-loaded-check.sh. Verified: 9/25 FAIL -> 25/25 on macOS, 25/25 on Linux. _al_mtime now returns a real epoch, deref through symlink intact.

title: pico: add standardAttributes.group reading X-Machine-Origin, then restart agentgateway
description:
Parent: dotfiles-ogkz. ORCHESTRATOR-OWNED — pico has no Claude Code and this is a different MACHINE, not a repo. Not for a worktree subagent.

Add to ~/.config/agentgateway/config.yaml under the existing `standardAttributes`
(which today has only `user`):

    group: 'default(request.headers["x-machine-origin"], "unknown")'

Why group: agentgateway_group is NULL in all 78,956 rows, already has a dedicated

first-class FILTER DROPDOWN in the admin UI, not a hidden label. Zig design call.

⚠️ REQUIRES A RESTART. `config:` is applied ONLY AT STARTUP — agentgateway hot-reloads
modelCatalog only. Restart interrupts fleet-wide LLM traffic (zig-computer, metis, and
the session doing the restart).

    launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.zig.agentgateway
    # KeepAlive={SuccessfulExit=false}, ThrottleInterval=10 -> self-recovers ~10s

⚠️ config.yaml is 0600 and references ${AGW_GOOSE_KEY}/${AGW_CC_KEY}. Back it up first
(a .bak-<stamp> sibling already exists for the plist, follow that convention). NEVER
print or copy the expanded values.

## Acceptance Criteria

Restarted with Zig's explicit go-ahead: pid 97491 (up 1d16h) -> 84195, health 401 on /claude/v1/models. VERIFIED END TO END: a real claude call recorded group=zig-computer user=zig-computer:dotfiles; stale-wrapper clients degrade to group=unknown as designed; the oldest row (2026-07-03, user=goose) still has user intact and group NULL, so 78,956 rows of history are untouched. title: healthcheck: bump qwen3-coder ollama completion probe timeout 30s -> 90s (cold-load can exceed 30s after Ollama restart)
description:
## Problem
healthcheck.sh probe_completion(qwen3-coder:30b, 30s) failed after Ollama restart on 2026-05-30, falsely flagging stack as wedged. Real behavior: qwen3-coder:30b cold-loads in ~60-70s after Ollama restart; my own probe with 120s timeout returned a valid completion at 68s.

2. Restart ollama (clean state, no model loaded)
3. Run `bash healthcheck.sh` immediately

Bumped probe_completion timeout from 30s to 90s. Empirically matches the cold-load worst case observed on pico (single 30b model into Metal: 60-70s; the 30s margin accommodates first-token latency).

- [x] Matrix H1 resumes successfully

title: bench-matrix: abort path skips stop-all-serving — gate abort (exit 6) left ollama + resident model running on pico
description:
## What happened
Cohort-1 end: analyze-variance --strict flagged → bench-matrix exited 6 — but the cohort's ollama serve (and its resident devstral runner) stayed up on pico. The happy path runs stop-all-serving + eviction probe at matrix end; the abort path released the pico lock but skipped eviction.

## Why it matters
Round-1 postmortem: orphan serving processes accumulated across runs and contaminated successors. The abort path is exactly when an operator is least likely to remember manual cleanup. (Leaving state up for diagnosis is defensible — but then it must be a LOUD deliberate choice in the abort message, not an omission.)

## Steps to Reproduce
Force any per-cohort blocking gate to fail (e.g. variance gate exit 1) and observe: bench-matrix exits nonzero, pico_release runs, but no stop-all-serving/eviction probe; pgrep on pico shows the cohort server still resident.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] bats test covering the abort path's cleanup behavior

title: offboard: the decision harvest labels '(closed this session)' from status alone, so it mislabels
description:
## Context
Found during a real /offboard in ~/linearb/dashboard-dev-interrupted on
2026-08-05.

Step 2.5's harvest prints `_(closed this session)_` for any decision bead whose
`status == "closed"`. It never compares the CLOSE TIME to the session window. So
every closed decision inside the (deliberately over-wide) cutoff window gets the
label, including ones closed days before the session started.

Measured in that run:
- session start          2026-08-04T14:08:42Z
- cutoff used            2026-08-01T00:42:40Z  (earlier of session start and marker)
- `bd-91xa`  closed      2026-08-03T17:01:29Z  -> labelled "(closed this session)"

bd-91xa was closed a day and a half BEFORE the session began. The label is
simply false, and it is false in the direction that matters: it invents session
activity that did not happen, in the one artifact whose whole job is telling the
next session what this session did.

This interacts badly with the over-wide cutoff by design. Step 2.5 deliberately
prefers `min(session_start, marker)` because "an over-wide window shows you a
bead you can judge and discard; a too-narrow one shows you nothing." That is the
right call for LISTING. But the `(closed this session)` label is not a listing,
it is an ASSERTION, and it is computed as if the window were exact. The wider the
window, the more confidently wrong the label gets.

The skill already tells the operator to judge the list. It does not warn that the
label itself is unjudged, and an operator transcribing the harvest into the note
verbatim (which is what the skill's own template invites) propagates the error.

## Steps to Reproduce
Run /offboard Step 2.5 in a project where a decision bead was closed after the
cutoff but before the session started. Observe the bead printed with
`_(closed this session)_`.

Compare `updated_at` against the printed session-start line:

    br list --type decision -a --json | jq -r '.issues[] | "\(.id) \(.created_at) \(.updated_at) \(.status)"'

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The label reflects the SESSION WINDOW, not `status`. A closed decision
      should only be marked closed-this-session when its close time is at or
      after session start.
- [ ] `updated_at` is a proxy for close time, not close time itself: a closed
      bead edited later reports the edit. Either accept that and say so in the
      output, or find a real close timestamp. Do not silently treat them as equal.
- [ ] When close time cannot be established, print the bead WITHOUT the label
      rather than guessing. An unlabelled true-positive costs a glance; a
      confident false label costs trust in the whole receipt.
- [ ] The two-line receipt keeps working, and gains nothing that reads as a
      verdict the data does not support.

title: retreat cruft B: retire the conduit machinery — and pre-commit references it, so check callers FIRST
description:
## Context
Once the seven rows run locally (done 2026-08-05), this machinery has no runtime caller.
Audited 2026-08-05.

    agents/scheduler/pulse-dispatch-remote.sh        (~2,300 lines) + test-
    agents/scheduler/vps-preflight.sh
    agents/scheduler/vps-repo-refresh.sh             + test-
    agents/scheduler/vps-repo-manifest.txt
    agents/vault/vps-peer-bootstrap.sh
    agents/vault/vps-phase2-symlinks.sh
    agents/scheduler/templates/claude-gateway-tunnel.{service,timer}
    agents/scheduler/templates/claude-vault-sync.timer   (verify: peer-only or shared?)

## ⚠️ THE TRAP — deleting these silently weakens a gate
`pulse-dispatch-remote.sh` is referenced by **12 non-test files**, including:

    agents/hooks/pre-commit-checks.sh      <- the pre-commit gate keys on it
    agents/skills/pulse/SKILL.md
    agents/infra.md

Delete the script without updating `pre-commit-checks.sh` and the gate either errors or —
worse — silently stops covering something while staying green. That is the exact failure
class this repo keeps hitting (`dotfiles-cxle`). **Check every caller before removing any
file here**, and re-run the hook suite after.

`vps-preflight.sh` and `vps-repo-refresh.sh` reference each other and the manifest, so they
come out together or not at all.

## Delete or archive — say WHICH, deliberately
The retreat doc requires the choice be stated, not defaulted. `pulse-dispatch-remote.sh`
carries hard-won knowledge (the glyph matcher, the ownership guards, the surface relay);
git history preserves it either way, so deletion is defensible — but say so.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] every caller of each removed file identified and updated FIRST
- [ ] `agents/hooks/test/` suite green after, and the pre-commit gate still bites (prove
      with a mutant, per CLAUDE.md rule 1 — a green suite is not evidence)
- [ ] delete-vs-archive stated per file
- [ ] no dangling reference anywhere, including SKILL.md files and infra.md

title: retreat cruft C: files that KEEP living but must lose their marketing-vps branches
description:
## Context
Audited 2026-08-05. These serve zig-computer, metis or pico too. **Deleting them would be
wrong**; they need the marketing-vps-specific logic and claims removed. Separated from
bead B precisely so nobody bulk-deletes by grep hit.

    agents/scheduler/ensure-fleet-tunnel.sh     "Runs on marketing-vps (or any box that can ssh to zig-computer)"
    agents/scheduler/gateway-switch.sh          branches on "(marketing-vps only)" for the tunnel timer
    agents/scheduler/fleet-creds.sh             "Runs on marketing-vps" — the ssh-boundary credential broker
    agents/hooks/lib/portable.sh                names it only as an example of a GNU box
    agents/hooks/session-end.sh                 a PEER branch that pushes transcripts at session-end
    agents/lib/claude-identity-wrapper.sh       + its test — the shared-tmux-namespace reasoning
    agents/scheduler/imc-pull.sh · pulse-retry.sh · pulse-surface-queue.sh
    agents/scheduler/lb-granola-publish-guard.sh · mutate-tunnel-ownership.sh
    agents/vault/memory.excludes · transcripts.excludes
    git/.gitconfig · bash/.bash_aliases · zsh/.zig-computer.zshenv · zsh/.metis.zshenv
    agents/skills/gdoc/SKILL.md · render_styled_blocks.mjs · tools/githooks/pre-commit

## The distinction that matters (CLAUDE.md, live-state vs historical)
- ❌ **Live-state claim** — "marketing-vps is a second writer", "runs on marketing-vps".
  Becomes FALSE at retreat. Fix.
- ✅ **Historical citation** — "measured 2026-08-04 on marketing-vps", "the rename that

`fleet-creds.sh` is the interesting case: it exists ONLY to move tokens across an ssh

title: pulse-inject.sh stages no surface — local loops silently lose the always-bell guarantee
description:
## Context

`pulse-dispatch-remote.sh` step 7 surfaces **ALWAYS** — every finished tick,
`done`/`quiet`/`blocked` — staging into the deferred-surface queue and raising the
AskUserQuestion from the local session (`dotfiles-5ts2`; Zig 2026-07-31: "there's no
such thing as a low-value bell ... you need to be in charge of making sure I see their
actions and I know when they're ready").

Local loops have **no equivalent**. Any loop moved from the remote dispatcher to a
local timer silently loses the guarantee, and `/pulse`'s "ticks never AskUserQuestion"
rule then stops the tick standing in. Nothing errors; the pane shows the idle glyph
over a deliverable waiting on Zig.

Bit `pulse-weekly-report` on 2026-08-07, five ticks after `dotfiles-1n50` moved it
local on 2026-08-05. Report published clean, tick logged `done`, `PushNotification`
returned "Remote Control inactive" (undelivered), Zig found out by asking.

Patched at the PROSE layer (decision `weekly-reporting-skd`): `refs/pulse.md` declares
`Surfacing: ATTENDED` and the tick raises the dialog itself. Works, but is per-project
and depends on the tick following instructions.

## ⚠️ DESIGN CORRECTION (2026-08-07) — the original framing of this bead was WRONG

This bead first said "teach `pulse-inject.sh` to stage a surface." **That cannot work.**
`pulse-inject.sh` returns as soon as it has typed the command; it does NOT block for the
tick (the `.service` files say so explicitly, and its verdict contract is about whether
INJECTION succeeded — injected / bounced / failed). At the moment it exits, the tick has
not run. Staging there would announce a tick that has not happened.

The dispatcher can surface only because its step 5 **polls `result.json`** and step 6
lands the ledger row — it OBSERVES completion. Nothing observes a local tick's
completion today.

## The actual fix — watch the LEDGER, ride the existing timer

The local tick's durable completion record is **its ledger row**, appended at wrap
(`/pulse` tick procedure step 5) for `done`/`quiet`/`blocked` alike — exactly the set
the dispatcher surfaces. So:

- A watcher compares each local loop's newest ledger row against a per-loop
  "last surfaced ts" marker under `~/.local/state/`, and stages a surface for any row
  newer than the marker.
- Ride **`pulse-retry.timer`** (already every 2 minutes, already drains the queue). No
  new unit, no new daemon — the same reuse argument `pulse-surface-queue.sh` makes for
  its own drain trigger.
- Loop → ledger path → row name comes from `~/harnessd/refs/harness-manifest.json`,
  which already pins `ledger` + `ledger_row` per loop and is already asserted per tick
  by `harness-assert-registration`.

Interaction with the ATTENDED prose fix is fine and needs no special casing: if the
tick already raised its own dialog, the window name starts with the bell glyph,
`pulse-inject.sh` refuses to type into it, and the staged surface stays queued until
the bell clears — the deferred-surface path working as designed. Collapse-per-row means
a loop that ran twice while Zig was away announces only its newest state.

## Check before building

Which loops are local vs dispatched — every local one has this hole right now:
`systemctl --user cat 'pulse-*.service' | grep -E 'ExecStart|^Description'`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A ledger-watcher stages a surface for any pulse row whose newest ledger `ts` is newer than that loop's last-surfaced marker
- [ ] Surfaces on `done`/`quiet`/`blocked` alike, matching the dispatcher's always-surface policy
- [ ] Exactly-once per ledger row: marker advances only on successful stage; a bounced drain leaves the entry queued, never dropped or duplicated
- [ ] Invoked from `pulse-retry.sh` (existing 2-minute timer) — no new systemd unit
- [ ] Loop -> ledger/row resolved from the harnessd manifest, not hardcoded
- [ ] Tests alongside `test-pulse-retry.sh` / `test-pulse-inject.sh`, including the exactly-once and bounce cases
- [ ] `/pulse` "ATTENDED loops" section updated to say local loops now surface mechanically
close_reason: Delivered across 413f7ab (build), 975baf4 (same-day gate-off after adversarial review), 3324d1b (blocker fix + hardening) and da6c35a (un-gate). Local pulse loops now surface every finished tick mechanically, via pulse-ledger-watch.sh riding the existing pulse-retry.timer -- no new systemd unit. The gate was RETIRED rather than defaulted-on (a switchable wiring is a second silent way to lose the bell); test-pulse-retry case 18 was inverted to pin that it runs with no flag AND that a stale PULSE_LEDGER_WATCH_ENABLE=0 cannot resurrect it. All four adversarial-review findings fixed: run-level flock (concurrent double-stage), marker RESERVED before staging (a stage could otherwise succeed while the marker write failed, re-staging forever), systemctl rc checked + zero-units is an error + corrupt marker announces instead of silently re-seeding past a finished tick + malformed ts errors (three silent 'nothing new' paths), and a floor marker so a newly-registered loop's FIRST real tick surfaces (the header's '<=2-minute install window' claim was wrong -- it was every new loop, always). Verified by me at REAL exit codes (not through a pipe): test-pulse-ledger-watch 76/76 rc=0, test-pulse-retry 26/26 rc=0, test-pulse-dispatch-remote 421/421 rc=0. Live: watcher runs clean, 17 loops seeded, pulse-weekly-report's marker matches its ledger ts exactly. Blocker dotfiles-sxsv closed first. REMAINING, tracked separately: dotfiles-eh21 (the watcher still reports errors:5 for five DISABLED units -- a false alarm, fix in flight) and dotfiles-qn4t (test-pulse-inject 6/113, pre-existing and unrelated).

title: pulse-ledger-watch flags 5 DISABLED units as errors — a false alarm every 2 minutes
description:
## ⚠️ RE-SCOPED and DOWNGRADED P1 -> P2 on 2026-08-07. The first filing was WRONG.

Originally filed as "5 local pulse loops are unregistered, they cannot surface and the
dashboard cannot see them", with an acceptance criterion of **adding manifest entries**.
Investigating before acting showed that would have been a mistake: it would have
registered five DEAD units and made the manifest less honest, not more.

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
bash ~/dotfiles/agents/scheduler/pulse-ledger-watch.sh > /tmp/lw.txt 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"
cat /tmp/lw.txt      # -> PULSE_LEDGER_WATCH_RESULT=staged:0:seeded:0:errors:5

for u in pulse-autonoveld-conceive pulse-autonoveld-mail pulse-autonoveld-voice \
         pulse-autonoveld-write pulse-picod; do
  echo "$u enabled=$(systemctl --user is-enabled "$u.timer") \
        manifest=$(grep -c "$u" ~/harnessd/refs/harness-manifest.json)"
done                 # -> all five: enabled=disabled  manifest=0
```

⚠️ Run the watcher WITHOUT piping to `tail`/`head` — a pipe makes `$?` the pager's exit
code, which caused a misread earlier the same day (see dotfiles-qn4t).

**Observed:** `errors:5` on every run, every 2 minutes, forever.
**Expected:** `errors:0` — a disabled loop cannot fire, so it cannot finish a tick, so
there is nothing to surface. It is not drift.

## What is actually true

All five units are `disabled`/`inactive`. The projects behind them are not dead, which is
what made the first reading plausible:

- `~/autonoveld` IS live — 38 ledger rows, newest today — but driven by the **`daily-ao3`**
  row (`pulse-daily-ao3.timer`, enabled), which IS in the manifest and verifies clean:
  `harness-assert-registration pulse-daily-ao3 daily-ao3` -> `state=healthy`, marker
  matches the newest row exactly. The four `pulse-autonoveld-*` units are superseded legacy
  that write nothing.
- `~/picod` has 22 rows, newest 2026-07-31 — genuinely dormant. `picod-health.timer` is a
  health check, not a pulse loop.

## Why it matters

`pulse-ledger-watch.sh` enumerates `pulse-*.service` without checking whether the timer is
enabled. That is the `explore-4x39` failure mode pointed the other way: **a false alarm on
a healthy system trains you to discount the alarm that will matter.** The error channel is
supposed to mean "a LIVE loop cannot be surfaced." (Demonstrated in practice the same day:
a monitor armed on this log was drowned by these five lines every 2 minutes and missed the
signal it was watching for.)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Watcher skips loops whose timer is disabled; keyed on the TIMER, not the service's active state (a oneshot service is inactive between runs by design)
- [x] `bash ~/dotfiles/agents/scheduler/pulse-ledger-watch.sh` reports `errors:0` on a healthy box, with staged/seeded unchanged
- [x] A live loop that is genuinely unregistered STILL errors loudly — regression test; do not fix the false alarm by silencing the true one
- [ ] Separately, Zig's call: delete the 5 dormant unit files, or leave them
close_reason: Fixed in 9aeaeb2. pulse-ledger-watch.sh probes 'systemctl --user is-enabled <loop>.timer' after ExecStart classification: disabled|masked|masked-runtime are SKIPPED with a log note (not an error, not counted); every other state takes the normal path. Live verdict verified by me at REAL rc=0 (no pipe): staged:0:seeded:0:errors:0, down from errors:5, staged/seeded unchanged, all 17 live loops still examined -- confirmed pulse-weekly-report still evaluated each run. THE REGRESSION GUARD HOLDS, which was the real risk here: an unclear answer (not-found, empty, failed probe) is treated as LIVE rather than disabled, because reading 'disabled' from an unclear answer would silence a running loop -- the exact failure this script exists to end. Keyed on the TIMER's enabled state, not the service's active state. Suite 76 -> 88 (cases 26-29), verified by me at REAL rc=0, 88/88; test-pulse-retry 26/26 and test-pulse-dispatch-remote 421/421 unaffected. Mutation-checked both directions: breaking the skip fails 8 cases; adding 'enabled' to the skip list fails 60 including 'an ENABLED unregistered loop is still an error' -- the blast radius is the point, since skipping live loops switches the whole mechanism off. NOT DONE, deliberately: the five dormant unit files remain on disk (Zig's call, AC 4); they are now silent skips rather than noise.

title: pulse-surface-queue.sh injected prose hardcodes 'REMOTE ... ran on marketing-vps' — wrong for local surfaces
description:
## ⚠️ RE-RATED P3 -> P1 on 2026-08-07. The original filing was WRONG.

I filed this as "cosmetic, not a correctness bug: the announcement still delivers."
**That was wrong, and the error is instructive: the injected text is not decoration, it
is an INSTRUCTION to the receiving Claude session.** Adversarial review of dotfiles-wqby
caught it hours later.

## Context

`pulse-surface-queue.sh` (lines ~331-336) builds the single-line command that
`pulse-inject.sh` types into the pane. It is hardcoded for the REMOTE dispatcher. Typed
verbatim, for BOTH the 1-pending and n-pending forms:

> "REMOTE PULSE SURFACE (...): a pulse tick that ran on **marketing-vps** has FINISHED
> ... File any bead it names that the remote side did not already file and push, and
> **land the ledger row at `<dir>/refs/pulse-ledger.jsonl`**. Do NOT re-run the tick."

For a REMOTE tick both clauses are right: the box ran the tick, the local session lands
the row (`pulse-dispatch-remote.sh` step 6).

For a LOCAL tick staged by `pulse-ledger-watch.sh` (dotfiles-wqby) both are FALSE:
- it did not run on marketing-vps;
- **the ledger row already exists** — the local tick wrote it at wrap (`/pulse` step 5),
  and that row is precisely what the watcher READ in order to stage this announcement.

## The failure, on the happy path

1. Local tick finishes, writes its ledger row.
2. Watcher sees a new row, stages a surface, advances its marker.
3. Drain types the command above into the pane.
4. The session obeys "land the ledger row" and writes a **duplicate** row with a fresh `ts`.
5. Next run (2 minutes later): that row is newer than the marker -> stage -> type -> (4).

Self-sustaining announcement loop, plus ledger corruption in the file the whole mechanism
reads. The only counter-instruction ("do NOT write another") lives in the surface JSON's
`.detail`, which the session reads AFTER the command that contradicts it.

`pulse-ledger-watch.sh` is **gated off by default** as of `975baf4` until this lands
(`PULSE_LEDGER_WATCH_ENABLE=1` forces it on). **This bead blocks dotfiles-wqby.**

## Why the test suite did not catch it

`test-pulse-ledger-watch.sh` case 14 drives the real queue and asserts the surface FILE's
contents — it never asserts what the drain **types**. The gap is the seam between the two
scripts, which is exactly where a shared-prose assumption hides.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The injected command is ORIGIN-AWARE: a local surface never claims marketing-vps
- [ ] A local surface does NOT instruct the session to land a ledger row (the row already exists); the remote form keeps that clause
- [ ] Both the 1-pending and n-pending forms fixed — they carry the text independently
- [ ] `test-pulse-dispatch-remote.sh` assertions updated in step (8 sites pin the literal string)
- [ ] New assertion on what the drain TYPES for a local surface, not only what the file contains — the gap that let this through
- [ ] Re-enable the watcher in `pulse-retry.sh` (drop the `PULSE_LEDGER_WATCH_ENABLE` gate) and re-run the mutation check on test-pulse-retry case 18
close_reason: Fixed in 3324d1b. pulse-surface-queue.sh's 'stage' now takes --origin remote|local (remote is the default, so pulse-dispatch-remote.sh is untouched) and selects the injected wording accordingly. Verified by direct inspection: the LOCAL branches say 'its ledger row is ALREADY WRITTEN — do NOT write another one. Do NOT re-run the tick.' and grep confirms 0 occurrences of 'land the ledger row' in any local branch, so the duplicate-row -> re-stage -> re-type loop is closed. All three forms handled: 1-pending, n-pending, and a MIXED form for a group holding both origins. REMOTE PROVEN UNCHANGED: the implementer drove the pre- and post-change queue through one fixture and diffed the typed command -- byte-identical at n=1 (601B), n=2 (961B), n=3 (1099B) after normalizing staging stamps; I independently re-ran test-pulse-dispatch-remote.sh -> REAL rc=0, 421/421. The test gap that let this through is closed: cases 16-19 now assert what the drain TYPES (both origins, both forms, mixed), not only what the surface file contains. Suite 42 -> 76 cases, verified by me at REAL rc=0, 76/76, with the implementer's mutation checks showing 4/4/4/2 failures when each wording fix is broken.

title: an UNIDENTIFIED ecdsa key has unrestricted inbound access to zig-computer
description:
## Context
Found 2026-08-07 while severing marketing-vps trust. Zig did not recognise it; investigated
at his request, then left in place at his instruction. Recorded so it is not forgotten.

    SHA256:do/3JL4uDFYRz1hYG2X40lc5AlFUjY6n3wAOuDH2+AY   ecdsa-sha2-nistp256
    line 3 of ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
    NO comment, NO from= restriction, NO command= restriction

## What it is NOT — checked
| source | result |
|---|---|
| `github.com/azigler.keys` | 2 keys, both match OTHER lines (personal ed25519, `pico@pico`) |
| `github.com/zigler.keys` | HTTP 200, **0 keys** |
| zig-computer `~/.ssh/*.pub` | `id_ha`, `id_rsa_ovh` — no match |
| pico user + host keys | no match |

Four of the five authorized_keys entries ARE accounted for: `andrew@metis.local`,
`andrewzigler@gmail.com`, `pico@pico`, and a comment line. This one is not.

## The `@zigler` red herring — resolved, record it so nobody re-investigates
The line ` #ssh.id - @zigler` is a COMMENT (leading space, then `#`; sshd skips whitespace
before the comment check). It is the marker `ssh-import-id` writes. It grants nothing. It
looked like a key comment only because a naive `awk {print $NF}` reports it as one.

## Not determined
- **Age.** `authorized_keys` mtime is now the 2026-08-07 edit; the file is not git-tracked,
  so there is no history to date the line from.
- **metis and iphone-15-pro were NOT checked.** infra.md lists a Termius client on the
  iPhone, and Termius commonly generates ecdsa-nistp256 — the most plausible candidate.

## Safe way to resolve it
Remove the line, then try connecting from the iPhone/Termius and from metis. If something
breaks, the key is identified and restorable in one line from
`~/.ssh/authorized_keys.bak.2026-08-07`, which still contains it. Nothing in daily use
should break: metis, pico and the personal key are all separately present.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] the key is identified, or removed after the two probes above
- [ ] if kept, it gains a comment AND a `from=` restriction so the next audit is cheap
- [ ] consider tracking `authorized_keys` (or a checksum of it) so additions are dateable

title: finding (CLASS): six tool idioms on this fleet that return a confident WRONG answer instead of an error
description:
## Why this is a bead and not a doc paragraph
Filed 2026-08-07 at Zigs instruction. These were originally scattered across a handoff
note (overwritten by the next /offboard), a retreat-scoped doc (deleted when that box is
finished with), and close-reasons on already-closed beads. None of those is queryable and
two are ephemeral. The record for a reusable finding is a bead.

Each item below produced a CONFIDENT WRONG ANSWER during the 2026-08-02..07 session — not
an error, not a crash. Several were reported to Zig as fact before being caught.

---

## 1. `find` does not follow symlinks without `-L`
`~/.claude/projects/-home-andrew-*` are SYMLINKS to `./-home-ubuntu-*`, created by
`agents/vault/vps-phase2-symlinks.sh` so an agent whose cwd is `/home/andrew/...` reads the
CANONICAL content.

    find ./-home-andrew-dotfiles -name "*.jsonl" | wc -l   ->   0     (correct POSIX behaviour)
    find -L ./-home-andrew-dotfiles -name "*.jsonl" | wc -l ->  578
    ls -1 -- -home-andrew-dotfiles/ | grep -c jsonl        ->  404

**Damage:** produced BOTH a false all-clear ("0 unique transcripts, nothing at risk") AND,
after I "corrected" it, a false alarm ("2,036 unique transcripts, none in the vault") — on
the question of whether a 6.8G wipe would destroy data. I also declared `find` broken on
that box, which it was not.
**Tell:** `ls` and `find` disagreeing on one directory is a symlink until proven otherwise.

## 2. `deferred` in the vault ledger is HEALTHY when the stamp is fresh
`vault-sync.sh` classifies three ways: deferred + fresh stamp (< `VAULT_SYNC_STALE_HOURS`,
default 6) = exit 0 / `OK (deferred)` / ledger `quiet`; deferred + stale = STALE/blocked;
deferred + no stamp = DEGRADED. The word is printed on the HEALTHY path deliberately, "so
the log never claims a push that did not happen."
**Damage:** I raised it as a data-loss alarm before the final wipe. The retreat docs own
warning ("a deferred row is not a push") is true but is only HALF the test — the stamp is
the other half.

## 3. `rm` is aliased to `rm -iv`
Non-interactively it PROMPTS and then HANGS rather than failing.
**Damage:** a 5-minute command timeout mid-Phase-4, in the middle of severing ssh trust.
**Correct form:** `command rm -f`.

## 4. `pkill -f <pattern>` matches its own shell
The invoking `zsh -c ...` command line contains the pattern, so pkill can kill itself.
**Damage:** truncated a Phase 2 command; the output vanished and looked like a failure.
**Correct form:** resolve the PID first (`ss -tlnp`, `pgrep` + filter) and `kill` by PID.

## 5. Leading-dash arguments — every project slug starts with `-`
`grep "$SLUG"`, `find $SLUG`, `br close -r "-..."` all parse the value as a FLAG.
**Damage:** `grep -c` returned 0 for a slug that was present; ugrep errored with
`invalid argument -m=e-andrew-dotfiles`.
**Correct forms:** `grep -F -- "$SLUG"`, `find ./-home-...`, `br close -r="..."`.

## 6. `ps -eo` / `ps axo` are unreliable on this fleet (uutils)
`error: conflicting format options` on invocations that are valid for procps.
**Damage:** an empty process list read as "no such processes"; I nearly reported an
orphaned claude that had simply already exited.
**Correct form:** read `/proc/<pid>/{cmdline,environ,stat}` directly.

---

## The shape they share
**Every one returns a plausible value instead of an error.** The failure is silent, and it
is indistinguishable from a true negative unless you already suspect it. That is the same
class as `dotfiles-cxle` (the consumer reports success while the step stopped working) —
this bead is its measurement-side twin.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] decide a home for the durable subset — a `/scrutinize` or `/onboard` checklist entry,
      or `agents/lib/` guard notes — so it is not only in this bead
- [ ] items 3 and 4 are mechanically preventable: consider a `pre-bash` hook warning on a
      bare `rm` without `-f` in a non-interactive context, and on `pkill -f` whose pattern
      would match the invoking command
- [ ] item 1 deserves a check in any script that walks `~/.claude/projects`
- [ ] cross-reference from `dotfiles-cxle` so the two classes are findable together

title: test-pulse-inject.sh: 6/113 failing (pre-existing) — bounce-log trim cases hit a missing state dir
description:
## Context

`test-pulse-inject.sh` exits **1** with 6 of 113 cases failing. Pre-existing and unrelated
to the 2026-08-07 surfacing work: both `pulse-inject.sh` and its test were last touched by
`c4b41aa` (2026-08-05), no commit on 2026-08-07 touched either, and the test imports
nothing from `pulse-retry.sh` / `pulse-ledger-watch.sh` / `pulse-surface-queue.sh`.

Found while verifying that work; surfaced independently by the implementing agent, and
confirmed by re-running.

## Steps to Reproduce

```bash
cd ~/dotfiles/agents/scheduler && bash test-pulse-inject.sh; echo "rc=$?"
```

⚠️ Run it WITHOUT piping to `tail`/`head`. Piping makes `$?` the pager's exit code, not the
suite's — which is exactly how this suite got reported as green earlier in the day. Use
`bash test.sh > file 2>&1; echo $?`.

## Observed

```
test-pulse-inject.sh: line 220: /tmp/tmp.XXXXXXXX/pulse-bounces.jsonl: No such file or directory
FAIL: 6/113 test cases failed
  - /pulse cmd gets absolute dir appended
  - bounce record written on 🔔 defer with --loop
  - bounce log trimmed to the newest half (lines=4)
  - the just-written bounce survives the trim
  - the oldest lines are the ones discarded by the trim
  - a log under the cap is left untouched
```

Five of the six are the bounce-log trim group and share one cause: line 220 writes to
`$HARNESS_STATE_DIR/pulse-bounces.jsonl` in a tmpdir that does not exist (not created, or
already cleaned). The sixth (absolute-dir append) may be independent — diagnose separately
rather than assuming one root cause.

## Why it matters

`pulse-inject.sh` is the delivery primitive for EVERY pulse loop, and the bounce log is
what `pulse-retry.sh` and the deferred-surface drain both key on. A suite that always exits
non-zero is a suite nobody can read a regression out of — and it now sits directly upstream
of the surfacing guarantee (dotfiles-wqby / -sxsv), where a real bounce-log regression would
silently cost announcements.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root-cause line 220's missing state dir; fix the setup (or the test's assumption), not the assertion
- [ ] Diagnose the absolute-dir case separately — confirm whether it shares the cause
- [ ] `bash test-pulse-inject.sh; echo $?` -> `rc=0`, 113/113
- [ ] Whatever broke it gains a case, so the same setup gap fails loudly instead of as 6 unrelated-looking assertions
